# C. VITRINGA

This is the nature of the matter, and there is no one who does not experience it for themselves. Let us survey the kingdoms and empires of our own time and see whether almost every single one—indeed, every single one—does not possess its own distinct languages and idioms, rather than mere dialects. It is so true that the separation of societies is a cause for the differentiation of languages, even if it is the least significant of all causes. 

Commerce, in truth, contributes even more to this process. For through trade, it happens that words from one dialect are poured into another. Not only are the dialects themselves influenced, but the vocabularies of both are mingled together. Consequently, the ancient language emerges in a new dress and character <note>original Latin: *apparatu*</note>, differing significantly from what came before. I need no other witness to this than what we have experienced in our own era. Since the **Dutch** <note>original: *Batavi*; Vitringa uses the Roman name for the people of the Netherlands.</note> began to conduct trade with the **French**, what a vast quantity of French words has been—not merely introduced, but forced into their language! 

And yet, this happened so gradually that one cannot point out precisely <note>original Greek: *ἀκριβῶς* (akribōs)</note> the specific moment it began, nor the exact occasions; indeed, it is almost impossible to accurately distinguish the words from one another. How much greater a change will occur if other nations—which were once separated from one another and thus developed new dialects—are mixed together again, and the inhabitants of diverse regions converge into one? We have already shown that this very thing occurred in **Egypt**. 

There is certainly nothing that accelerates the transformation of a language more than this very process. Let the **French** and the **English** serve as evidence for us; indeed, the **Jews** themselves provide the most powerful argument. No one doubts that these peoples formerly used the same idiom; indeed, it is impossible to doubt it, since [it is] express—

# SACRED OBSERVATIONS

So much so that this is precisely what I maintain regarding the Hebrew nation: specifically, that the most common words of that people’s language, along with their inflection, pronunciation, and the greater part of their construction, were preserved just as they were used by the Ancients. Lest anyone think this could hardly happen, as it seems somewhat contrary to nature, I appeal to the Greek dialect. From the era when it first began to grow famous through public writings, it resisted change through many centuries so effectively that it suffered only a slight transformation, though in these days it has been much corrupted. But why should I hesitate? I appeal to the **Welsh** <note>original: *Cambros*</note>, who possess the **British language**; and the **Cantabrians** <note>original: *Contabros*</note>, whom they now call **Biscayans**, among whom the ancient **Spanish** language survives. Concerning the **Welsh**—or if you prefer, the **Walli**, as they are now called—this is a very well-known matter. to distinguish Egyptian words! But I could never imagine that the prefixes *p* or *ph* served as articles among the Ancient Egyptians. If you examine all the names that we can judge to have belonged to the Ancient Egyptians from the oldest writings, none will occur to you—certainly none have occurred to me—in which you might notice the same thing happening. Take as examples the names *Osiris*, *Horus*, *Isis*, *Serapis*, *Apis*, *Nilus*, *Zoan*, *Manes*, and many more like them. 

To me, therefore, it seems far better to derive the term <term>Pharaoh</term> <note>original Hebrew: פרעה (*Par‘oh*)</note> from the root <term>parah</term> <note>original Hebrew: פרע (*P-R-‘A*)</note>, which signifies <gloss>to be free or released</gloss>, and among the <term>Chaldeans</term> <note>Speakers of Aramaic, a language closely related to Hebrew; Vitringa often looks to related Semitic dialects for word origins.</note> denotes <gloss>to avenge or vindicate</gloss>. This is because he who vindicates himself from an injury makes himself free and released from that which restricted both his right and his honor. What more fitting derivation could be devised? Surely those who first subjected nations or families to themselves rendered themselves *free*, while making others *servants*. For in every age, kings have been released from all laws. 

Indeed, when God commands that the <term>rights of the king</term> <note>original Hebrew: משפט המלך (*mishpat ha-melekh*)</note> be described to the nation of Israel in the <term>First Book of Samuel, chapter 8</term>, just as it was practiced by the kings of other nations at that time, He depicts it clearly so as to leave the fullest power of acting to kings, even if their actions are most unjust. Regarding the *Kings of the Persians*, *Herodotus* <note>A 5th-century BCE Greek historian known as the "Father of History."</note> asserts this in *Book III* of his histories. *Plutarch* <note>A Greek-Roman biographer and philosopher.</note> also says the same in his book *On the Three Forms of Government*: <gloss>The Persians obtained by lot a monarchy that was absolute and unaccountable</gloss> <note>original Greek: Πέρσαι μὲν αὐτοκρατῆ βασίλειαν καὶ ἀνυπεύθυνον ἐπεκληρώσαντο</note>. *Atossa* also says of *Xerxes* in *Aeschylus’s* <note>The famous Greek tragedian.</note> play *The Persians*: <gloss>Even if he fares ill, he is not accountable to the city</gloss> <note>original Greek: Κακῶς δὲ πράξας οὐχ ὑπεύθυνος πόλει</note>. Therefore, we shall state what appears most likely to us. **Berech** <note>original Hebrew: ברך</note> denotes *knee*, and **Berachim** <note>original Hebrew: ברכים</note> denotes *knees*. From this, **Barach** <note>original Hebrew: ברך</note> means *to kneel*. Imagine, then, that the Egyptian language suffered such a change that the letter **Aleph** <note>original: א</note>—specifically the formative part of the Imperative used in forms outside of the *Kal* <note>The "Kal" is the most basic verb conjugation in Hebrew grammar.</note>—was turned into a **He** <note>original: ה</note>. This could have happened very easily because these letters differ very little in sound and shape; and thus, substitute **Abrech** <note>original: אברך</note>, meaning *kneel!*, for the standard Hebrew **Habrech** <note>original: הברך</note>. For it was clearly the custom among Eastern peoples to bow their knees as a sign of reverence and honor. And thus our Dutch version states it best: *And they cried before his face, kneel.* <note>original Dutch: Ende sy riepen voor syn aengesichte / knieldt.</note> This is also the opinion of the *Vulgate translator* <note>The author of the 4th-century Latin translation of the Bible, St. Jerome.</note>, as well as of **Kimchi** <note>David Kimchi (1160–1235), a celebrated medieval rabbi and grammarian.</note> and **Rabbi Jonah, the Spanish Grammarian** <note>Jonah ibn Janah (c. 990–1050), an influential Hebrew philologist in Islamic Spain.</note> as cited in the works of **Aben Ezra** <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167), a prolific medieval scholar and biblical commentator.</note>.

We come now to the name **Zaphenath-paneah** <note>original Hebrew: צפנת פענח; the name Pharaoh gave to Joseph in Genesis 41:45.</note>, which is much more difficult to explain than the preceding words. The **Septuagint** <note>original: LXX; the ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note> has *Psonthonphanech* <note>original Greek: Ψονθονφανηχ</note>, a word which everyone interprets as *the revealer of future things*. Those who follow the wisdom of **Kircher** <note>Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680), a Jesuit polymath who attempted to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs.</note> interpret *Psonthon* <note>original Greek: Ψονθον</note> or *Psonthou* <note>original Greek: Ψονθου</note> as *future things* and *phanech* <note>original Greek: φανηχ</note> as *prophet* or *soothsayer*; thus *Psonthonphanech* would be *Prophet of the Future*. That is, *A man to whom hidden things are revealed* <note>original Aramaic: גברא דטמירן גלין ליה (Gabra de-temiran gelin leh)</note>, as the **Targum Onkelos** <note>The authoritative Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Torah.</note> has it. From this, some also conjecture that the name *Psonthonphanech* was not written accurately enough in the history written by Moses, but that this occurred because the Hebrews pronounced that foreign word poorly. All of these theories would certainly have the appearance of truth, if the term **Zaphenath-paneah** <note>original Hebrew: צפנת פענח</note> [later...]

### C. VITRINGA

...of those times; or if it could be proved that the words of Moses, though of the same meaning, were translated into the Egyptian idiom of a later age—something which has not been proved so far. But why would the Israelites find it more difficult to pronounce **Tsaphnath** <note>original Hebrew: צפנת</note> or **Tsaphnach** <note>original Hebrew: צפנח</note> than **Tsaphnath** <note>original Hebrew: צפנת</note>? 

I therefore believe that the phrase **Zaphnath-Paaneah** <note>original Hebrew: צפנת פענח</note> was truly an Egyptian word, given to **Joseph** by **Pharaoh**; indeed, even the Greek form **Psonthon Phanech** <note>original Greek: Ψονϑον Φανὴχ</note> arose from this very Hebrew spelling, and the explanation for both can be sought from the Hebrew dialect. 

Let us attempt this. To the Hebrews, **Zaphan** <note>original Hebrew: צפן</note> means *to hide, cover, or conceal* <note>original Greek/Latin: κρύπτειν, tegere, abscondere, occultare</note>; from this, **Zaphnath** <note>original Hebrew: צפנת</note> means *a hidden or secret thing*. I suspect that **Paaneah** <note>original Hebrew: פענח</note> should be derived from the root **Panah** <note>original Hebrew: פנה</note>, which enjoys the meaning of *looking at, inspecting, or contemplating*. 

Clearly, I believe that the final letter **Cheth** <note>original Hebrew: ח</note> was pronounced more harshly by the Egyptians than by the Hebrews, exactly like the letter **He** when marked with a **Mappick** <term>Mappiq: a dot placed in a Hebrew letter (usually at the end of a word) to indicate that it should be fully pronounced as a consonant rather than remaining silent.</term>. I believe this also occurs in other Oriental languages. Thus, the root **Panah** was changed to **Panach** <note>original Hebrew: פנח</note> according to that pronunciation. 

But you may ask, where did the **Ayin** <note>original Hebrew: ע</note> come from? I have no doubt that the ancients used the letters **Aleph, Vav, Yod, and Ayin** <note>original Hebrew: א ו י ע</note> in place of vowels <term>Matres lectionis: "mothers of reading," consonants used to indicate the presence of a vowel in ancient scripts before modern vowel points were invented.</term>, since vowel points had not yet been invented. Therefore, the letter **Ayin** in the word **Paaneah** performs the duty of a vowel, either an *a* or an *e*. 

Nor should this seem strange when done by the Egyptians, since it was common among other Eastern peoples and even among the Hebrews themselves. I would certainly wander too far from my goal if I were to go off again into a lengthy demonstration of this truth; for I have many such examples at hand, which I have collected in great number, from which I can show that these same letters were placed in the stead of vowels not only in common Hebrew writings but in the **Holy Scripture** itself in ancient times. I shall do this on another occasion. And this...

# SACRED OBSERVATIONS

->111<-

According to the interpretation of **Zaphnath-Paaneah** <note>original Hebrew: צפנת פענח</note>, it would mean "a contemplator of hidden and secret things," an "interpreter of dreams" <note>original Greek: ὀνειροκρίτης</note> and "a discoverer of secrets" <note>original Greek: κρυπτῶν εὑρετὴς</note>, just as **Josephus** <note>Flavius Josephus, a 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian</note> and **Philo** <note>Philo of Alexandria, a Hellenistic Jewish philosopher</note> have stated. This etymological reasoning seems to me to rightly correspond to the deeds performed by **Joseph**. **Rabbi Abraham** <note>Abraham ibn Ezra, a medieval biblical commentator</note> believed that the word *Sohar* <note>original Hebrew: סהר; refers to the "prison" where Joseph was held in Genesis 39:20</note> was also Egyptian, not Hebrew, because it is immediately followed by an explanation: "the place where the king’s prisoners were bound" <note>original Hebrew: מקום אשר אסורי המלך אסורים</note>. Its origin cannot be shown from the modern Egyptian language, but must be sought in Arabic, where *sahar* means *he kept watch* and *he detained in watchfulness*. From this, we gather that *Sohar* denotes a *round tower* intended for custody and watchfulness. Compare *Song of Solomon 7:2* and see the Reverend **Heidegger** <note>Johann Heinrich Heidegger, a 17th-century Swiss theologian</note> *part 2, Exercise 20, section 7*. It has also long been noticed that the name *Nile* <note>original Greek: τὸ Nilus</note> originates from *Nachal* <note>original Hebrew: נחל; a term for a river or valley</note>. For instead of *Nahal* or *Naal*, the Syrians and Egyptians said *Neel*; just as the Phoenicians and others said *Beel* instead of *Bahal* or *Baal*. Therefore, just as from *Beel* comes *Bel*, and then *Belos* <note>original Greek: Βῆλος</note>; so from *Neel* comes *Nel* or *Neil*, from which we get *Neilos* <note>original Greek: Νεῖλος</note>. Moreover, **Mela** <note>Pomponius Mela, a Roman geographer</note> *book 3, chapter 10*, reports that the source of the Nile in Ethiopia is called *Nuchul* by the inhabitants—undoubtedly from *Nachal* <note>original Hebrew: נחל</note>, from which we derive *Neilos*. If you wish, see the same man <note>Heidegger</note> *Exercise 3, section 41*. And by the same reasoning, we could point out the etymologies of **Horus** <note>original Latin: Ori</note>, **Osiris** <note>original Latin: Ofiridis</note>, **Apis**, and **Serapis** from the Hebrew dialect, had great men not already performed this task, and if the purpose of this dissertation of ours did not forbid it.

Now that we have contemplated the fates of the Egyptians, let us give the next place to the Greeks; since their language differs greatly today from the Oriental languages, it will be necessary to briefly indicate the origin and progress of that change, and the reasons for it;

I would first like it to be noted, then, that the most ancient Greece does not owe its origin to any single family or single nation, but was born from many families and various men arriving from different regions of the earth. I shall add here a very remarkable passage from **Strabo** <note>Strabo (c. 64 BC – 24 AD) was a Greek geographer and philosopher whose work "Geographica" is a vital source for ancient history</note>, which appears in *Book VII, page 322*:

"Now, **Hecataeus of Miletus** <note>An early Greek historian and geographer (c. 550 – 476 BC)</note> says concerning the **Peloponnese** that before the Greeks, barbarians <note>term: barbarian — from the Greek *barbaros*, used to describe anyone who did not speak Greek; it did not initially mean "uncivilized" but "foreign-tongued"</note> inhabited it. Even from some of their names, their barbarian origin is evident: **Cecrops**, **Codrus**, **Aeiclus**, **Cothus**, **Drymas**, and **Celaenus**. Furthermore, the Thracians, **Illyrians**, and **Epeirotes** are even until now located on the borders."

These things are translated as follows:

*Concerning the Peloponnese, Hecataeus of Miletus relates that before the Greeks it was inhabited by Barbarians. ...Tereus <note>A legendary Thracian king</note> held Daulis; the Phoenicians, who were companions of Cadmus, held the Cadmeia <note>The citadel of ancient Thebes</note>; and the Aones, Tembices, and Hyantes <note>Ancient tribes of Boeotia</note> held Boeotia itself. By "barbarians," however, **Strabo** understands those who neither knew Greek nor pronounced it correctly—that is, for the most part, the Eastern <note>original: "Orientales"</note> peoples. Thus, in *Book XIV*: <note>original Greek: Βαρβαρίζειν γὰρ ἐπὶ τῶν κακῶς Ἑλληνιζόντων, οὐκ ἐπὶ τῶν Καρσὶ λαλούντων εἰώθαμεν λέγειν.</note> "For we are accustomed to use the term 'to barbarize' for those who speak Greek poorly, not for those who speak in the Carian tongue."

Indeed, if no other testimony remained to us, this alone could suffice for our purpose. Where there is such a great mixture <note>original: "colluvies," implying a dense gathering or confluence</note> of various men, families, and peoples, should we not expect a huge and indeed very rapid change in the language? And truly, that is exactly what happened. For there was nothing naturally suited to promoting the transformation of languages that was not found in abundance in Greece. But it will be necessary to investigate the origin of the Greek race and the Greek dialect from this point a little more precisely.

Among those who revere the writings of the **Divine Moses**, there is no one who does not believe that the first men arrived in Greece from the East, since the parents of all mankind—the **Sons of Noah** <note>Referring to the biblical "Table of Nations" in Genesis, where the descendants of Noah's son Japheth are traditionally associated with the Isles of the Gentiles or Greece</note>—were born there and eventually filled the whole world. However, at exactly what age after the Great Flood those men set out from the East into Greece, I consider a matter that is indeed very difficult to determine.

This much, at least, must be established beyond all doubt: that the **Egyptians** were much earlier than the Greeks, since the Greeks themselves assert that they owe much of their origin to the Egyptians. Therefore, they are more recent than the Egyptians, although otherwise ancient—

This man, however, brought Oriental <note>In this context, "Oriental" refers to the Near East, including Egypt and Phoenicia</note> customs, letters, and many words—whether Egyptian or Phoenician is debated—into Greece. Cadmus was certainly entirely of *Egyptian* origin; but because the Egyptians were not skilled in maritime affairs, nor was their land equipped with convenient harbors, he was carried into Greece by a Phoenician fleet, just as I suspect all those said to have traveled from Egypt to Greece were transported. Indeed, it should be noted that the ancient Greeks wrote from right to left in the manner of the Orientals. Thus *Pausanias* <note>A 2nd-century AD Greek traveler and geographer</note> says: *The name is inscribed on the statue of Agamemnon: and it is also written toward the left from the right.* <note>original Greek: γέγραπται δὲ καὶ τὸ ἐπὶ τὰ λαιὰ ἐκ δεξιῶν</note> *This, moreover, was also written from the right toward the left.* He identifies the third migration as that of *Danaus*, who, by the advice of *Minerva* <note>The Roman name for Athena, the goddess of wisdom</note>, built a ship and set out from Egypt for Greece with his daughters. This epoch falls in the 52nd Attic Year. *Eusebius, in the second book of his Chronicles*, says that this Danaus corresponds to the final years of *Moses*, during which he lived in the desert (page 79). As for **Inachus**, who was mentioned among the first and who is older than **Cecrops**, **Cadmus**, and **Danaus**, I judge his origin to be entirely uncertain. Some maintain the conclusion that he migrated from Phoenicia into Greece based on his name, which they derive from the words *Anakim* and *Anak* <note>original Hebrew: ענקים & ענק</note>; from which also the word *anax* and *anakes* <note>original Greek: αναξ & ανακες</note>, by which Kings and Princes are called by the Greeks, descends. This much is certainly established: his immediate descendants undertook many migrations back and forth between Greece and Egypt. For **Cadmus** and **Danaus** are counted among his progeny. From this we might perhaps conjecture that even this **Inachus** originated from Egypt.

Since these things are so, I can hardly wrap my head around why the most learned **Bochart** <note>Samuel Bochart (1599–1667), a French Protestant biblical scholar</note> in **book I, chapter xv, page 68**, so constantly denies that Ancient Greek agreed with the ancient Egyptian language. Indeed, I would not dare to assert what he claims **Kircher** <note>Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680), a Jesuit polymath who claimed all languages derived from Egyptian</note> urges: namely, that Ancient Greek was as similar to the Egyptian language as Italian is now to Ancient Latin. For I would not be able to prove that, just as the venerable Kircher cannot. But nor can the most learned Bochart deny it, since nothing certain is established even for him regarding either ancient language. For neither from modern Greek to the language...

...v, nor did they have the letters *pi* <note>original: "$\pi$"</note> and *phi* <note>original: "$\phi$"</note> in the most ancient times. Consequently, no letter remained that could represent the Hebrew letter *Vav* except for the single letter *pi* <note>original: "$\varpi$"</note>. This letter was used by them in that earliest age, just like the Hebrew letter *Bet* <note>original: "$\beth$"</note>, which corresponds to both our *p* and *ph*. In this way, they translate the Greek word for a bowl or vial, *phiale* <note>original: "$\Phi\iota\alpha\lambda\eta$"</note>, in the *Torat Cohanim* <note>The "Torat Cohanim" is the Sifra, an ancient legal commentary on the book of Leviticus.</note> as *piks* <note>original: "פיקס"</note>; and they translate *phiale* as *piyla* or *piyli* <note>original: "פיילא & פיילי"</note> in the tractate *Sotah* <note>A volume of the Talmud dealing with ritual laws.</note>. From these examples, it is established that the Hebrew *Bet* is sometimes expressed by them as a *phi* <note>original: "$\phi$"</note>. And so it happened even among the ancient Greeks. 

Because of this, I consider it evident that the Greek word for fire, *pyr* <note>original: "$\tau\grave{o}$ $\pi\tilde{\upsilon}\rho$"</note>, is derived from the Hebrew word for light, *or* <note>original: "אור"</note>. Furthermore, from this same root *or*, which also carries the meaning "to shine," descend the Greek words *orao* <note>I see</note>, *horama* <note>a vision</note>, *orthomai* <note>I rise</note>, *ouranos* <note>heaven or sky</note>, *ouranio* <note>to reach to the sky</note>, and other similar roots. From the word *nur* <note>original: "נור"; Vitringa defines this as "to dwell" or "habitation," though it more commonly means "fire" in Semitic roots; he likely associates it with the "hearth" of a home.</note>, meaning "to dwell" and "a dwelling place," come the Greek terms *naio* <note>I dwell</note>, *noisma* <note>a dwelling or habit; Vitringa notes these are very common in Homer</note>, *naos* or *neos* <note>a temple</note>, and also *nao*, which some have used in place of *naio*. From the Hebrew *barah* <note>original: "ברה"</note>, meaning "to feed," and *habrah* <note>original: "הברה"</note>, meaning "food," come the Greek *brotos* <note>mortal or edible</note>, *brosimos* <note>edible</note>, *brosis* <note>the act of eating</note>, and *brotikos* <note>relating to food</note>. 

From the Hebrew *kaved* <note>original: "כבד"</note>, meaning "mighty" or "strong," we get the *Kabeiroi* <note>original: "$\kappa\acute{\alpha}\beta\varepsilon\iota\rho o\iota$"; These were "The Great Gods" of Samothrace, mysterious deities of the ancient Greek world.</note>, the gods of the Samothracians. From the Hebrew *maha* <note>original: "מחא"</note>, meaning "to strike" or "to hit," descend the Greek words *mache* <note>battle</note>, *machetos* <note>fought</note>, and *machomai* <note>I fight</note>. The Hebrew word *shevet* <note>original: "שבט"; meaning a rod or staff</note> gave rise to the words *skeptron* <note>a scepter</note>, *skepto* <note>to prop or lean</note>, and *skeptomai* <note>to lean upon or pretend</note>. In these cases, the letter *r* is not essential to the root of the word. Hence, in the **Doric** dialect, it is *skapton*. **Pindar**, in his first *Olympian Ode*:

->who wields the scepter of divine law<-

We could present many more proofs of this kind, and indeed they have been presented everywhere by learned men. <meta>This page continues Vitringa's philological study of the relationship between Hebrew and Greek. Having previously discussed phonetic similarities (like the letter Vav/Bet), he now moves to a crucial methodological warning: distinguishing ancient Hebrew roots in Greek from later Greek loanwords that entered Jewish speech.</meta>

<page-num>121</page-num>
<header>SACRED OBSERVATIONS. 121</header>

...were, we have intentionally omitted out of diligence. However, it must be observed that from the category of these words which were transferred from Hebrew to Greek, one must entirely exclude those which the Hebrews received from the Greeks in later times. We have noticed that this distinction has been neglected by some. Certainly, **Abraham Mylius**, in his most worthy little book titled *The Belgian Language* <note>original: "Lingua Belgica"</note>, chapter iv, when intending to show specimens of words that are common to the **Hebrew and Greek languages**, mixes in certain terms of a type that the Hebrews or Chaldeans received from the Greeks in a later age—when their language began to be corrupted—and certainly not words the Greeks received from the Hebrews.

Examples include: *symphonia* <note>original: "סמפניה"</note>, which occurs in **Daniel 3:5, 10, 15** and corresponds to the Greek *symphonia* <note>original: "συμφωνία", meaning a harmony of sounds or a musical instrument</note>; *psanterin* <note>original: "פסנטרין"</note>, which agrees with their *psalterion* <note>original: "Ψαλτήριον", a stringed instrument</note>; and *sanhedrin* <note>original: "סנהדרין"</note>, which is the very same as the Greek *synedrion* <note>original: "συνέδριον", an assembly or council</note>, or "a seat of judges" <note>original: "מושב הדיינין"</note> as the Hebrews themselves interpret it. 

But truly, all these words are purely Greek. None of them are found in the original Hebrew context <note>Vitringa refers here to the core vocabulary of the Hebrew Bible</note>, but are words which the Chaldeans, and later the Hebrews, received into their speech in quite large numbers when they attempted to live among the Greeks and engage in trade with them—indeed, at a time when the whole world spoke Greek. 

If, however, you desire to see a vast catalog of such words, you should consult the distinguished man **David Cohen de Lara** in his book titled *The City of David* <note>original: "עיר דוד"</note>, or, *On the Agreement of Rabbinic Words with Greek and Certain Other European Languages*, which was collected with the greatest industry. Therefore, that kind of agreement in no way aids our purpose, since we are concerned with Hebrew words, not Rabbinic ones; we seek Greek words derived from Hebrew, not Rabbinic words derived from Greek.

...let us derive. Just as Greek words have been derived by us, so too can entire **phrases** <note>original: "φρασεις"</note> and modes of expression be most easily and conveniently derived from the **Hebrew**; a task which has also been most successfully performed in more than one place by learned men.

This resulted in a remarkable change in their language in a short time compared to other Eastern peoples, yet in such a way that it is still clear from evident examples that their language was born in the East. First, however, we take up those things found in the work of the most illustrious man *Barnabas Brissonius* <note>A French jurist and scholar (1531–1591) who wrote a famous study on Persian customs titled *De regio Persarum principatu*.</note> concerning the *Kingdom of the Persians, Book 2, page 279.* There he recounts many Persian names and words, although he explains none of them from Oriental languages. *Add to these,* he says, *that CYRUS in the Persian language signifies the SUN.* The author *Ctesias* <note>A Greek physician and historian who served at the court of the Persian King Artaxerxes II.</note>, who relates that *Parysatis bore another son to Darius besides Artaxerxes, adds: and he was given the name Cyrus after the sun.* <note>original Greek: καὶ τίθεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἡλίου Κῦρον</note> *Plutarch* in his life of *Artaxerxes* says: *Cyrus, therefore, took his name from the ancient Cyrus; and they say he [the ancient Cyrus] was named after the sun.* <note>original Greek: ὁ μὲν οὖν Κῦρος, ἀπὸ Κύρου τοῦ παλαιοῦ τοὔνομα ἔσχεν: ἐκείνῳ δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἡλίου γενέσθαι φασí</note>

# C. VITRINGA

...and that "the Persians call the Sun *Cyrus*." <note>original Greek: κῦρος δὲ καλεῖν Πέρσας τὸν Ἥλιον. This is a common claim in ancient Greek histories, suggesting the name of the great Persian king was synonymous with the sun.</note> To this, he adds several points. We are certainly unaware of what all the learned men have said regarding the etymology of this name *Cyrus*, for we do not have the leisure to look into every one of them. We will, therefore, only state what seems likely to us. The Persians were accustomed to pronounce the letter *h*—which corresponds to the Hebrew letters *He* [ה] and *Heth* [ח]—very forcefully. The most learned *Bochart* <note>Samuel Bochart (1599–1667), a French Protestant biblical scholar and geographer famous for his work on the animals of the Bible and ancient geography.</note> notes this in his *Phalegh*, Book II, chapter XX: *It is customary,* he says, *for the Persians and the Carmanians <note>A people from the region of Carmania, modern-day Kerman, Iran.</note> who live nearby, to pronounce the letter "He" [ה] more forcefully, as if it were an "x" or a "k".* Thus, the "Brachmann" <note>likely referring to the Brahmins or Indian linguistic sources as understood by 17th-century scholars</note> name is written in Persian as *Brah-mah* [ברה המה] with a simple *He*. This is also seen in *da-he* [דה] for "decem" <note>Latin for "ten"</note> and *sha-he* [שאה] for "Shah," which signifies a King. If the letter *He* [ה] was pronounced in this way, how much more so the letter *Heth* [ח], which has a far harsher sound. From this, I gather that the word *Cheres* [חרס] was pronounced by them as *Keres*, though *Keres* and *Cheres* differ very little in pronunciation.

In the Hebrew language, however, *Cheres* [חרס] signifies the Sun. For example, in **Job 9:7**: *Who speaks to the Sun* [לחרס], *and it does not rise.* Also in **Judges 14:18**: *Before the sun* [ההחרס] *had gone down.* <note>The Hebrew text literally refers to the sun setting, though some Latin translations used by Vitringa interpreted this as rising.</note> This word *Cheres* [חרס] seems to me to be the very same as *Kyros* [κῦρος] or *Cyrus*, with a slight change of vowels, as happens in all languages. It should not bother us that the name *Cyrus* is written in the Hebrew language as *Koresh* [כורש] by **Isaiah**, **Ezra**, and other sacred writers; for these holy men were attempting to express the Persian pronunciation of the name *Cyrus*, just as was done with the name *Darius* [דריוש] and others found in the book of **Ezra**.

We add another name, which *Brissonius* read in the works of *Ammianus Marcellinus* <note>A 4th-century Roman soldier and historian.</note> in Book XXIV. *Naarmalcha*, he says, *signifies the "Royal River," according to the interpretation of Ammianus.* These are his words on page 286. ...[though it is split] <note>The text continues from the previous page's discussion of the river Euphrates.</note> by great masses of water from the river, leading toward the **Babylonian** regions to serve the fields and surrounding cities; another branch, named *Naarmalcha*, which translates to the "River of Kings," flows past **Ctesiphon** <note>An ancient city on the eastern bank of the Tigris, serving as a royal capital for the Parthian and Sassanid Empires.</note>. Truly, nothing is easier than explaining the origin of this word *Naarmalcha*, for the components are essentially Hebrew. *Nahar* [נהר] and *Naar* signify a river, and *Melech* [מלך] or *Malca* [מלכא] signifies a King. *Narmalca*, therefore, is the Royal Stream, which **Strabo** <note>A Greek geographer and historian (c. 64 BC – 24 AD).</note> in his sixteenth book called the "Royal River" <note>original Greek: ποταμὸν βασίλειον</note>, and which is still called *Almalchar* by the **Assyrians** today—with the *Nar* contracted into *Ar*—as recorded in **Pliny**, Book VI, chapter 26. See, if you please, the notes of **Lindenbruch** <note>Friedrich Lindenbruch (1573–1648), a scholar known for his editions of Latin authors including Ammianus Marcellinus.</note>. Many other names of this kind occur in **Ammianus** <note>Ammianus Marcellinus (c. 330–397 AD), a Roman soldier and historian.</note> which are just as easy to explain as this one.

We cannot, however, overlook the word *Suren* or *Surena*, the name used to distinguish those among the **Persians** who held the second rank of power after the King. **Ammianus**, in Book XXX, writes: *Surena arrived, a man of the second rank of power after the King.* **Zosimus** <note>A Greek historian living in Constantinople (c. 490s–510s AD).</note> also notes: *Surena; this is the name of an office among the Persians.* <note>original Greek: Σουρήνας, ἀρχῆς δὲ τοῦτο παρὰ Πέρסαις ὄνομα.</note> This is especially noteworthy because the most learned **Lindenbruch** has nothing to say on the matter here. I believe *Surena* should be derived from the Hebrew *Sar* [שר], which with the suffix becomes *Sari* [שרי]. From this comes *Sarena* or *Surena* by adding a very common suffix. Indeed, *Sar* designates a "Great Prince" or leader, a meaning I believe is very fitting in this context.

**Brissonius** <note>Barnabé Brisson (1531–1591), a French jurist and scholar of Persian antiquities.</note> proceeds in his listing of names. **GANGAMELA**, according to the Persians, is the *House of the Camel*, on the authority of **Strabo** (Book XV or XVI) and **Plutarch** in his *Life of Alexander*. To me, certainly, this word also appears clearly Hebrew. Who does not know that *Gamal* [גמל] signifies a **Camel** to the Hebrews? From which word also the Greek *kamēlos* [κάμηλος]...

-># SACRED OBSERVATIONS.<-

They were called *Scythians*, or *Nomads* (as by *Homer*), and as the western regions became known over time, they began to be called *Celts*, *Iberians*, or by the mixed names *Celtiberians* and *Celtoscythians*; previously, out of ignorance, all these individual nations were addressed by a single name. Therefore, all the nations that spread toward the north were called *Scythians* by the *Ancients*. These excursions were either *Asiatic* or *European*, which is why the inhabitants of both tracts of land were called *Scythians*.

The *Asiatic Scythians* are those who lived within and beyond the very high *Imaus* <note>The Imaus range generally refers to the Himalayas, Pamir, or Hindu Kush mountains in ancient geography.</note> mountains, to say nothing of the *Taurus* mountains. *Strabo* <note>A Greek geographer and historian (c. 64 BC–24 AD).</note> mentions them in *Book 11, page 88*. Those called *Europeans* wandered near the *Euxine Sea* <note>The Black Sea.</note> and were to the north in relation to the *Macedonians*. These same people lived all around the *Sea*. Indeed, *Diodorus Siculus* <note>A Greek historian of the 1st century BC.</note> speaks in this manner in *Book IV*: <note>original Greek: τὸν δὲ Πόντον κατ᾿ ἐκείνους τοὺς χρόνους περιοικούμενον ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν βαρβάρων καὶ παντελῶς ἀγρίων ἄξενον προσαγορεύεσθαι, ξενοκτονούντων τῶν ἐγχωρίων τοὺς καταπλέοντας.</note> "The Black Sea, since in those times it was inhabited all around by *Barbarian* and utterly wild nations, and because the locals would slaughter any guests who sailed to them, was called *Axenus* <note>The term 'Axenus' means 'inhospitable' in Greek. This was the original name of the Black Sea before it was euphemistically renamed 'Euxinus' or 'Hospitable Sea'.</note>."

*Apollodorus* <note>Likely Apollodorus of Athens, a 2nd-century BC scholar.</note> testifies to the same in *Strabo, Book VII*. Thus, under the name of the *European Scythians* are included the *Thracians*, the *Mysians*, and the other nations who lived either near or beyond the *Black Sea*. As *Homer* describes them in *Iliad, Book V*. Indeed, these *European Scythians* are more famous in all history than the *Asiatic Scythians*—though mention of the latter is not infrequent—because they were able to extend the boundaries of their expeditions further, and they found a more fertile region than...

Asiatic. Since we have this prior knowledge about the Scythians, it will not be difficult for us to investigate the time when these Scythians began their migrations. Indeed, we cannot imagine that people at that time would have begun expeditions into the harsh northern region while the most fertile lands of the East were vacant and not yet occupied by other men. To be sure, we do not believe that all peoples remained in the East until the time of *Abraham*, as we will soon demonstrate the contrary. But neither do we think it somehow fits the human character to choose worse lands while leaving behind more abundant ones. That some men moved into *Egypt* and *Greece* is certainly also based on reason. For those places were both very pleasant and very fertile at the same time, and in no way inferior to the Eastern plains. From this we conclude that certain nations only withdrew into the Northern regions when the more pleasant areas of either Greece or the East had already been claimed by others. This happened in the East during the age of *Abraham*; and in the West—that is, in *Greece*—during the age of the Patriarchs; for we have previously shown that Greece began to be populated at that time. Those Scythians who, in the age of Abraham, began to migrate toward the North and live in the neighboring mountains, were wild men, living in a rustic manner, and occasionally attacking other nations unexpectedly. In our previous description, they appeared to us under the name of the *Elymaeans* <note>The Elymaeans were an ancient people of Elam, located in present-day southwestern Iran.</note> and the *Ancient Persians*, since they too were Scythians, as we briefly mentioned before. Moreover, since these Scythians themselves originated from Asia, they could have used no other language than one very similar to the Oriental <note>In this context, "Oriental" refers to the Semitic languages of the ancient Near East, such as Hebrew and Aramaic.</note> languages. 41. <note>The original Greek numeral "μα." indicates section 41.</note> For **ARI** is said to be **ONE** in Scythian, while **MASPUS** means **EYE**. We certainly do not know by what reasoning learned men have interpreted this Scythian term in the past; to us, indeed, it seems it should be derived from the Oriental languages. We therefore comment freely on the matter. We truly cannot imagine that the word **ARI** was recorded with the correct spelling; rather, we believe **ADI** should be substituted. If this word had been written in Hebrew characters, we could easily discover the origin of this error. For the letters Resh [ר] and Dalet [ד] differ very little from each other in shape, which is the source of so many errors found in the work of the Seventy <note>The "Seventy" refers to the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note>. Note: The OCR likely reflects a common scribal or printing error where the letter Dalet (ד) was replaced by Resh (ר), the very confusion Vitringa is discussing.</note>. As seen in *Ezekiel 33:30*: "one with another" <note>original Hebrew: חד את אחד, chad et achad</note>. This *Chad* is indeed written by Latin authors as *Chad*, *Had*, or *Ad*, and with the addition of the letter iota it becomes *Adi*. In this way, *Chad* was also the name given to the ancient god *Ammon* <note>Vitringa suggests a link between the name of the Egyptian/Libyan deity Amun and the Semitic word for "one," implying a concept of a "sole" or "unified" deity.</note>. **MASPUS**, however, leads us directly to the root *tsaphah* <note>Hebrew: צפה</note>, which means "to watch" or "to observe." The letter Mem [מ] is often prefixed to nouns, resulting in *mitzpeh* <note>Hebrew: מצפה</note>, meaning a "watchtower" or a "lookout" <note>original Greek: σκοπια, skopia</note>. From this comes the old Scythian word *mitzpeh*, referring to that which we observe with the eye. And thus, the *Arimaspi* are called "one-eyed" by the Scythians.

<header>OBSERVATIONS ON SACRED MATTERS.</header>

...[we] see. A very frequent word in the Sacred Code is **Topheth** <note>Hebrew: תפת</note>, which signifies a place of perpetual flame. **2 Kings 23:10**: *And he defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom.* <note>original Hebrew: וטמא את התפת אשר בגי בן הנם</note>. **Jeremiah 7:31**: *And they built the* **high places of Topheth** <note>Hebrew: במות התפת, bamot ha-tophet</note> *to burn their sons and daughters in the fire.* These are elsewhere called the **high places of Baal** <note>Hebrew: במות הבעל, bamot ha-Ba'al</note>. 

Authors derive that word **Topheth** from **toph** <note>Hebrew: תף</note>, which signifies a **drum** <note>Latin: tympanum</note>, because the worship of **Molech** <note>A Canaanite deity associated with ritual fire and sacrifice.</note> was performed with drums <note>Traditional accounts suggest drums were played to drown out the cries of sacrificed children.</note>. I do not, for my part, have weighty or solid reasons to despise that etymology, but neither do others have strong arguments to confirm it. I say only this: words of that grammatical form more unusually descend from those same roots. In this way, **mophet** <note>Hebrew: מופת; usually meaning a "wonder" or "miraculous sign."</note>, which matches the form of **Topheth**, they trace to a different origin. 

Therefore, I strongly doubt whether **Topheth** might not come from an unusual root that has the meaning of "burning," and thus for this **Topheth** to signify that place in which there are perpetual flames, or that God or Goddess who presides over that fire, or whom that fire represented. As it seems to be taken entirely in that passage of Jeremiah. And so **Topheth** would plainly agree with **Vesta** <note>The Roman goddess of the hearth and home, whose temple fire was never allowed to go out.</note>, especially since that word also has its origin from **esh** <note>Hebrew: אש</note>, "fire," as has long been proven by learned men. 

From **Topheth**, therefore, the name **Tabiti** <note>A Scythian deity identified by Herodotus as the goddess of fire, equivalent to the Greek Hestia or Roman Vesta.</note> is easily derived, if the letter *p* [פ] is changed to *b*, which is a very frequent linguistic shift. Moreover, the name **Papæus** <note>The Scythian supreme god, identified by Herodotus with Zeus.</note> is undoubtedly from **abba** [אבא] and **ab** [אב] <note>Hebrew/Aramaic for "father."</note>, from which come "Father" and other words of that nature. For we cannot linger too long on these and similar points. We are merely giving examples. Now, these **Asiatic Scythians**, extending into the north or toward the East or West—that is, into the borders of Europe—betook themselves...

# SACRED OBSERVATIONS.

### THE ORIGINS OF THE NORTHERN TONGUES

The languages of the Scythians, Celts, Goths, Getae, Massagetae, Cimbri, Teutons, and Germans—that is, the **Ancient Belgian** <note>In the 17th century, "Belgian" often referred to the Low German or Dutch dialects of the Low Countries as a whole.</note> (for all these nations formerly used one idiom, although the manner of pronunciation was somewhat varied over the course of time)—must be derived entirely from the **Oriental Languages**. We could bring forward infinite examples and specimens of this fact, not only from the most ancient remains of that Old Belgian language—in the investigation of which the very diligent **Boxhornius** <note>Marcus Zuerius van Boxhorn (1612–1653), a Dutch scholar who was one of the first to propose the "Scythian" (Indo-European) origin of languages.</note> applied much industry—but also from our modern tongue, and especially indeed from **Frisian**, which, as it is simpler, is much purer and possesses more monuments of antiquity.

We have:
* from *ʿābar* [עבר] <note>meaning 'to cross over'</note> our word **over**; 
* from *šebaʿ* [שבע] the word **seven**; 
* from *pereq* [פרק] <note>meaning 'to divide'</note> **break** <note>original: "breecken"</note>; 
* from *ʾereṣ* [ארץ] **earth** <note>original: "aerde"</note>; 
* from *pāʿal* [פעל] <note>meaning 'to do' or 'work'</note> **toil** or **labor** <note>original: "pielen" and "arbeyden"</note>; 
* from *gebûl* [גבול] <note>meaning 'border' or 'boundary'</note> **gable** <note>original: "gebel"</note>; 
* from *bāraḥ* [ברח] <note>meaning 'to pass through'</note> **bread** <note>original: "broodt"</note>; 
* from *qôl* [קול] <note>meaning 'voice' or 'sound'</note> **up** <note>original: "hup"</note>; 
* from *hûʾ* [הוא] <note>meaning 'he'</note> **after** <note>original: "achter"</note>; 
* from *šēš* [שש] **six** <note>original: "ses"</note>; 
* from *ṣad* [צד] **side** <note>original: "syde"</note>; 
* from *ʾēm* [אם] **mother** <note>original: "mem," a Frisian word for mother</note>.

You will see many other such examples in the work of **Abraham Mylius** <note>Abraham van der Mijle (1563–1637), author of "Lingua Belgica," which argued for the antiquity of the Dutch language.</note>, whom I recently praised, on pages 26 and 27 of *On the Belgian Language*; indeed, you will collect them yourself without any great effort, if only you pay attention. Furthermore, you can find a wealth of words of this kind—that is, truly **Celtic**—scattered throughout the writings of the aforementioned **Boxhornius**. 

I believe this one thing must be added: the **Hebrew language** can be arranged through no other language as conveniently and emphatically as through **Belgian** [Dutch], since their modes of speaking agree much with one another. It has been a pleasure for me to notice many examples of this from time to time in my reading of the **Sacred Scripture**. I will add one from **Isaiah**, chapter 24, verse 2.

### OBSERVATIONES SACRÆ ###

...it could not have happened, if you maintain that the origin of languages took place at the building of the **Tower of Babel**, unless you were to maintain that God impressed imperfect ideas of words into men’s minds—which is absurd. The names of the most ancient Gods worshiped by the nations, as well as the names of lands and regions used only after the construction at Babylon, must all be explained from the **Hebrew language** and from no other. From this, it is clearly gathered that those other languages had not yet emerged among those nations at that time. Furthermore, the families of **Ham** and **Japheth** (if one wishes to add him) were so few in number at the time of the Babylonian structure that it is plainly <term>absurd <note>original Greek: ἄτοπον (atophon), meaning "out of place," "strange," or "unfitting."</note></term> for such a great diversity of languages to have existed among them at that time. **Moses** makes no mention at all of the origin of these various languages in his narrative. I will not even mention the other difficulties that weigh against this opposing view, which are exceedingly heavy. 

We would have pursued all these matters more extensively if the nature of this writing had required it; for our intention is only to provide samples of our observations. Indeed, we are quite annoyed with ourselves that these dissertations have grown so large. Truly, this was far from our original intent and purpose. However, it was done for this reason: so that I might convince my reader of the truth and compel him to embrace one of the interpretations presented in the first dissertation—that is, to yield to the truth, which we believe to be a pious endeavor.

"They shall seek [it] from his mouth." <note>original Hebrew: יבקשו מפיהו (*yebakshu mipihu*). For the Priests and the <term>nomikoi</term> <note>original Greek: νομικοὶ; refers to those expert in the Law, often translated as "lawyers" or "legal scholars"</note>—who interpreted the Law and were the guardians of those traditions—were able to know something that the Jewish people *could not know*. However, under the New Covenant, there is no truth that every single one of the faithful *cannot* know equally, provided they apply themselves diligently to it and are willing to use those means which God Himself, in His goodness, has established for us. We believe this to be the genuine sense of that prophecy read in *Jeremiah* chapter 31:34. <note>Jeremiah 31:34 describes the New Covenant where "no longer shall each one teach his neighbor... for they shall all know me."</note> 

And this is also what we believe our Lord was rebuking in those who were appointed to explain the Law: that they hid the genuine sense of the Law from the people, concealed and distorted the prophecies that existed concerning the Messiah, and then substituted a most wicked interpretation of the Divine Words for that true and genuine one. By doing so, they entangled that unrefined and dull-witted people in carnal thoughts and desires, and turned their minds away from the true Messiah. And these are the things which it was necessary to say by way of preface concerning the true *Kabbalah* <note>Vitringa uses this term to mean a "received tradition" of spiritual interpretation handed down from the time of Moses</note> which existed in the Dispensation of the Old Covenant.

Those of the Jews who excel the others in both antiquity and the knowledge of divine matters all assert that the compendium of this *Kabbalah* is found in the ten **Sefirot** <note>original Hebrew: ספירות</note> or *enumerations*, which we always see depicted in this form in their books.

FROM THE APPEARANCE OF HIS LOINS AND UPWARD AND FROM THE APPEARANCE OF HIS LOINS AND DOWNWARD I SAW AS THE APPEARANCE OF FIRE, and it had brightness all around it.* Here the loins are placed as the midpoint between the upper and lower parts, and it is said that above the loins and below the loins there was the same color, like fire. In my judgment, this is to be understood entirely as a <term>toga talaris: a long, formal robe reaching down to the heels</term> of the same color—that is, a most brilliant garment—in which this Son of Man sat upon the throne. To these may be added that figure shown to *Isaiah* in chapter 6:1: *Where* <note>original Hebrew: "שוליו מלאים את ההיכל"</note> *His skirts filled the temple.* This refers to Jesus Christ, whose <term>incarnation: the act of God becoming human</term> <note>original Greek: "ἐσαρκωσις"</note> is prefigured here. For "skirts" <note>original Latin: "Ora"</note> are most especially attributed to *robes*.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Now that we have contemplated the figure we depicted in a general sense, let us proceed to its individual parts. The CORONA <note>original Hebrew: "כתר" (Keter)</note> or CROWN is to be ascribed entirely to our Lord Jesus Christ, since he is delineated in this manner more than once by the Sacred Writers. A worthy passage is that found in *John* [Revelation] chapter 6:2: <note>original Greek: "Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός . Καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ, ἔχων τόξον . &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The word *diadem* <note>Greek: διάδημα</note> is the same for the <term>LXX: the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</term> as the Hebrew word *Keter* <note>Hebrew: כתר</note>, meaning CROWN. Examples are found in the book of *Esther*. But it should also be noted that the *diadem* refers to the *tsaniph* <note>Hebrew: צניף</note> and the *mitsnephet* <note>Hebrew: מצנפת</note>. For the word *diadem* comes from the Greek verb *diadein* <note>διαδεῖν</note>, meaning to bind around or to encircle; and hence it was properly called a certain white *band* with which the head was bound, which was a badge of Kings. It is exactly like the *tsaniph* <note>Hebrew: צניף</note>, which for the <term>LXX</term> is a tiara, a miter, a wreath, or a diadem. <note>original Greek terms: κίδαρις, μίτρα, στέφανος, διάδημα</note> This word descends from the Hebrew root *tsanaph* <note>צנף</note>, which enjoys the meaning of winding and rolling around. 

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, the *tsaniph* is also attributed to Kings. The passage is found in *Isaiah* chapter 62:3: <note>The text incorrectly cites chapter 62:9. Original Hebrew: והיית צניף מלוכה בכף אלהיך</note> *AND YOU SHALL BE A ROYAL DIADEM in the hand of your God.* It is for no other reason that the *mitsnephet* <note>priestly turban</note> is attributed to Priests in the Old Testament, since they were indeed **PRINCES** among the Jewish People, and of that sort regarding them...

To this is added the fact that only a single crown, that is, the *priestly turban*, <note>original Latin: "cidaris Sacerdotalis," referring to the ceremonial mitre of the High Priest.</note> is recorded as being placed on his head in *chapter* III. 5. From this, I conclude that the earlier words should be translated thus: **And you shall make crowns / and you shall set one of them upon the head of Joshua.** <note>original Dutch: "Ende ghy sult kroonen maecken / ende ghy sult daer van een settet op 't hooft van Josua."</note> This mode of speaking is very familiar to the Hebrews. But in this very chapter, a more manifest piece of evidence stands out in *verse* 13: <note>original Hebrew: ומשל על כסאו</note> *And he shall rule upon his throne...*

# C. VITRINGA

After the **Crown** <note>original Hebrew: *Keter*</note>, there follow in one order **Wisdom** <note>original Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</note> and **Understanding** <note>original Hebrew: *Binah*</note>, which we also assign to the head <note>In the symbolic "body" of the Sephiroth, these three attributes form the intellectual faculties located in the head.</note>. Truly, there is no one who does not know that these two *virtues* are very frequently attributed to our Lord Jesus Christ in the sacred scriptures. We have a notable proof in *Isaiah* chapter 11:1–2: *And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the Spirit of* **WISDOM** and **UNDERSTANDING** <note>original Hebrew: *V’nachah alav ruach Yehovah, ruach chokhmah u-binah*</note>. 

A certain Learned Man <note>likely referring to a contemporary Hebraist or commentator</note> has very well said: *Since* **Wisdom** <note>original Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</note> *is usually joined with* **Knowledge** <note>original Hebrew: *Da’at*</note> *or* **Understanding** <note>original Hebrew: *Binah*</note>, *just as Paul often joins* **Wisdom** and **Prudence** <note>original Greek: *sophian kai phronesin*</note> *or* **Knowledge** <note>original Greek: *gnōsin*</note>. *Wisdom’s companions are prudence and circumspection, by which—according to the rules of wisdom, through the love and fear of God—evil is rejected and what is best is chosen, in good conscience.* 

And elsewhere: **Understanding** <note>original Hebrew: *Binah*</note>; Prudence; **Prudence** <note>original Greek: *phronēsis*</note>. The dexterity of judging and choosing according to the conscience of the true and the good. For prudence is the utility of wisdom *in practical matters* <note>original Greek: *en praktois*</note>. Hence **Wisdom** and **Understanding** <note>original Hebrew: *Chokhmah* and *Binah*</note> are joined, as are **Wisdom** and **Prudence** <note>original Greek: *sophia* and *phronēsis*</note>. Prudence is the mother of wisdom. And in this very way, these two virtues are taken in this place, where wisdom is placed first, and prudence follows. 

Let us add another example from the *Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Colossians*, chapter 2:2–3: *To the acknowledgment of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ; In whom are hidden all the treasures of* **WISDOM** and **Knowledge** <note>original Greek: *eis epignōsin tou mystēriou tou Theou kai patros kai Christou; en hō eisi pantes oi thēsauroi tēs sophias kai tēs gnōseōs apokryphoi*</note> (or **UNDERSTANDING** <note>original Hebrew: *Chokhmah* and *Binah* or *Da’at*</note>). 

To which corresponds that which was recorded by the same Paul in the *Epistle to the Ephesians*, chapter 1:8: *Which abounded toward us* (or rather *in us*) *in all* (**Wisdom** and **Understanding**) **WISDOM**—

...**WISDOM** AND **PRUDENCE**. To these, I wonder if I might be permitted to add that which is found in the *Book of Revelation*, chapter 1:14, where His eyes are described as a flame of fire: *And his eyes were like a flame of fire* <note>original Greek: Καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶ ὡς φλόξ πυρός</note>. There follow in order **MAGNIFICENCE** and **POWER** <note>original Hebrew: *Gedulah* and *Gevurah*</note>. All the Hebrew scholars are accustomed to interpret **Greatness** <note>original Hebrew: *Gedulah*</note> through **Loving-kindness** <note>original Hebrew: *Chesed*—the eager desire for doing good</note> and **Might** <note>original Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note> through rigor and severity. I believe both of these attributes are drawn from that most elegant Psalm 145, where without any doubt the Kingdom of Jesus Christ is described: *I will exalt you, my God the King* <note>original Hebrew: *Aromimcha Elohai ha-Melech*</note>, he says. In Dutch: *You who are King* <note>original Dutch: *Ghy die Koninck*</note>. Thus it is said in verses 3 and 4: *Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised, and of His* **MAGNIFICENCE** *there is no searching out* <note>original Hebrew: *Gadol Yehovah u-mehullal me’od ve-ligdulato ein cheker*</note>. *One generation shall praise Your works to another and shall declare Your* **POWER** <note>original Hebrew: *Dor le-dor yeshabach ma’asecha u-gevurotecha yagidu*</note>. Here these two virtues are found. **Might** <note>original Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note> is also ascribed to Him in *Isaiah* chapter 11:2: *And the Spirit of counsel and* **POWER** *shall rest upon him* <note>original Hebrew: *V’nachah alav ruach etzah u-gevurah*</note>.

In the Septuagint <note>The influential Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note>, these terms are rendered as strength, might, dominion, and excellence; certain of these words are also ascribed to our Lord in the New Covenant.

Let us take note of the passage found in the *Book of Revelation*, chapter 4, verse 12: *saying with a loud voice, "Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honor, and glory, and blessing."* <note>original Greek: λέγοντες φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, Ἄξιόν ἐστι τὸ ἀρνίον τὸ ἐσφαγμένον λαβεῖν τὴν δύναμιν καὶ πλοῦτον καὶ σοφίαν καὶ ἰσχὺν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν καὶ εὐλογίαν</note>. Saying with a loud voice: Worthy is that slaughtered Lamb to receive **POWER** <note>original Hebrew: *Gedulah*—also meaning Greatness</note>, and riches, and **WISDOM** <note>original Hebrew: *Chokmah*</note>, and **MIGHT** <note>original Hebrew: *Gevurah*—representing divine strength</note>, and **honor** <note>original Hebrew: *Tiferet*—often translated as Beauty or Splendor</note>, and **glory** <note>original Hebrew: *Hod*—meaning Majesty</note>, and blessing. Likewise in verse 13: *And to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and might.* <note>original Greek: Καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ ἡ εὐλογία καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος</note>. Let us also add what the Apostle writes in the *Epistle to the Ephesians*, chapter 1, verses 20 and 21: *Whom* (Christ) *he seated at his right hand in the heavens, far above all principality and authority* <note>original Greek: ὑπεράνω πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας</note>—above all (**POWER**) — *and might* <note>original Greek: καὶ δυνάμεως</note>—(& **MIGHT**) — *and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the one to come.*

But since we have previously noted that Hebrew scholars interpret **Greatness** <note>Hebrew: *Gedulah*</note> as **Mercy** <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*—the attribute of loving-kindness</note>, and **Might** <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*</note> as severity, we can easily conjecture that they intended for **Greatness** to represent the right hand or the right arm, while **Might** represented the left side. The right hand, certainly, held the Scepter, the greatest sign of *Magnificence* and authority. But the left side is a sign of severity, rigor, and wrath. It seems to me that these things are best explained in the *Gospel of Saint Matthew*, chapter 25, verse 34: *And he will place the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.* <note>original Greek: Καὶ στήσει τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ, τὰ δὲ ἐρίφια ἐξ εὐωνύμων</note>.

Then, since the previous individual *Sephiroth* have so far corresponded most successfully to individual parts of the human body, this belt occurred to us naturally, since both the order seemed to demand it, and no other specific part of the body suggested itself; and at the same time, we understood a King to be described here—crowned, clothed, and holding a sceptre. To this was added the fact that no meaning is so fitting for the word **Tiferet** as that of the belt, which was of the greatest ornament and beauty to Oriental Kings. ...your **authority I will deliver into his hand** <note>original Latin: *Imperium tuum tradam in manum ejus*; a reference to Isaiah 22:21</note>. Kimchi <note>David Kimhi, a 12th-century Jewish rabbi and grammarian</note> explains this most excellently:

The tunic and the belt of magnificence are, therefore, <term>symbols</term> <note>original Greek: σύμβολα</note> of strength and rule. I have also observed another passage from *Job*, chapter 12:18: <gloss>original Hebrew: מוסר מלכים פתח ויאסר אזור במתניהם</gloss> **He loosens the bond [the belt] of kings, and binds a girdle to their loins.** This sentiment signifies nothing other than what Hannah, the mother of Samuel, sang in the first book of Samuel: namely, that the power belongs to God to create kings and, in turn, to cast them down from their throne according to His good pleasure. This is abundantly clear from the belts of the Hebrew Priests. They were <term>needlework</term> <note>original Hebrew: מעשה רקם; *ma’aseh roqem*</note>—*Phrygian work, embroidered work, or many-colored weaving* <note>original Latin: *Opus Phrygionicum, plumarium, aut polymitum*</note>, in French *brodé*, in Dutch **geboorduert** <note>embroidered</note> / just as the Learned Man interprets it. ...which I have brought forth to this end, so that the words of this song, <term>and your right hand shall teach you awesome things</term> <note>original Hebrew: וְתוֹרְךָ נוֹרָאוֹת יְמִינֶךָ (*ve-torekha nora'ot yeminekha*) from Psalm 45:4</note> might receive some light from this. These words can be understood as: *And your right hand, and whatever is on your right side, shall teach You terrible things.* Other points on this matter occur on page 103. Among the Romans, to be presented with a girdle and a belt was considered an honor. And for this reason, those who served in the military were called the "girded" (*cincti*), and conversely, those who had been dismissed were called the "ungirded" (*discincti*), having been stripped of their military service and deprived of their belt. <term>Isidore</term> <note>St. Isidore of Seville (c. 560–636), a scholar and bishop whose *Etymologies* served as an encyclopedia for the Middle Ages</note> says: *A belt is so named not only because it is what one is girded with, but also that from which weapons hang.* Furthermore, the belts of soldiers were highly decorated and precious, according to the rank of each individual. <term>Virgil</term> <note>The Roman epic poet; these lines are from the *Aeneid*, Book 12, describing the belt of Pallas stolen by Turnus, which leads to Turnus's death</note> writes in the twelfth book of the *Aeneid*:

> And now, even now, the speech had begun to move him
> as he hesitated more and more, when the unlucky belt 
> appeared high on the shoulder, and the strap flashed with the well-known studs.

<term>Pausanias</term> <note>A Greek traveler and geographer of the 2nd century AD</note> in his *Description of Greece (Boeotia)* says: <term>the ancients called putting on armor "to gird oneself"</term> <note>original Greek: τὸ δὲ ἐνδύναι τὰ ὅπλα ἐκάλουν οἱ πάλαιοι ζώסασθαι</note>. There are many instances of this kind. We may rightly conclude from them that the words of David just cited must be understood entirely in terms of the same *girding of the belt*, which it was our task to prove. For the thighs follow the loins. Let us examine the matter again.

The seventh <term>Sephira</term>, therefore, which is in the right thigh or leg, is called <term>Victory</term> <note>Hebrew: נצח (*Netzach*)</note>; the eighth, however, which is depicted in the left thigh, is <term>Majesty</term> <note>Hebrew: הוד (*Hod*)</note>. Also holding a **SCEPTRE** in his hand, as seen in verse 7: *The sceptre of equity is the sceptre of your kingdom* <note>original Hebrew: שֵׁבֶט מִישֹׁר שֵׁבֶט מַלְכוּתֶךָ (*shevet mishor shevet malkhutekha*)</note>. He is clothed in the most fragrant, that is, royal garments: *Myrrh, Aloes, and Cassia are all your garments* <note>original Hebrew: מֹר וַאֲהָלוֹת קְצִיעוֹת כָּל בִּגְדֹתֶיךָ (*mor va-ahalot ketzi'ot kol bigdotekha*)</note>.

And finally, which we now consider, he is **GIRDED WITH A BELT**. We gather this, moreover, from verse 4: **GIRD** *your sword* **UPON YOUR THIGH**, *o Mighty One* <note>original Hebrew: חֲגוֹר חַרְבְּךָ עַל יָרֵךְ גִּבּוֹר (*hagor harb'kha al yerekh gibbor*)</note>. For indeed, the *belt* had that use among the Ancients, so that *weapons* might hang from it, and especially the *sword*. This can be seen on ancient coins and marbles, as well as in those authors who described the military service of the Ancients. Look only at those figures which are in the commentary of <term>Godescalcus Stewechius</term> <note>A 16th-century Dutch scholar whose 1585 commentary on Vegetius provided detailed archaeological insights into Roman warfare</note> on the first book of <term>Vegetius</term> <note>A late Roman author whose manual *De Re Militari* was the primary source for medieval and Renaissance understanding of Roman military tactics</note>, pages 62, 63, and 64. His words, worthy of note in that same place, are these:

> From these figures I also observed that, during the era of the free Republic 
> and the flourishing Empire, the swords of the Romans were smaller and 
> worn on the right side; whereas as the Empire declined, the swords were 
> larger and hung on the left. This custom of carrying the sword on the left 
> remains to this day. Although many testimonies are available for this

> **HANGS AT THE RIGHT THIGH**; *they call it the Spanish sword;* 
> *it is double-edged, with an excellent point—*

...to the end, so that the words of this song, *And your right hand shall teach You awesome things* <note>original Hebrew: וְתוֹרְךָ נוֹרָאוֹת יְמִינֶךָ (*ve-torekha nora'ot yeminekha*); Psalm 45:4</note>, might receive some light from here. They can be understood in this way: *And your right hand—and whatever is on your right side—shall teach You awesome things.* Other examples of this occur on page 103. Among the Romans, to be presented with a <term>cingulum</term> <note>a military belt or girdle</note> and a <term>balteus</term> <note>a sword-belt or shoulder-strap</note> was bestowed as an honor. And hence: *those who served in the military were called the "girded" [cincti], and conversely, those who were discharged were called "ungirded" [discincti], as they were stripped of military service and deprived of the belt.* Isidore notes: *It is called a "balteus" [belt] not only because one is girded by it, but also because weapons hang from it.* Moreover, those belts of the soldiers were highly decorated and precious, according to the rank and dignity of each individual. Virgil writes in the twelfth book of the *Aeneid*:

> *And now the speech had begun to move him more and more as he hesitated, when the ill-fated, massive shoulder-belt appeared high on the shoulder, and the straps flashed with the well-known studs.*

Pausanias, in his *Description of Greece (Boeotia)*, writes: *The ancients called the putting on of arms "to be girded"* <note>original Greek: τὸ δὲ ἐνδύναι τὰ ὅπλα ἐκάλουν οἱ πάλαι ζώνεσθαι</note>. The ancients used the term "to be girded" for being clothed in armor. There are many examples of this kind. We have rightly concluded from these that the words of David just cited must be understood entirely as referring to that same girding of the *belt*, which it was our task to prove. But all these things will become even clearer if we explain the two following <term>Sephiroth</term> <note>The ten divine emanations in Kabbalistic tradition, which Vitringa uses here as symbolic categories for divine attributes</note>.

After the attribute of **Beauty** <note>original Hebrew: תפארת (*Tiferet*)</note>, there appear again two virtues which we assign to no part of the body more appropriately than the thigh, which we have already begun to discuss. For the thighs follow the loins. Let us examine the matter again.

The seventh Sephirah, therefore, which is located on the right thigh or leg, is called **Victory** <note>original Hebrew: נצח (*Netzach*)</note>; the eighth, however, which is depicted on the left thigh, is **Majesty** <note>original Hebrew: הוד (*Hod*)</note>. These terms, along with others now explained, appear in the first book of Chronicles, chapter 29, verse 11. David says: *Yours, O Lord, is the greatness...* <note>original Hebrew: לְךָ יהוה הַגְּדֻלָּה (*lekha Adonai ha-gedulah*)</note>

What, I ask, could we bring forward that is more manifest?

It is just the same, therefore, whether one ascribes the *highest Majesty* to someone or declares him to be the *Lord of Lords*. ...which authors call the **COVENANT**; certainly, the <note>original Greek: σαρκωσις (sarkōsis)</note> incarnation of the Son of God would never have taken place without it. Therefore, we repeat the conclusion just made: that this very concept was understood by the Ancient Kabbalists through the <term>Yesod (Foundation)</term> <note>original Hebrew: יסוד</note>, since they exhibit the truest *Foundation* of <term>Malkuth (Kingdom)</term> <note>original Hebrew: מלכות</note> and of its union with the higher Sephirot—that is, the union of the *Human Nature* with the *Divine*. We come now, therefore, to the exposition of the last *Sephirah*, <term>Malkuth</term>. For the last of the Sephirot is <term>Malkuth</term>, which signifies *Kingdom*, or <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>original Hebrew: שכינה</note>, which is to say, *dwelling*. For it must be known that the Kabbalists use these words interchangeably, and are accustomed to speak more frequently of the <term>Shekhinah</term> than of <term>Malkuth</term>. Our intention, then, is first to explain what the Ancient Hebrews understood by the <term>Shekhinah</term> and then to interpret the word <term>Malkuth</term>.

To the Ancient Jews, the <term>Shekhinah</term> was nothing other than that in which God *dwells*; for it is derived from the word *shakan* <note>original Hebrew: שכן</note>, meaning *to dwell*. Specifically, God had promised that he would *dwell* in the midst of the Israelites in Exodus 25:8:

> <note>original Hebrew: ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם</note> *And they shall make for me a Sanctuary, and I WILL DWELL in the midst of them*.

And in Leviticus 26:11:

> <note>original Hebrew: ונתתי משכני בתוכם</note> *And I will place my Tabernacle in the midst of them*.

Which indeed He brought to pass in some measure when He willed that the *cloud* and the *fire* be present with them day and night as a most certain testimony of His presence. But truly, the wisest of the Israelites did not believe that the Divine promise was satisfied by this *dwelling* which they experienced in the desert and afterwards in Canaan; rather, they were waiting for another more worthy and more excellent dwelling. For such is the amplitude of those sacred sayings, which God, most wise—

...all our teachers have been accustomed to speak in the same way regarding this argument. *You are not a lord in this matter: the DIVINE DWELLING (Shekhinah) and the HOLY SPIRIT are not with you, for you have judged me as guilty, and not as innocent.* <note>original Latin: *Non tu es Dominus in hac causa: Non est DIVINA HABITATIO (Schechina) & SPIRITUS SANCTUS apud Te, quod judicasti me tanquam culpabilem, non autem ut insontem.*</note> Where those two terms signify one and the same thing.

There are many other points by which we could confirm this, but it is better to come to the matter itself, and to undertake the resolution of the point which is chiefly debated. Namely, there is a very ancient tradition of the Ancient Hebrews, which we encounter everywhere in their writings, that five things were missing in the Second Temple <note>The temple rebuilt in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, which lacked the supernatural artifacts of Solomon's original temple.</note> which the first had enjoyed. We therefore set one *Gemara* against another *Gemara*, and follow the most constant tradition of the Hebrews, which called the Holy Spirit the *Shekhinah*.

When God led the descendants of Abraham out of Egypt into a desert place, He offered Himself to be seen by them day and night in a *pillar of cloud and fire*, lest that people, not noticing an external sign of the Divine presence, should either wander aimlessly in the desert or distrust Moses and the other ministers sent by God as His legates. For they were a very uncultivated and unrefined people.

From this, whenever that pillar moved, the Israelites understood that they also had to move from that place; and when it rested in a certain place, they also stayed and camped in that same spot. 

And this sign of the Divine presence remained with this people until they were led into the land of the Canaanites, which had been promised to their ancestors by a sworn oath. This is indeed a most worthy testimony for us to explain. To be sure, the whole difficulty seems to me to lie in the word *era’eh* <note>original Hebrew: אראה</note>, whose true force and significance must be uncovered here. Certainly, nothing is more frequent among the Hebrews than that the root *ra’ah* <note>original Hebrew: ראה</note> has the meaning "to see," and it is used constantly in that sense in the Holy Scriptures. The passive form, therefore, means "to be seen" or "to appear." 

But truly, this passive meaning is sometimes so turned in the Hebrew idiom that it does not indicate the *appearance of that person* who is being spoken of (as it seems to signify at first glance), but rather the *appearance of others before him*. I shall fail my case unless I prove this with clear evidence. An excellent passage exists in the second book of Moses <note>The Book of Exodus</note>, chapter

...which would cover the <term>Mercy Seat<note>original Greek: ἱλαστήριον (*hilastērion*)</note></term>, lest he die; this is the same cloud mentioned at the beginning of this chapter. ### SACRED OBSERVATIONS

[Boe]theus, <note>Vitringa likely refers to Boethus, who along with Sadok is traditionally cited as a student of Antigonus of Socho.</note> among whose disciples and followers was *Sadokus*, from whom came the *Sadducees*, according to the *Avoth* <note>The Pirkei Avoth, or "Ethics of the Fathers."</note> chapter 1, section 3: **Antigonus of Socho received the tradition from Simeon the Just. He used to say: Do not be like servants who serve the Master on the condition of receiving a** **REWARD** (פרס); <note>original Hebrew: peras; original Latin: MERCEDEM</note> **but be like servants who serve the Master on the condition of not receiving a reward, and let the fear of Heaven be upon you.** <note>original Hebrew: אנטיגנוס איש סוכו קבל משמעון הצדיק...; original Latin: Antigonus vir Socho accepit a Simeone iusto...</note> Thus far the words of *Antigonus of Socho*, who handed down this same maxim to his disciples and listeners, who took the opportunity from this to forge their own opinions. <note>According to tradition, Sadok and Boethus misinterpreted this to mean there is no reward after death, leading to their denial of the resurrection.</note>

Moreover, *peras* <note>פרס</note> is nothing other than **recompense** <note>original Greek: μισθαποδοσία (misthapodosia)</note>, the retribution of a prize, which is the word the Apostle Paul uses in the Epistle to the *Hebrews*, chapter 11:26, when speaking of *Moses*: **He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures in Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.** <note>original Greek: ἀπέβλεπε γὰρ εἰς τὴν μισθαποδοσίαν</note> I clearly believe that the Apostle Paul was looking back to this very word *peras*, which carried the same force and emphasis. For the Apostle was a **Pharisee**, <note>original Greek/Hebrew mix: Φαריסאיος</note> as he himself declares.

Furthermore, he wrote this Epistle to the *Hebrews*, of whom it is established from all history that the largest and most noble part were devoted to the Pharisees. Therefore, it served to convince the minds of those men if they recognized that he had not changed his own ancient viewpoint. Indeed, it seems to me the Apostle did this with deliberate purpose.
