# C. VITRINGA
<page-num>302</page-num>
<header>CAMPEGIUS VITRINGA</header>

...they do not seem to me to have attained the genuine sense of these words. They advise, however, that the particle <note>original Greek: $\delta \iota \alpha^{\prime}$ (*dia*)</note> most often signifies *through*. Thus, in the Notes to No. 18: **"Or / through his glory and virtue. But the Greek word** <note>original Greek: $\delta \iota \alpha^{\prime}$ (*dia*)</note> **does not always mean 'through,' but also sometimes 'to'."** <note>Vitringa is quoting a Dutch commentary here: *Ofte / door sijne heerlijckheyt ende deught Doch het Griex woort dia beteeckent niet altijt door, maer oock somtijts tot.*</note> Romans 6:4. These points are taken from the Venerable Beza <note>Theodore Beza (1519–1605), a successor to John Calvin and a major biblical scholar</note>, who noted this same passage and entirely believes that <note>original Greek: $\tau \grave{o}$ $\delta \iota \alpha^{\prime}$ (*to dia*)</note> sometimes signifies *to* or *toward*. This can be seen in his own major annotations. We, however, are of the opposite opinion, and judge that both passages ought to be restored <note>re-evaluated or corrected in their interpretation</note>.

To make this more convenient, it must be entirely noted that the particle <note>original Greek: $\delta \iota \alpha^{\prime}$ (*dia*)</note>, when used with the genitive case in the sacred Codex of the New Testament, corresponds to the <term>Hebrew Letter Beth (ב)</term>, which matches the prepositions *in, through, concerning, with*, but never signifies *to*, so far as we know. And we shall note this indeed for the illustration of certain passages: Romans 11:36: *For from him and through him* <gloss>original Hebrew: ב בו (*be bo*), meaning "in/through him"</gloss> *and to him are all things.* Hebrews 2:10: *For it was fitting for him, for whom are all things and through whom* <note>original Greek: δι' οὗ (*di’ hou*)</note> *are all things.* *Through whom all things.* <note>original Latin: *Per quem omnia*</note> Which in Hebrew we would say: *Through God we act valiantly.* <gloss>original Hebrew: באלהים נעשה חיל (*be-Elohim na'aseh chayil*)</gloss> Thus: *the one in whom [or through whom] all things are.* <gloss>original Hebrew: אשר בו הכל (*asher bo hakol*)</gloss>

But since the <term>Beth (ב)</term> signifies not only *through*, but also *in*, it follows that the Greek word <note>original Greek: $\delta \iota \alpha^{\prime}$ (*dia*)</note> also acquires this meaning, which otherwise seems in some way to be at odds with its natural Greek usage. A passage exists in Paul’s Epistle to the Romans, chapter 4:11: *So that he might be the Father of all those who believe* <note>original Greek: $\delta \iota'$ ἀκροβυστίας (*di’ akrobystias*)</note> *while uncircumcised.* *That he might be* (Abraham) *the Parent of all those who believe* IN UNCIRCUMCISION, i.e., *those not circumcised.* And for the same reason, the Venerable Beza very well transposed the passage of the Apostle which is in the Epistle to Timothy—

in the former [letter], chapter 2:15: *She shall be saved through childbearing.* <note>original Greek: Σωθήσεται δὲ διὰ τῆς τεκνογονίας (*Sōthēsetai de dia tēs teknogonias*)</note>. But in reporting this version, we cannot help but remember that difficulty which spontaneously presents itself to those who do not have a clear perspective on the <term>emphasis</term> <note>original Greek: $\varepsilon^{\prime}\mu \phi \alpha \sigma \iota \nu$ (*emphasin*); refers to the rhetorical force or underlying weight of a word</note> of these words. ->C. VITRINGA<-

...is sought, and <term>virtue</term> <note>original Greek: ἀρετή (*aretē*)</note> corresponds as closely as possible to the Hebrew <term>Hod</term> <note>original Hebrew: הוד (*hod*); typically translated as majesty, splendor, or vigor</note>. From this we conclude that the word <term>virtue</term> is quite correctly applied in this passage, even though it was certainly a point of hesitation for many interpreters. *Theodore Beza <note>A prominent 16th-century French Protestant theologian and scholar</note> states in express words: "Furthermore, everyone sees how much better the name of <term>virtue</term> <note>original Greek: τῆς ἀρετῆς (*tēs aretēs*)</note> suits men than God, to whom <term>power</term> <note>original Greek: δύναμις (*dynamis*)</note>—that is, potency or authority—or <term>might</term> <note>original Greek: κράτος (*kratos*)</note>—that is, strength—is rather attributed. For here, <term>virtue</term> <note>original Greek: ἀρετή</note> denotes to us nothing other than a royal VIGOR, full of majesty."* Indeed, the **Venerable Beza** himself remarked that *Peter*, in the second chapter, ninth verse of his previous Epistle, expressly ascribes <term>virtues</term> <note>original Greek: ἀρετάς (*aretas*)</note> to God. The words are as follows: *...that you may declare the virtues of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.* <note>original Greek: ὅπως τὰς ἀρετὰς ἐξαγγείλητε τοῦ ἐκ σκότους ὑμᾶς καλέσαντος εἰς τὸ θαυμαστὸν αὐτοῦ φῶς (1 Peter 2:9)</note>. For there the Apostle Peter also discusses our *vocation* <note>The divine "calling" of believers</note>, and in that context, he says God exercised *his virtues*, exactly as in this passage of ours. This manner of speaking also agrees with the meaning of the word <term>virtue</term> <note>original Greek: ἀρετή</note> as assigned to it by those who were thoroughly skilled in the Greek language. *Hesychius* <note>An Alexandrian grammarian and lexicographer, likely of the 5th century, who compiled a famous dictionary of rare Greek words</note>, who alone is a sufficient authority, interprets <term>virtue</term> <note>original Greek: ἀρετή</note> as <term>divine power</term> <note>original Greek: τὴν θείαν δύναμιν (*tēn theian dynamin*)</note>.

The doubt which seemed to arise from the word <term>virtue</term> <note>original Greek: ἀρετή</note> could be seen as removed in this way, and our interpretation would not be so readily rejected, were it not for the addition of the word <term>glory</term> <note>original Greek: δόξα (*doxa*)</note>, which seems entirely out of place. *For what does this mean, if you say: He called us through glory?* Such expressions do not seem customary in the Sacred Codex <note>The Bible</note>. This we do, in some measure, concede. But we advise that one must look here to the construction, which is very familiar to the Hebrews, not only in this word but in many others as well. Vi-

### SACRED OBSERVATIONS

...namely, two substantives, whether synonymous or distinct in meaning, are sometimes joined together, and one of them takes the place of an adjective, holding its meaning with emphasis. This mode of speaking is called **Hendiadys** <note>original Greek: ἓν διὰ δυοῖν (*hen dia dyoin*); literally "one through two," a figure of speech where two words joined by "and" express a single complex idea</note>. This rule is found in the most learned **Glassius**, *Sacred Philology, book III, Tract 1, Canon VI, page 27* <note>Salomon Glassius (1593–1656) was a German theologian and biblical critic whose "Philologia sacra" was a standard reference for linguistic analysis of the Bible</note>. The various examples subjoined to it are as follows:

*Jeremiah 22:3*: Thus said the Lord, do **judgment and justice** <note>original Hebrew: משפט וצדקה (*mishpat u-tsedakah*)</note>, *that is, just judgment.*
*Job 4:16*: **I heard silence and a voice** <note>original Hebrew: דממה וקול (*demamah ve-kol*)</note>, *that is, a low voice, or one arisen from deep silence.*
*Jeremiah 29:11*: **To give us an end and expectation** <note>original Hebrew: אחרית ותקוה (*acharit ve-tikvah*)</note>, *that is, an expected end.*
*Job 10:17*: **Changes and armies are against me** <note>original Hebrew: חליפות וצבא (*chalipot ve-tsava*)</note>, *that is, those who go and return in turns <note>referring to successive waves of affliction or alternating shifts of soldiers</note>.*
*Acts 14:13*: **bulls and garlands** <note>original Greek: ταύρους καὶ στέμματα (*taurous kai stemmata*)</note>, *that is, crowned bulls.*

While I was occupied in describing these examples, I finally came, quite unknowingly, to our present passage—the very reason I had sought out these references in our **Glassius**—and I noticed that **Glassius** entirely corresponds to our earlier thoughts, even though I was previously unaware of it. I rejoice in this now, however, because I am all the more confirmed in the truth. Thus, he writes: *Who called us **through glory and virtue** <note>2 Peter 1:3; original Greek: διὰ δόξης καὶ ἀρετῆς (*dia doxēs kai aretēs*)</note>, that is, through glorious virtue and power.* For <term>virtue</term> <note>original Greek: ἀρετή (*aretē*)</note> in God is the same as <term>divine power</term> <note>original Greek: θεία δύναμις (*theia dynamis*)</note>, as **Hesychius** <note>An influential 5th-century Greek grammarian who compiled a dictionary of difficult or rare Greek words</note> says; and thus in *Zechariah 6:13*, it is used for the Hebrew **Hod** <note>original Hebrew: הוד (*hod*); signifying majesty, splendor, or vigor</note>. Because I see the most learned **Glassius** has noted this here, I cannot doubt that others have thought the same. For it often happens to this man of letters that he reviews the opinions of others himself, even if he does not approve them by his own reckoning. I clearly think...

...sage, this place must be translated in this way: *Who called us through His glorious power*. That is, He who gave a proof of His glorious majesty and exercised a truly divine power in calling us. In Dutch: *Through faith in Him, who has called us through His very glorious (Divine and Royal) power.* If these matters are understood in this way, how elegantly they agree with those expressions which the sacred writers have used in similar cases! Let us only attend to that which is found in Paul’s Epistle to the Ephesians, chapter 1:18–19:

->...so that you may know what is the surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of His mighty strength which He worked in Christ, raising Him from the dead. <note>original Greek: εἰς τὸ εἰδέναι ὑμᾶς τί τὸ ὑπερβάλλον μέγεθος τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ εἰς ἡμᾶς τοὺς πιστεύοντας κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ κράτους τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ. ἣν ἐνήργησεν ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ, ἐγείρας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.</note><-

And in this same way, the word **glory** <note>original Hebrew: כבוד (*kavod*)</note> is sometimes used in other places. Let us note that which is in Psalm 63:3: **To see your strength and your glory** <note>original Hebrew: לראות עוזך וכבודך (*li-rot ozka u-kvodeka*)</note>; that is, your most glorious strength. In Dutch: *Your very glorious strength*. And with the word **splendor** or **beauty** <note>original Hebrew: תפארת (*tipheret*)</note> in Psalm 89:18: **For you are the glory of their strength** <note>original Hebrew: כי תפארת עזמו אתה (*ki tipheret ozmo atah*)</note>; that is, their most glorious strength.

Let us add that which is in Mark, chapter 13:26: **they shall see the Son of Man coming with great power and glory** <note>original Greek: ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον μετὰ δυνάμεως πολλῆς καὶ δόξης</note>. Coming with **MUCH POWER** and **GLORY**, that is, with His most glorious power. Since, moreover, the joining of these two words is so frequent, it is no wonder if one is sometimes omitted, and these two meanings are included in the other alone. And from this it happens that the word **glory** <note>original Hebrew: כבוד (*kavod*)</note>, if it occurs alone, sometimes signifies not only glory, but also most glorious virtue and power. There is an elegant passage in Psalm 24:8 <note>Vitringa uses the term "Canticum" (Song), referring to the Psalm</note>.

<meta>This page is a formal dedication to Gerebrand Anslo. The author describes a traumatic event—a pirate attack—that occurred while he was traveling to have his work published, and how Anslo's generosity and library helped him recover his lost research.</meta>

<sig>* 2</sig>

## To the Most Learned and Distinguished Man,
# GEREBRAND ANSLO.

It seemed fitting, Most Learned Man, to inscribe your name upon this book, which I was the first to translate from Hebrew into Latin and illustrate with my own notes. What impelled me to do this was your own erudition and virtue. The former is memorable for your knowledge of many excellent things, and especially for your rare understanding of Oriental <note>In this period, "Oriental" referred primarily to Semitic languages like Hebrew, Arabic, Aramaic, and Syriac.</note> literature; the latter is evidenced by your extraordinary generosity and munificence toward those who are either skilled in those studies or lovers of them. 

When you learned that I was among that number—though I had hardly been seen by you, and certainly was hardly known—you immediately embraced me with that same benevolence with which you are accustomed to support all those by whose help and industry you believe these literary studies can be promoted. For when I was hurrying here from our Academy <note>Likely referring to a university such as Leiden or Franeker.</note> after a long and difficult voyage, intending to see to the printing of this and other books I had prepared for publication, behold: in the middle of the journey, a band of pirates suddenly descended. They invaded, captured, struck, and plundered us. Having fiercely broken open my trunks, they tore up and scattered my books and my labors; I myself barely escaped unharmed from such a ruin of my possessions. 

Here, as soon as you understood that I had arrived—sorrowful in spirit, lacking a plan, and destitute of means from such a bitter calamity—you sustained me with your conversation, helped me with your advice, and cherished me with your generosity. And, what is alone worth an immortal benefit, you opened to me the most precious Treasure of your most beautiful library. You even offered it of your own accord for me to use and enjoy as I saw fit, obeying not a desire for fame or glory as others are wont to do, but only your own beneficent nature. 

I cannot recall your most profuse humanity and the so many timely benefits bestowed upon me without being forced at the same time to remember my own good fortune. By your generosity alone, and from the abundance of your well-furnished library, I was able to repair in great part the loss which this ill-omened journey had inflicted upon me—after all my books and my scholarly works <note>original: "lucubrationibus," referring to studies or writings produced by lamplight late at night.</note> had been snatched and plundered. Thus, if the world of letters can hope for any fruit from this labor of mine, such as it is, that entire [fruit belongs] to your [libe]-

<meta>catchword: -rality [ralitati]</meta>

<summary>In this dedication, the author thanks his patron, Gerebrand Anslo, for providing him with financial aid and access to a private library after pirates destroyed his original manuscripts during a sea voyage. The text highlights the risks of 17th-century travel and the vital role of wealthy patrons in preserving scholarship.</summary>

<keywords>Gerebrand Anslo, dedication, pirate attack, Hebrew scholarship, patronage, private libraries, book history, Oriental studies</keywords>

--- Page 386 ---
<meta>This page continues the dedication to Gerebrand Anslo. The previous page ended with the author describing how Anslo helped him after he was robbed by pirates. This page concludes with a tribute to Anslo’s patronage and a formal signature.</meta>

...generosity <note>original: "liberalitati," completing the word from the previous page</note> that I must acknowledge: you, who indeed spare no effort and no expense, provided that you can promote the public good of the literary world. To build a most wealthy library at immense cost—for the use of the learned even more than for your own—and to liberally foster brilliant minds born for the public good, was once the glory of Princes; now that glory is yours alone as a private citizen. Allow me, I pray, most excellent patron <note>original: "Meccænas," a reference to Gaius Maecenas, the famous patron of the Roman poets Horace and Virgil</note>, while I admire and love your virtues, to at least lightly taste of their praises here in passing—praises which your modesty usually admits only reluctantly—though they deserve to be spoken with a full voice elsewhere. May you be honored for that generous spirit, great Man, by which you deserve to be eternally remembered through these Divine favors, not only by us, but by all posterity. Future generations will surely know that there once lived among the Dutch <note>original: "Batavis"</note> a Man whom those who knew him could not value enough, and those who did not value him never truly knew him. But I restrain myself and cease, offering only this one prayer which we all desire with our whole heart: that He who gave it may preserve and increase for you that spirit born for promoting the common good. Farewell, my protection and sweet glory <note>original: "præsidium & dulce decus meum," a famous quotation from the poet Horace addressing his own patron</note>, and receive this literary gift—rightly owed to your virtues—with a countenance as kind as the grateful spirit with which it is offered to you.

Given at *Amsterdam*,
The day after the Nones of July <note>July 8th</note>
1642.

->A great admirer of your<-
->virtues,<-

->**JOHANN STEPHAN RITTANGEL** Professor of Oriental Languages at the Electoral Academy of Königsberg <note>original: "Regiomontana"</note>.<-

**A**nd who is **RITTANGEL** <note>Johann Stephan Rittangel (1606–1652) was a scholar of Oriental languages and a convert from Judaism to Christianity who specialized in translating Jewish mystical and legal texts.</note> that he should speak before the magnificent figures of his age and the leaders of his people’s assembly? Truly, though I have now crossed the boundaries of the inner chambers of my own thoughts, and set my face like flint, and placed my head among the heads of the lofty mountains, and approached a place where the strength of my meager knowledge does not reach; my faithful witness is in the highest heavens that I did not do this to display magnificence or sharpness of wit, but rather to find grace in the sight of God and men. For I am the least of all among those who pour water—I will not say over the hands, but rather over the feet—of those who know the knowledge of the holy ones. From my infancy, I have striven with all my might <margin>a To sprinkle myself with dust.</margin> <sup>a</sup> to cover myself in the dust of the feet of the Wise, who have been men of renown <note>original: "Viri nominis," a Latin rendering of the Hebrew "Anshei HaShem," referring to famous or legendary figures.</note> from ages past. And now, who will lift up Rittangel, since he is the least among thousands of the Wise? None but the "men of my peace" <note>A biblical idiom for close, trusted friends.</note>, who with their persistent prayers (to which was added the order and command of the honored men and leaders of our land, whom I judge it always beautiful and most just to obey) insisted that I bring to public light certain very firm foundations of our faith, like fortified bulwarks against every kind of assault attacking our true religion. Since, however, on this journey of mine, whatever useful material had been written for this purpose was lost; lest I return and appear entirely empty-handed before them, I have [joined] to the body of the book

And who is RITTANGELIUS <note>John Stephen Rittangel (1606–1652) was a professor of Oriental languages at Königsberg. Lest therefore <gloss>their beauties seem unbeautiful</gloss> their richness seem meager, and their desirable things despised, and so that no deception of mine reaches you, I have translated everything word for word. I have followed the elegance of the Hebrew speech, observing the sequence of individual words and letters, so that the intention of the Authors might not be changed. And in certain places where the Latin language did not offer itself as I wished and as it was spoken in the Hebrew tongue, it was necessary at times to coin <gloss>barbarous</gloss> foreign words: For it is a task of the heaviest labor, as is known to every wise heart, to transfer each and every thing from one language into another; they are also difficult to understand because of the difficulty of translation. For that reason, because the translator expresses the words of the book as it seemed best to him, I also wished to preserve the words and order of the Authors to benefit students of the Hebrew language. <column-break/>

in the pages of my translation, it has happened that I have hardly been able to explain many things, even with the greatest difficulty, according to the proper manner and character of the Latin language. And this is because I, the translator, <gloss>I was forced to follow in their footsteps</gloss> was led by the aforementioned languages <note>referring to Hebrew and Aramaic mentioned on the previous page</note>. The words which occur in this book that do not have a literal meaning but instead signify some unique mystery, I have rendered in **UPPERCASE**; the words of the ancient Authors, which are cited and explained by more recent ones, I have rendered in **lowercase**; as I have also done for passages of Scripture along with my own observations; everything else is in the usual typeface. And now, kind Reader, please accept this gift of mine, which is offered to you with a good heart and a willing mind; though small in quantity, it is yet great in quality. And since there is no perfection except for that **TRUE & SUPREME PERFECTION**; please cover my deficiency with the cloak of my good intentions, and you shall have your wish. Farewell.

<column-break/>

<note>This column contains a Hebrew translation of the Latin text provided in the first column, following the common scholarly practice of providing parallel texts in bilingual editions.</note>

It is a thing well known to every wise person regarding all the holy things that have been translated from one language to another, that the burden and distance of the translation is seen as a lack of grace and a source of few results. Thus I too, the translator, have followed after the aforementioned languages. The words that are very powerful, which point to the crowns of exalted secrets, were set in **LARGE LETTERS**; and the words of the ancients which are explained by the later ones in **small letters**, as well as some places from the Scripture. After all these matters are in their order: And now, wise reader, please do not [refuse] my offering which is brought to you with a good heart and a willing soul, even though the quantity is small, the quality is great. And because there is no perfection except for the **True and Supreme** [Perfection], please cover my deficiency with the cloak of my intention <note>original: "כמעיל רצוני" (ke-me'il retzoni), literally "like the cloak of my will/desire"</note> so that your own desire may be fulfilled.

->Rabbi Abraham ben David says:<-

The first path is called the Wonderful or Hidden Intelligence, that is, derived from the phrase <term>כי יפלא ממך דבר</term> <note>original: *Ki yippale mimmeka dabar*</note> *If a matter be too hidden for you*, Deuteronomy chapter 17, verse 8 <note>The Latin text cites verse 5, though the phrase appears in verse 8</note>. This the Chaldee <note>The Aramaic translation, or Targum</note> rendered as <term>ארי יתכסי</term> <note>original: *ari yitkassi*</note> (which means the same thing, namely: "if it shall be hidden"): as if he were to say, the Hidden Intelligence is concealed and secret from all things that are outside of it. For just as the <term>Cause of Causes</term> <note>God, as the ultimate source of all existence</note> is not grasped by any besides itself; so also the Wonderful or Hidden Intelligence is concealed from all that are outside of it. And in this lies a mystery: for it is known that the form of the letter <term>Aleph</term> <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet: <term>אלף</term></note> is the form of all letters, and all the paths are within it, but in a universal manner. Therefore, the letters of the word <term>Pele</term> <note>meaning 'Wonder': <term>פלא</term></note> are also the same letters as the word <term>Aleph</term>, though in a reversed order. And for this reason, the first path is called <term>Pele</term> (Wonderful or Hidden) according to what the Scripture says in Isaiah chapter 9, verse 6: *And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God...*

<column-break/>

# THE FIRST PATH
It is called the Wonderful Intelligence (The Supreme Crown), and it is the primordial intellectual light, and it is the First Glory, the existence of which no creature (is able) to withstand or fully grasp.

## The RaBaD <note>Acronym for Rabbi Abraham ben David</note> says:
The First Path is called the Wonderful Intelligence, explained by the language of the phrase *If a matter be too hidden from you*, which the translation <note>The Targum</note> renders as *it shall be covered*. It is as if one said: an intelligence that is hidden, covered, and secret from all that is external to it. And just as the Cause of Causes cannot be attained by anything outside of itself, so the Wonderful Intelligence is hidden from the attainment of anything besides it. The secret in this is that it is known that the form of the letter Aleph is the form of all the letters, and all the paths are in it, albeit in a general way. Therefore, "Pele" [Wonder] contains the letters of "Aleph." Thus the First Path is called "Pele" as it is said: *And his name shall be called Wonder, Counselor, Mighty God*. And this path is called the Intellect of the Cause of Causes, because it does not depart from its high degree and its necessity. And it is called Primordial, because it is prior in all degrees to everything else.

As the Scripture says in Isaiah, chapter 40, verse 5* <note>The quote "To whom will you liken me?" actually appears in Isaiah 40:18 and 40:25, though the author cites verse 5</note>: *To whom will you liken me, etc. For there is absolutely no similarity of shape or substance between us and* HIM; *but only a certain, as it were, intention of the members. Indeed, our members, which are improperly attributed to* GOD, *are nothing but signs of the highest, hidden, and most deeply concealed things, which are incomprehensible to the human mind. Therefore, beware of thinking that the* NUMERATIONS, *or modes of existence, undergo any of the human measures except in name only. For just as the hands, feet, eyes, ears, face, heart, mouth, and soul; so also the intention of the* NUMERATIONS, *as we said above, represents neither a limit, nor a mass, nor a continuous or discrete quantity, nor a quality; but an example or a thin likeness. <meta>This page continues the preface by Johann Stephan Rittangel, transitioning from the symbolic language of Scripture to the specific Kabbalistic structure of the ten "Numerations" (Sephiroth), particularly focusing on the relationship between the higher intellectual triad and the lower seven attributes.</meta>

*although the power of Holy Scripture sets the truth of the* **MOST HIGH** *before our eyes through the mouth, heart, soul, hands, feet, right hand, and so forth; nevertheless, what those things that are said about* **God** *actually are in* **God** *and what they signify, no creature is able to sufficiently define. Therefore, they have established that there are ten* **NUMERATIONS** <note>original Latin: *Numerationes*; a translation of the Hebrew *Sephiroth*, the ten creative powers or attributes of God in Kabbalah</note> *in* **God**, *the seven lower of which are called* *Middot* <note>original Hebrew: מדות; literally "measures," referring to the divine attributes or qualities</note> *(properties or attributes); which are* **MAGNIFICENCE** *or* **MERCY**, **STRENGTH** *or* **SEVERITY**, **BEAUTY** *or* **ORNAMENT**, **VICTORY** *or* **ETERNITY**, **GLORY**, **FOUNDATION**, *and* **KINGDOM**. *Indeed, the remaining three superior* **NUMERATIONS** *are called spiritual or intellectual, and they established that these are, as it were, the* **SPIRIT**, **BREATH**, *and* **SOUL** *to those seven lower* **NUMERATIONS** *mentioned above: through which those three superior, spiritual or intellectual ones operate, just as the soul operates through the members of its body. From this it is first manifest that both the ancient and more recent Hebrew theologians, by the unanimous consensus of their assembly, took this liberty for themselves—not only out of the greatest necessity but also from notable utility—to wrap the matter contained in the sacred writings in certain titles and terms, and to use them in explaining mysteries, so that they might express the matter denoted by the terms with significance, and expose the ambiguities and frauds of heretics, who are accustomed to mimic the sense and phrases of Holy Scripture. I also think it is clear without a doubt to all and singular who are devoted to the sacred page, that the most ancient and learned Hebrew theologians since the time of Abraham (as the books of more recent Hebrews testify) established, cherished, and adored three primordial modes of existing—or rather, according to the better significance of the Hebrew word* **NUMERATIONS**, **EMANATIONS** *or* **PROCESSIONS** *(the first of which they called the* **HIGHEST CROWN**, *the second* **PRIMORDIAL WISDOM**, *equal in all things and coeternal to the* **HIGHEST CROWN**, *and the third* **UNDERSTANDING**) *and that their coeternal splendor, the most brilliant of all brilliant things, goes forth from the very self-ness* <note>original Latin: *ipseitas*; a philosophical term for the essential nature of the "self"</note> *of the Deity, and from the inaccessible abyss of the fountain-light of infinity, yet in such a way that nothing is understood to emanate or proceed from it by which this most brilliant splendor of the Deity might be spread thin or poured out, or its ungraspable infinity diminished. And [they established] that those three* **NUMERATIONS**, **Emanations**, *or* **Modes of Existing**, *are in a* **Unity** *that is most singular and perfect, nor do they suffer any division in themselves; although by reason of their procession one is distinguished from the other in its order as either inferior or superior, even though any of these in itself cannot be measured or circumscribed in the least. Therefore, the first of these, which is treated in this* **Path**, *is called the* **HIGHEST CROWN**. *And for this reason its shrine is also called "admirable" or "hidden," because in the contemplation of this, the eyes of all minds grow dark, tongues are struck dumb, every voice falls silent, and the spirit fails, on account of its inscrutable depth: for it has this peculiar and proper quality, that all* **NUMERATIONS** *proceed from it, but it proceeds from none: And it is understood within the three superior* **NUMERATIONS**, *which our theologians have called* **PERSONS** <note>Rittangel here links the top three Sephiroth—Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah—to the Christian concept of the Trinity</note>, *each of which, as we have said, is incomprehensible according to its essence, but not according to its emanation.*

<summary>Rittangel explains the Kabbalistic structure of the ten Sephiroth, dividing them into three intellectual "spiritual" emanations and seven "lower" attributes. He argues that ancient Hebrew theologians used these terms to protect sacred mysteries from heretical distortion and equates the highest triad with the Christian Trinity.</summary>

The Second Path is called the Illuminating Intelligence and it is the crown of creation and the splendor of the equal unity, etc. Know that Non-Being <note>original Hebrew: האין; *Ayin*, "the Nothing"</note> (referring to the Crown) is not subject to number—neither the number of unity nor the number of plurality. ...is never severed or divided from the **HIGHEST CROWN** <note>original: *CORONA SVMMA*, referring to the Sephirah *Keter*</note>, as well as from **UNDERSTANDING** <note>original: *INTELLIGENTIA*, referring to the Sephirah *Binah*</note>, nor from **WISDOM** <note>original: *SAPIENTIA*, referring to the Sephirah *Chokhmah*</note>, nor from the **HIGHEST CROWN** by any truncation or division.

It should further be noted that, since besides these three preceding ones, all the subsequent paths also go by the name of "Intelligences," this has occurred due to the poverty of the Latin language. Among the Hebrews, the words *Sekhel* <note>original: שכל, often translated as 'Intellect' or 'Consciousness'</note> and *Binah* <note>original: בינה, usually translated as 'Understanding'</note> are distinct. The first, *Binah*, refers to the third hypostatic **ENUMERATION** <term>Numeratio: The author uses this Latin term to describe the *Sephirot*, the ten creative powers or attributes of God in Kabbalah</term> in the order of the Sacrosanct **TRINITY** <note>The author is likely interpreting the top three Sephirot through a Christian Kabbalistic lens as a Trinity</note>. The other, namely *Sekhel*, only denotes divine attributes at certain times. However, we have had to render both as **INTELLIGENCE**, since another word that might conveniently express *Sekhel* did not occur to us. I have deemed it necessary to warn the reader of this here once and for all.

(b) **TIFERET** <note>Hebrew: תפארת</note> (**BEAUTY**:) To this **ENUMERATION**, which is the sixth in order, is attributed the name **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHVH, considered too sacred to pronounce</note>. This is because the name Tetragrammaton alone uses all the names and surnames of the **ENUMERATIONS** like a garment; from the ornament of their connection, **BEAUTY** itself emerges, with which the Tetragrammaton is decorated. Some of these names and surnames stand on the left, like attendants and accusers, while others stand on the right like guardians and supporters of the name Tetragrammaton, which is always placed in the middle.

(c) **ATARET** <note>Hebrew: עטרת</note> (**DIADEM or LOWER CROWN**) This Enumeration, when we begin from the higher and tend downward, holds the last rank among all the **ENUMERATIONS** and attributes. This is because it is the consummation of union in the Archetypal or divine world, and the mystery of His kingdom: for it has the power of reigning over all creatures. For this reason, it is also surnamed **MALKHUT** <note>Hebrew: מלכות</note>, which means **KINGDOM**, because through it the King, the Tetragrammaton, performs all His duties. And this **ENUMERATION** is closest to all created things; through it, access is given to them to the Tetragrammaton, whose peculiar name—the name of the Supreme King and highest Architect upon whom all things in this universe depend—signifies existence. And to this **ENUMERATION**, namely the **DIADEM**, is attributed the name **ADONAI** <note>Hebrew: אדני</note> (which denotes Lordship). It is believed to be the president and ruler of the whole circuit of the earth, because the name Tetragrammaton confers every abundance of influence upon the name Adonai; and in it, as if into one, the most opulent goods of the King converge. From there they are further transmitted, to fulfill whatever the necessity of the Creator demands: for it stands as a treasury and a storehouse of riches, and to that name, Adonai, torrents of blessings and the down-flowings of His immense goodness are applied from the Tetragrammaton.

To this **ENUMERATION** is also adapted the surname **OHEL MOED** <note>Hebrew: אהל מועד</note> (**The Tent of Meeting**); a term by which it is called in many places by the Hebrews. For through it, as through a channel, the influence of every kind of goodness collected from all the superior **ENUMERATIONS** is derived into all universal beings.

<meta>This page continues the technical description of the divine emanations (Sephirot), transitioning from the previous discussion of "Intelligence" and "Beauty" into the specific functions of "Severity" and the final "Enumeration," often known as the Kingdom (Malkhut).</meta>

...By the **ENUMERATION** <term>Numeratio: The author uses this Latin term for the *Sephirot*, the ten divine attributes or powers in Kabbalah</term> indeed of **SEVERITY** or **FORTITUDE** <note>original: *SEVERITATIS* and *FORTITVDINIS*, referring to the Sephirah *Gevurah*</note>, when an inundation flows forth, it carries out judgment unto death or life, unto famine or plenty, and peace or war. For this power, having received its character from the **ENUMERATION** of Severity, administers all the judgments of this world and carries out the battles of the **MOST HIGH**. For this reason, the Hebrews assert that sixty "mighty men" <note>A reference to the Song of Solomon 3:7, often interpreted in Kabbalah as the sixty guards of the divine throne</note>, valiant and girded with swords, masters of war, surround it; these men, at a mere nod, overthrow and destroy the enemies of the **MOST HIGH**. Because of the sins of mankind, they plunder and devastate entire provinces, subvert kingdoms, level impregnable walls to the ground, and exact punishments of every kind of vengeance. From these points, established according to the mind of the Hebrews, it is clear that under the command of this **ENUMERATION**, known by the name *Tzedek* <note>original: צדק, Hebrew for "Justice"</note> (which signifies justice), a massive number of legions or battle lines are brought into subjection. These they call "defenders," and they assert that they carry spears, swords, weapons, arrows, bows, and darts to defeat the enemies of the **MOST HIGH**. Hence, they also name this **ENUMERATION** the "sword taking vengeance" upon those who break the covenant. For this power, by seizing sinners, takes away their iniquities and crimes from them and renders them just. This is because, as they say, it is the vestibule where the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God (YHVH), considered too sacred to pronounce</note> separates the just from the impious; it grants the impious no way of entry unless it has first taken vengeance for their sins and inflicted punishment for them.

Sometimes it is also called **THE WELL** by them, because they say it represents the type of a **WELL** of living waters, into which torrents of every kind of blessing flow, according to that passage in *Song of Solomon chapter 4, verse 15*: "A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters distilling from Lebanon." And in *Jeremiah chapter 2, verse 13*: "My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and hewed out for themselves broken cisterns."

Sometimes the name of **THE SEA** is ascribed to it, because just as all rivers flow into the sea, so also into this power are gathered the pools of blessings from all the higher **ENUMERATIONS**, according to that passage in *Ecclesiastes chapter 1*: "All rivers enter into the sea," etc. In this place, it should be noted that "sea" does not denote the water contained, but the containing channel, according to *Isaiah chapter 11, verse 9*: "As the waters covering the sea," etc. Therefore, the receptacle of the waters is also called "the sea."

Conclude, therefore, that this **ENUMERATION** undergoes the name of **DIADEM** <note>original: *DIADEMA*, a title for the final Sephirah, *Malkhut* (Kingdom)</note> according to what is brought down into it—whether good or evil—either internally from the innermost heart of gratuitous mercy, or externally from the punishment of human sins. For this reason, it is also called the **TREE OF KNOWLEDGE** of good and evil. If, according to the mind of the Hebrews, the influence is drawn from the side of grace, the name "good" is bestowed upon it. If, however, it is drawn from the side of judgment—I mean the judgment drawn from the inner chambers of the **ENUMERATIONS**—this too is called "good." But if the judgment emanates from external sources <note>In Kabbalah, "external" often refers to the *Sitra Achra* or "Other Side," the realm of demonic forces and husks</note>, it will be the worst evil and a wicked disposition. For they say that all higher things are drawn into it according to the malice or goodness of men; sometimes the holy channels of judgment are diminished, and the flows of grace and mercy are increased. More often, however, on the contrary, the impious block the channels of grace and mercy, and open many channels of judgment...

...to perish. Therefore, because of the malice of men, all the sharpest and most cruel things come forth into this **ENUMERATION** <term>Numeratio: The author uses this Latin term for the *Sephirot*, the ten divine attributes or powers in Kabbalah</term>; from this, the age is oppressed by various hardships, and so massive misfortunes, slaughters, and every kind of evil, pain, and affliction are brought into the world. Therefore, by right and merit, the name **ADONAI** <note>original: אדני, Hebrew for "Lord"</note> (which signifies Lordship) belongs to this **ENUMERATION**, which is nicknamed the **LOWER DIADEM**. For this reason, the name **TETRAGRAMMATON** is marked with the same vowel points and is pronounced in the same way as the name **ADONAI**. 

Thus, the name **ADONAI**, clothed in the appearance of a devouring fire, sitting on the sublime throne of the **MOST HIGH** as a prince and Lord of the entire world, adorned with royal insignia, shines forth as the most steadfast presiding power over the whole **CHARIOT** <term>Quadriga: Literally "four-horse chariot," here referring to the *Merkabah*, the divine throne-chariot of Ezekiel's vision</term> and of things both above and below. For this power, as they say, seizes one man and carries him to the heavens, while another it casts down to the depths and the abyss of eternal destruction; it makes this man weak and restores that one to health and vigor, just as the equity of judgment from the higher **ENUMERATIONS** seems to demand. From these higher powers, it receives a multiform vigor of **SEVERITY**, **MERCY**, or **CLEMENCY**, etc., sometimes for destruction and sometimes for life. For in that place, nothing is unjustly twisted, nothing is forgotten, and there is no favoritism; rather, as it draws from the things above, so it dispenses to the things below. 

And therefore, as we said above, it is called by various nicknames of the **ENUMERATIONS**, such as the names of **SEVERITY** or **FORTITUDE**, **MERCY** or **MAGNIFICENCE**, and **CLEMENCY**, etc. For it is the storehouse and temple of all the higher **ENUMERATIONS**, inasmuch as the modes of all divine flows are stored within it; yet properly speaking, it is the storehouse of the sixth **ENUMERATION** in order, namely **BEAUTY** <note>original: *PVLCHRITVDINIS*, referring to the Sephirah *Tiferet*</note>. 

For with **BEAUTY** (to which the name **TETRAGRAMMATON** is attributed) acting as a guide, six hundred and twenty columns of inaccessible light break forth from the thirteen peaks of the **HIGHEST CROWN** <note>original: *CORONÆ SVMMÆ*, referring to *Keter*</note> and flow into this storehouse like emerging rivers. Then, from the thirty-two paths of **WISDOM** <note>original: *SAPIENTIÆ*, referring to *Chokhmah*</note> and the fifty gates of **INTELLIGENCE** <note>original: *INTELLIGENTIÆ*, referring to *Binah*</note>; furthermore, from the seventy-two bridges proceeding from the waters of the highest **MERCY**, as well as from the forty-two types of flaming fire of **SEVERITY** from the **HIGHEST MINDS**, passing through the **MIDDLE LINE**, seventy lights of blessings leap forth and gush out. These are joined through the way of **ETERNITY** and **GLORY** in the **ENUMERATION** called *Ehl-Chai* <note>original: אל חי, meaning "The Living God"</note>, otherwise known as the **FOUNDATION** <note>original: *FVNDAMENTVM*, referring to *Yesod*</note>; and from there they flow together into the **KINGDOM** itself, or the **LOWER CROWN**, called **ADONAI**: as appears in the accompanying diagram.

However, it should not be thought that all the aforementioned blessings flow together continuously in the same way (for, as was said above, a multitude of the godly increases the influence of blessing, while a multitude of the ungodly diminishes it). But when the name <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>original: *Tetragrammaton*; the sacred four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, often considered too holy to pronounce.</note> shall prevail so widely that the whole world worships one God—which is believed will happen in the time of the <term>Messiah</term>—then finally all the <term>Numerations</term> <note>original: *Numerationes*; these are the Sephirot, the ten divine attributes or emanations through which God interacts with the universe.</note> will flow together into the lower **Crown** called <term>Lord</term> <note>original: אדני (*Adonai*).</note>. This lower Crown will in turn lavishly bestow that same abundance of goods, which it received from the higher **Numerations**, upon every individual creature according to the limits of each one's nature.

Furthermore, it should be noted that the individual **Numerations** are considered either according to their proper names or their surnames. For example: the **Numeration** fourth in order is surnamed **Magnificence**; by this, **Mercy** is understood. **Mercy**, however, is the surname of that **Numeration** whose proper name is <term>God</term> <note>original: אלוה (*Eloah*).</note>. Likewise, <term>God</term> <note>original: אלהים (*Elohim*).</note> is the proper name of the fifth **Numeration** in order, and it is surnamed **Strength** or **Severity**. The sixth **Numeration**, which is surnamed for **Beauty** or **Ornament**, is properly called the <term>Tetragrammaton</term>; upon which all the holy names of God depend. The proper name of the seventh **Numeration**, which is surnamed for **Eternity**, is <term>God of Hosts</term> <note>original: אלוה צבאות (*Eloah Tzevaot*).</note>. The eighth, surnamed **Glory**, is properly called <term>God of Hosts</term> <note>original: אלהים צבאות (*Elohim Tzevaot*).</note>. The ninth is surnamed **Foundation**, and is properly called <term>The Living God</term> <note>original: אל חי (*El Chai*).</note>. The tenth, which we have discussed so lengthily until now, is surnamed **Kingdom**, and is properly called <term>Lord</term> <note>original: אדני (*Adonai*).</note>: as appears from the accompanying figure.

*Finally, it must also be observed that the epithets are various and manifold for each* <term>Enumeration</term> <note>original: "numerationis," referring to the Sefirot, the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah</note>, *some of the first order, and others of the second order which arise from the epithets of the first order.*

**El** <note>original: אל</note> *(Ehl), is the epithet of the* HIGHEST CROWN <note>original: "Coronæ Summæ," the Sefirah Keter</note>, *whose proper name, as appears from the diagram placed above, is* **Eheyeh** <note>original: אהיה</note> *(Ehejeh). The epithets of the name* **El** *(Ehl) of the second order, however, are* GREAT, GRACIOUS, POWERFUL, SLOW TO ANGER, SUPREMELY MERCIFUL, FREELY WORKING, HOLY, FORGIVING, & RICH IN GRACE, *etc.*

*The epithets of the second order of the name* **Elohim** <note>original: אלהים</note> *(ELOHIM) are* STURDY, JUDGE, JUDGING WITHOUT CONNIVANCE, VEHEMENT, MAN OF WAR, VIGOROUS, STRONG, VISITING SINS, PAYING RETRIBUTION, *etc.*

*The epithets of the name* **YHWH** <note>original: יהוה</note> *(TETRAGRAMMATON) are TERRIBLE, SUSTAINING INIQUITY, PASSING OVER OFFENSES, TRUTHFUL, SUBLIME, EXALTED, GUARDING GRACE, DWELLER IN ETERNITY, HOLY, etc.*

*Regarding the aforementioned epithets: some are instruments of the name* **El** *(Ehl, which is the standard-bearer of the highest grace); others are of the name* **Elohim** *(who goes forth in arms like a warrior), which provide all types of weapons for visiting the sins of men. *From those letters that fall into specific positions, they construct the name of that Angel whose protection they employ, and whom they believe to be the Ruler and President of that work. # FOURTH PATH.

It is called the **Settled** <term>Intelligentia metalis</term> <note>original Latin: metalis; likely a Latinization of the Hebrew "Kavu’a," meaning fixed, established, or permanent. The Latin translator may be connecting it to "meta" or boundary</note> or **Receptacular Intelligence**; and it is so called because into it, as if into a destination, are brought [emanations] from the higher Intelligences, and from it emanate all spiritual virtues through the subtlety of emanations, which emanate one from another by the power of the primordial emanator (I mean the **SUPREME CROWN** <note>original Latin: CORONÆ SVMMÆ; refers to Keter, the highest of the ten Sephiroth or divine emanations</note>), blessed be He.

### *Rabbi Abraham Ben David says:*

The fourth path is called the **Settled** or **Receptacular Intelligence**, and it is so called because from it all virtues emanate, and because all virtues are collected within it and are, as it were, planted in a certain nursery. And for this reason, all spiritual virtues are brought forth from it through the subtlety of emanation; just as the form of a building exists within the **Architect** in the ingenious design of his mind. Therefore, all forms of the building which are in the building itself are all produced from the power of the forms designed in the architect’s mind; each kind exists from its own kind and not from another. An example of this: the form of the window’s structure which is in the design of the craftsman’s mind is the cause of the window actually existing; but the design of a window in the craftsman’s mind is not the cause of a bird painted on the wall of the house; for the design of a window is not the design of a bird. And for this reason, the *wise ones* said that one emanates from another, that is, each kind...

The 4th Path:
It is called the **Fixed Intelligence** <note>original Hebrew: שכל קבוע (Sekhel Kavu’a)</note> and it is so called because from it are emanated all the spiritual powers in the subtlety of the emanation, which are emanated one from another by the power of the Primordial Emanator (the **Supreme Crown** <note>original Hebrew abbreviation: כ״ע (Keter Elyon)</note>, may He be blessed).

And therefore all the spiritual powers were emanated from it in the subtlety of emanation, in the manner of the form of a building in the builder, in the subtlety of his design. And therefore all the forms of the building which are in the building, all of them are emanated from the powers of the design which are in the builder; each kind from its kind and not from another. And the parable for this is that the form of the building of the window which is in the design of the builder is the cause for the window found in actuality; however, the window which is in the design of the builder is not the cause for the bird drawn on the wall of the house. ### THE FIFTH PATH.

<meta>This page continues the commentary by Rabbi Abraham ben David on the Fifth Path (the Rooted Intelligence). It completes a sentence from page 19 describing how divine emanations spread in different directions before providing a philosophical analogy using the sun to explain how a single, simple divine cause can produce multiple, even opposite, effects.</meta>

...are directed to the (a) right or to the left, or (b) forward or backward, or toward judgment or toward mercy: all of them, however, are rooted in one most absolute and equal root, namely in the **second path** <note>The "second path" refers to *Chokmah* (Wisdom), the second Sephirah, which acts as the primordial root for subsequent emanations</note>. For example, the sun softens and liquefies wax, yet congeals and hardens mud, through one and the same power that is within it; and from this we do not conclude that there are diverse powers in the sun—namely, a drying or hardening power and a liquefying or softening power—nor that there is in the sun a quality of drying and liquefying, which would be absurd <note>original Latin: *quod absit*; a traditional phrase used to reject an idea as logically or theologically impossible</note>. This is because the sun is superior to all elements and much more superior to all qualities of the elements; rather, by one and the same power found in the sun, it dries, and so on. And that power, insofar as it is in the sun, is a **simple power** without the influence of any element, and without any quality or diversity. The same is also to be understood concerning the **fifth path**, in which there is an **equal unity** and from which are derived the **children of transition** <note>original Latin: *filii transitus*; a translation of the Hebrew *bnei chalof*, referring to things that are subject to change, flux, or temporary existence</note> and of permutation and variety. And from this, you will grasp the appropriate likeness for the difference between the fifth path and the second path: for the second path is likened to the **soul**, and the fifth path to its **radiance** <note>original Latin: *splendori*; Hebrew: *zivah*</note> in the explanation of the most equal unity.

<column-break/>

...things spreading from it to the right and to the left, and forward and backward, and to judgment and to mercy; all were rooted from one simple and equal root in the **second path**. And the parable for this is the sun, which melts wax and congeals and hardens clay by the power of a **simple unity** within it; not that we should understand from this that there are different powers in the sun—a drying power and a melting power—or that there should be in the sun the quality of melting or dryness, God forbid <note>original Hebrew: *chalilah ve-chas*; a common pious expression used when mentioning something unthinkable or heretical</note>! But the sun is above the elements, and certainly it is above the qualities of the elements. However, by one power in the sun it dries, and that power, while it is in the sun, is a simple power without elemental power and without any quality or change. So too it should be understood regarding the **fifth path**, in which there is an **equal unity**, from which the **children of change** <note>original Hebrew: *bnei chalof*; things that are transient or shifting</note>, substitution, and variation spread. And you can take a likeness of the difference between the fifth path and the second path: for the second path is like the **soul**, and the fifth path is like its **radiance**, in the explanation of equal unity.

<summary>This page uses the analogy of the sun—which can both soften wax and harden clay with the same heat—to explain how the simple, unified power of God produces the diverse and often contradictory effects seen in the created world. It distinguishes between the "Second Path" (the soul/root) and the "Fifth Path" (the radiance/expression), showing how multiplicity arises from a single divine source.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Sephirot (divine emanations). # RITTANGELIUS.
C 3

(a) Either to the right or to the left. It should be noted that among Hebrew theologians <note>original Latin: *Hebraeorum Theologos*</note>, the **right** signifies **mercy** <note>the quality of *Chesed*</note>, while the **left** signifies **severity** or **judgment** <note>the quality of *Gevurah* or *Din*</note>.
(b) Forward or backward; otherwise translated as from the front or from the back.
(c) From which are derived the **children of transition** <note>original Latin: *filii transitus*; a reference to things that change or pass away, often meaning mortal beings or temporal effects</note>, and so on. The virtues <note>or spiritual powers</note> which are brought down and rooted in this fifth path from the higher paths were hitherto similar and equal; however, when they are led down from this path into the lower paths, they pass through and are changed—according to the various behaviors of men—into either mercy or into severity and judgment.

### THE SIXTH PATH

It is called the **Intelligence of the Mediating Influence**, and it is named so because within it the influxes of the **emanations** <note>the process by which divine energy flows from the Infinite into the created world</note> are multiplied. For it causes that very abundance to flow into all the **pools of blessings** which are united to it.

->*Rabbi Abraham, son of David, says:*<-

The sixth path is called the **Intelligence of the Mediating Influence**. It is well known that the word **Affluence** <note>original Hebrew: שפע, *Shefa*; a technical term for the divine "influx" or "flow" that sustains existence</note> is derived from a word signifying "distillation" <note>a trickling or dripping</note> and a great quantity of abundance. As it is said in Job 22:11: *And an abundance of waters shall cover you*; that is, a great influx of waters. And behold, the trickling and the abundance of the influx that flows down from the sixth path behaves in the same way that the light of the sun flows forth: its light is drawn down by derivation into the moon, and the sun’s light also flows over all existing things. In this same way, from the sixth path, a diverse and distinct influx flows—namely, from the sixth path down to the lakes and springs which are united to the sixth path itself.

<column-break/>

**The Sixth Path:**
It is called the **Intelligence of the Mediating Influx**, and it is called thus because in it the influx of the emanation is multiplied. And it causes that influx to flow upon all the blessings that are united in its essence.

**The Ravad <note>Acronym for Rabbi Abraham ben David, a 12th-century French scholar and kabbalist</note> said:**
The Sixth Path is called the Intelligence of the Mediating Influx. It is known that "Influx" <note>Hebrew: שפע, *Shefa*</note> comes from the language of "flowing" and "increase," as it is said: *and an abundance of water covers you*, which means a multitude of flowing water. And behold, the flowing and the increase which flows from the Sixth Path is like the light of the sun, from which light flows and trickles to the moon; and further, light flows from the sun upon all existing things. Thus, from the Sixth Path, a mediating influx flows and is separated from the Sixth Path unto the blessings and the sources that are united in the essence of the Sixth Path.

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic transition from the Fifth Path (Judgment/Mercy) to the Sixth Path (the Mediating Influence), using the analogy of sunlight reflecting onto the moon to describe how divine energy flows through the universe.</summary>

# THE SEVENTH PATH.

It is called the **Hidden Intelligence**, and it is so named because it is the refulgent splendor that shines into all the intellectual virtues which are perceived by the eyes of the intellect and through the contemplation of faith.

->Rabbi Abraham, son of David <note>original Latin: *Abraham F. D.*, referring to the medieval commentator known as the Ra'avad</note>, says:<-

The seventh path is called the **Hidden Intelligence** because it is hidden from all others besides itself, and it is not comprehended except through the **Intelligences of the NUMERATIONS** <note>original Latin: *Numerationum*; original Hebrew: *Sefirot*. These are the ten divine emanations or attributes in Kabbalistic thought</note>. And this is the difference between the seventh path and the path which is called "admirable" or "concealed": namely, that it is denied to the Intelligences themselves to comprehend the admirable or concealed path by means of reason; yet the seventh path is apprehended by the Intelligences which are in **those Numerations**, and also by the mind and contemplation of the inferior **DIADEM** <note>original Latin: *Diadematis*; original Hebrew: *Atarah*. A term for the tenth and final Sephirah, Malchut (Kingdom), representing the manifest presence of God</note> which is called "faithful."

->RITTANGELIUS <note>Johannes Stephanus Rittangel (1606–1652), a professor of Oriental languages who translated this work into Latin</note>.<-

(a) (**Intelligences**) *Intelligence* in this place signifies divine attributes, which are otherwise called the **lower Numerations** and **Properties** <note>original Hebrew: *Middot*; the qualities or character traits of the Divine</note>.
(b) (**In the Numerations**) namely, in the seven lower ones.

### THE EIGHTH PATH.

It is called the **Absolute or Perfect Intelligence**, and it is named so because it is the foundation of primordiality <note>original Latin: *apparatus primordialitatis*; suggesting the primary "setup" or structure of ancient existence</note> which has no root in which it may cling or reside, except in the inner chambers of **MAGNIFICENCE** <note>original Latin: *Magnificentiae*; original Hebrew: *Gedulah*. This is another name for the Sephirah of *Chesed* (Loving-kindness or Mercy)</note> which emanate from the very essence of its own existence.

<column-break/>

The Seventh Path:
It is called the **Hidden Intelligence**, and it is so named because it is a brilliant light shining for all the intellectual powers that are seen with the eye of the mind and in the thought of faith.

->The Ra'avad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David</note> said:<-

The seventh path is called the **Hidden Intelligence** because it is hidden from all that is outside of it, and it is not grasped except by the Intelligences of the **Sephirot**. And this is the difference between the seventh path and the "Wondrous Path": that the Intelligences are prevented from understanding the Wondrous, but the seventh path is grasped by the thinkers who are in these **Sephirot**, and also by the thought and contemplation of the **Atarah** <note>The Diadem or Crown</note> which is called "Faith."

### The Eighth Path:

It is called the **Perfect Intelligence**, and it is so named because it is the disposition of primordiality <note>or "ancientness"</note> which has no root to settle in except in the chambers of **Gedulah** <note>Magnificence/Mercy</note> which are emanated from the essence of its existence.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom from the Sefer Yetzirah. Having concluded the description of the Seventh Path, it proceeds to the Eighth and Ninth Paths, exploring the nature of perfection and purification within the divine emanations or Sefirot.</meta>

### Rabbi Abraham F. D. <note>original: *Abraham F. D.*, referring to Rabbi Abraham ben David of Posquières, known as the Ra'avad, a 12th-century French Kabbalist</note> says:

The eighth path is called the **Absolute or Perfect Intelligence**, derived from the words of Isaiah 60:20: "And the days of your mourning shall be ended" <note>original Hebrew: *ve-shalmu yemei evel-ekha*</note>; that is to say, because they are made perfect and have reached their fulfillment. And this is because these paths are absolute and perfect. It is impossible to reach the end of this path except through the **INTELLIGENCE** which is called "illuminating," and for that reason, it is also called absolute or perfect. And do not wonder at this matter, for a difficulty of this kind exists between every pair of path types. To give an example of this: behold (a) [**THE PURPLE-DYE CREATURE** <note>original Latin: *COCCUM DIADEMA*; Hebrew: *hilazon*. This refers to the legendary sea creature, often identified as a snail, used to produce the sacred blue or purple dye for priestly garments</note>] — it is impossible to determine whether it belongs to the class of fish or to the class of plants, because it lives and moves, yet does not change its location, being fixed and rooted to the earth <note>This reflects a medieval understanding of certain marine life, like corals or anemones, as "zoophytes" that blur the line between animal and plant</note>. And whoever wishes to reach that point to know the truth of this path must search for it within the innermost chambers of **MAGNIFICENCE** <note>original Latin: *Magnificentiae*; referring to the Sephirah *Chesed* (Greatness/Mercy)</note> (**BEAUTY** <note>original Hebrew abbreviation: *תת'* (T.T.) for *Tiferet*; Latin: *Pulchritudinis*</note>) from which it emanates.

It is called the **Pure Intelligence**, and it is so named because it purifies the **NUMERATIONS** <note>original Latin: *Numerationes*; original Hebrew: *Sefirot*. These are the ten channels of divine creative energy</note> and proves and corrects the shaping of their image; it arranges the unity of those things which are joined to it without any cutting away or division <note>A warning against "cutting the shoots," a Kabbalistic metaphor for heresy where one perceives the divine attributes as separate gods rather than a unified whole</note>.

### Rabbi Abraham ben David says:

The eighth path is called the **Perfect Intelligence** <note>original Hebrew: *Sekhel Shalem*</note> from the expression "and the days of your mourning shall be ended," for they are finished and have reached their limit. Because the paths are finished and perfected, and it is impossible to stand upon the purpose of this path except by means of the illuminating intelligence, it is therefore called "perfect." And do not be surprised by this thing, for this doubt exists between every two species. The parable for this is: behold the **snail** <note>original Hebrew: *hilazon*</note>; it is impossible to determine if it is among the class of fish or among the class of plants, for it is alive and moves, yet does not change its place, for it is stuck and fixed in the earth. And everyone who comes to know the truth of this path must investigate it from the chambers of **Greatness** <note>original Hebrew: *Gedulah*, another name for the Sephirah *Chesed*</note> (**Beauty** <note>original Hebrew: *Tiferet*</note>) which is emanated from it.

...then we may understand they say: just as the **Diaphragm** <note>The author uses the Latin *Diaphragma* to refer to the midriff muscle, which he likens to a spiritual barrier</note>, to which they liken this path, divides the instruments of nutrition and of the soul by its position, so this path distinguishes the higher paths from the lower ones, or God from His attributes.

Having found this opportunity, I have decided to treat briefly the various kinds of Hebrew interpretation of Sacred Scripture, especially for the purpose that the reader might be better versed in their writings; furthermore, to show how much the method of the ancient Rabbis, who were imbued with true knowledge, differs from the training and delusions <note>original: *deliriis*; the author reflects a common 17th-century scholarly view that older Jewish traditions were "scientific" while contemporary mystical practices were "madness"</note> of modern Jews. I openly testify that I do not wish to teach, but to relate, on the condition that to have related some things is to have looked down on all. Before I enter upon this undertaking, I judge it worthwhile to digress a little from the purpose and to preface it with brief remarks so that what we are treating may be better understood; whoever is observant can see that our digression is not unnecessary. For by these things, we have decided to pave the way for the reader, lest they produce weariness if they are poorly understood. It is known to the more learned that glorious mention is made among the Hebrews of **Kabbalah** <note>original: *Cabalæ*; the Jewish mystical tradition</note>, and that this is said to be the hidden doctrine handed down from God to Moses on Mount Sinai. Some of their wise men have called this "divine philosophy" or "speculative theology," which, if compared with our theology, will not differ much from it. Truly, the modern Jews do not use this kind of Kabbalah, but another: where, for instance, through the likeness of things, or through the artificial equivalence of characters in arithmetic calculation, they think they have a certain and settled hope—not a deceptive conjecture—of future events and prophetic meaning. Through the breaking down of the very words in which Scripture is expressed, or through different meanings, or construction, or division, or through context, re-weaving, transposition, combination, or the mutual exchange of letters among themselves, they try to pull back the general veil of enigmatic meaning and investigate the truth of divine mysteries; and through individual characters, they believe they can explain the divine mysteries hidden in the minds of the Angels.

There are three types of these Kabbalistic modes and methods still in use today, through which the Hebrews—and indeed some among our own theologians who are imitators of the Hebrews and seem to themselves to be very wise—strive to explain Sacred Scripture. From individual phrases, words, characters, letters, and curls of the pen, they strive to elicit not only single but manifold mysteries, or rather delusions, which I pass over. Although many things from the books and fragments of the Hebrews would be available for us to say, our purpose does not allow us to pursue every detail. Lest we seem to promise much but perform nothing, we will subjoin some trifles worthy of note; finally, setting aside all discussions, we will set forth our mind in a single word.

Furthermore, I return to the purpose. There are three kinds of Kabbalistic interpretation of Holy Scripture, as I said, marked by these terms among modern Hebrews: <term>Temurah (Permutation)</term> <note>original Hebrew: תמורה; the system of substituting one letter for another according to a set code</note>, <term>Notaricon (Shorthand)</term> <note>original Hebrew: נוטריקון; a method of creating acronyms or breaking words into phrases</note>, and <term>Gematria</term> <note>original Hebrew: ג'מטריא; the practice of calculating the numerical value of letters to find connections between words</note>.

...while the characters of a single word, when transposed or swapped among themselves, seem able to indicate something else. Another species of this permutation is the swap of the letters of the alphabet; this is done such that the first letter **Aleph** <note>א</note> is swapped with all others, and all letters with **Aleph**. Concerning this, Rabbi Moses Botarel <note>a 14th-century Spanish scholar and commentator</note> treats at length in chapter 2, section 4, page 1 of the *Book of Formation* <note>original: *Libri Formationis*, better known as the *Sefer Yetzirah*</note>. However, before we withdraw our hand from this first type of the second species, we shall submit a single "delusion" <note>original: *delirium*</note> worthy of laughter. If, therefore, I were to attempt to elicit another name from this name written above—namely **BENEDICTUS DE MONTE ORO BARABRANTO**—it would necessarily be done via the "Minor Table of All Things" through a <term>Ziruph</term> <note>permutation</note>, specifically the 157th part. They use this kind of Kabbalah, first, in publishing books to which the authors prefix their names in this hidden manner, so that they are known not to just anyone, but only to those skilled in Kabbalah. Let the author of *Maaseh Torah*, and Rabbi Kalonymus, and the author of the book *Turei Zahav*, etc., be examples for us. Secondly, this same kind is familiar to those who attach names with transposed or swapped letters to the poems they have composed in honor of authors, as can be seen in the book *On the Properties of Animals*, and in many of my own writings and poems where you will sometimes find "Benedictus de Monte Oro Barabranto," and occasionally even "Nathan Nestoli of Prague." Thirdly, they sign their names in this way in books to be sent from afar, for which they fear interception.

It should be noted that if they should find themselves "stuck in the water" <note>original: *aqua hæreat*; a Latin idiom for being at a loss or stuck</note> even once, and cannot explain their dream using one type of Kabbalah, they make an attempt in a second, third, or following conjugation, until they finally arrive at that one which relates and represents that same dream of theirs. They have no reason to fear frustration, since two thousand sixteen parts—<term>Ziruphim</term> or conjugations—well known to them, are available in the "Minor Table," even before considering the other tables and conjugations and combinations...

<meta>This page continues the author’s critique of Kabbalistic methods. ...I will pass over those combinations and transmutations which neither their own intellects can grasp nor their memories retain. <meta>This page continues the author's explanation of how Kabbalists use numerical calculations to interpret the origins of souls. From this, it is concluded that when a Gentile associates himself with the Jews <note>That is, when a non-Jew converts to Judaism.</note>, a soul is created for him of a kind that has not yet been created in all the years since the beginning of the world; instead, that soul had previously only wandered in its own state of lostness among the remaining 974 generations. For as long as the Israelites were in Egypt until the proclamation of the Law, they shared in the souls from those 26 generations that had remained. From this it is clear that the Israelites possessed souls of the same rank and dignity as those 974 generations. 

And this is what the Scripture intends to say through that verse: <note>original: ואתם ידעתם את נפש הגר כי גרים הייתם בארץ מצרים</note> *And you know the soul of the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt* (Exodus, chapter 23, verse 9). This means: You know what kind of soul a stranger <note>The Hebrew word "Ger" (stranger/peregrinus) is often used to mean a convert to Judaism.</note> possesses—namely, that he has a soul from the 974 generations, from which you also received your own souls as long as you were in Egypt, because you too were "strangers" in the land of Egypt, as the Scripture testifies. 

Furthermore, they imagine that **Jethro** <note>The father-in-law of Moses.</note> was both the first stranger and the one who obtained the first soul from these 974 generations. Nor is there any ground, they say, for the objection that Abraham preceded him; this is because Abraham possessed a soul from those 26 generations which had already been brought into actual existence long before. Hence, this number 974 is also contained within the name **Jethro** <note>original: יתרו</note>. For if the four letters of the name Jethro are written out in their "fullness and power" <note>A Kabbalistic technique called *Fillings* (Millui), where each letter of a word is spelled out as a full word (e.g., writing the letter 'A' as 'Ay').</note> in this manner—*Iod, Resch, Thau, Vau* <note>original: יוד ריש תו ויו</note>—they result in the number 968. Furthermore, there exists among the Jews a daily prayer called *Keryat Shema* <note>original: קרית שמע</note> (meaning "The Reading of 'Hear'"). (They use this term in their books to refer to the reading found in Deuteronomy, chapter 6, verse 4, where the text begins: *Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one.* <note>original: שמע ישראל ה' אלהינו ה' אחד</note> The Hebrews are accustomed to recite this reading as a prayer both morning and evening with the greatest possible concentration.) In this prayer, 120 doubled letters are found, which must be accurately discerned and distinguished from one another in pronunciation. For unless a person does this, they will be liable—as the Jews themselves teach—to 120 punishments. These punishments result from the Kabbalists' skillful transposition of the permutations <note>The "conjugation" or rearranging of letters to find hidden meanings</note> of the Divine Attribute ***Elohim*** <note>original: אלהים</note>. 

For they have a common rule stating that "five stones build 120 houses." <note>A classic rule from the *Sefer Yetzirah*, an early Kabbalistic text, explaining that five letters can be rearranged into 120 different combinations (5 factorial)</note> From this, two properties arise: one in the kingdom of holiness called ***Tzel*** <note>original: צל</note> (meaning "shadow" or "protection"), and the other, conversely, in the kingdom of impurity, called ***Letz*** <note>original: לץ</note> (meaning "scoffer" or "mocker") by transposing the letters. Each of these terms, through the calculation of Gematria <note>original: *supputationem Geomatricam*; the practice of assigning numerical values to letters</note>, equals 120. 

This is the source for the commentary in the *Vayikra Rabbah* <note>A homiletic Midrash on the book of Leviticus</note>, section 1, regarding the words of the prophet <note>The text attributes this to Joel 1:4-5, but the quote "revertentur habitatores in umbra ejus" actually corresponds to Hosea 14:7</note>: *They shall return and dwell in his shadow.* <note>original: ישובו ישבי בצלו</note> These, it says, are the strangers <note>Converts to Judaism</note> who come and seek refuge in the shadow of the Holy God. From this it also follows that strangers are admitted to the property and virtue of the "shadow" (*Tzel*). Holy Scripture expresses this in 1 Chronicles, chapter 29, verse 15, with these words: *For we are strangers before you... our days on the earth are like a shadow.* <note>original: כי גרים אנחנו לפניך כצל ימינו</note> It is as if it says: because we are strangers, we have trust and access to the shadow of holiness. Therefore, it is said in the *Midrashim*: the scoffer <note>original: *derisor*, referring to the Hebrew *Letz*</note>—that is, **Amalek** <note>The biblical arch-enemy of Israel, representing the "impure" side of the 120 permutations</note>—will be crushed, while the simple—that is, **Jethro**—will become wise.
