...assigned to every nation is a prince or an Angel as a Ruler in the heavens; when that figure falls or is conquered in the heavens, that nation also falls in this sublunary world. Hence, when the prince or Ruler of the Amalekites <note>The Amalekites are portrayed in the Bible as the ancestral enemies of the Israelites; in mystical tradition, they represent the essence of doubt and impurity.</note> fell in the heavens, the nation itself—the most wicked of all on earth—likewise fell. For before Amalek fell, it was not possible for Jethro, as a foreigner, to become a Jew. For foreigners held their perception in the power of the **shadow** <note>original Hebrew: צל (*tzal*); here meaning divine protection or the "shadow" of holiness</note>, and at that time the power of the **derider** <note>original Hebrew: לץ (*letz*); a play on the letters of "shadow" reversed, representing the "Kingdom of Impurity" or mockery</note> of the Amalekites prevailed from the side of the kingdom of impurity. 

It is well established that the Kingdom of Holiness and the kingdom of impurity regard each other as opposites; while one prevails, the other falls. After the power of the **derider** of the kingdom of impurity was weakened, the power of the **shadow** of the kingdom of holiness gained dominance. Jethro then became a Jew and took hold of the trust in the power of the **shadow** of the kingdom of holiness. 

This is what is said concerning the fall of Haman in *Esther chapter 8, verse 17*: **And many of the people of the land became Jews.** <note>original Hebrew: ורבים מעמי הארץ מתייהדים</note> (That is: after the characteristic of the **derider** of the kingdom of impurity was weakened, and the power of the **shadow** gained dominance, many became Jews. For after the prince or Ruler of the nation of Amalek fell in the heavens in the kingdom of impurity, Haman himself and his nation fell on earth; the power of the **shadow** of holiness gained dominance, and then many became Jews and took hold of the power of the **shadow** of holiness.)

The third type [of interpretation] through which they attempt to twist Holy Scripture into a foreign sense—contrary to the intention of the Holy Spirit—is called **Notaricon** <term>Notaricon: A Kabbalistic shorthand method where the letters of a word are treated as an acronym for a full phrase, or initial letters of a phrase are combined to form a new word.</term>. This occurs in two ways. First, they combine the initial, middle, or final letters of distinct words so that they can elicit some convenient meaning from them when combined into one. Second, they diligently inquire whether words proposed in a specific text occur in other places as well; they then pay attention to the meaning of those other words with which they are found constructed, and they foolishly attach that same meaning to their own words.

They use this species of interpretation when, as said above, they busily try to elicit a mystery from Scripture according to their own madness in this manner. Let the passage concerning **Esau** <note>original Hebrew: עשו</note> serve as an example, of whom Scripture says that he returned as a hunter from the field. From this, through Kabbalah, they produce a far different meaning: that Esau committed three sins. Indeed, they attribute as much faith to this sense—out of a certain foolish superstition—as if it had actually happened in reality. Thus, it is read in *Genesis*: *That Isaac called his firstborn Esau.* **And they called his name Esau.** <note>original Hebrew: ויקראו שמו עשו; Genesis 25:25</note> 

They say the Prophet Malachi <note>Malachi 1:3</note> points out the reason why he imposed this name in these words: **And I hated Esau** <note>original Hebrew: ואת עשו שנאתי</note>; they claim the initial letters of these words (just like those mentioned before) constitute the name **Esau**. Furthermore, they say the cause of this divine hatred toward Esau becomes known from the words: **And Esau came from the field and he was weary.** <note>original Hebrew: ויבא עשו מן השדה והוא עיף; Genesis 25:29</note> According to the mind of the author of the book titled **Midrash Rabbah** <term>Midrash Rabbah: An ancient collection of homiletic and allegorical interpretations of the Torah, often exploring the moral or legal implications of the text.</term> in the section **Toledot** <note>original Hebrew: תולדות ("Generations"); the portion of Genesis covering the life of Isaac and his sons.</note>, these words indicate and signify three sins committed by Esau on that same day; the first of which...

<meta>This page continues the critique of Jewish interpretive methods, specifically focusing on how the "Pharisees" (Rabbinic Jews) use word associations to vilify Esau, before transitioning into a discussion on the historical animosity between Rabbinic Jews and the "Textuaries" or Karaites.</meta>

...first, they prove it was theft from the words of **Obadiah** chapter 1, verse 5: **If thieves come to you** <note>original Hebrew: אם גנבים באו לך (*im gannavim bau lach*)</note>, because the word **and he came** <note>original Hebrew: ויבא (*v-yavo*)</note>, which appears with **Esau** in **Genesis** chapter 25, verse 29, is found joined with the word **thieves** <note>original Hebrew: גנבים (*gannavim*)</note> in **Obadiah** chapter 1, verse 5. They say the second sin was that on the same day he forced himself upon a betrothed young woman, which they derive from the word **field** <note>original Hebrew: שדה (*sadeh*)</note>. Moreover, because the word **field**, from which **Esau** is said to have returned—just as the words quoted above sound: **And Esau came from the field** <note>original Hebrew: ויבא עשו מן השדה (*v-yavo Esau min ha-sadeh*)</note>—also appears in **Numbers** chapter 22, verses 25 and 27, where sexual assault with a betrothed woman is prohibited; they conclude from this that **Esau** himself committed such a crime. The acronym uses the Ayin from *Ayef*, the Shin from *Sadeh*, and the Vav from *Vayavo*.</note>.

And let it suffice to have spoken thus about the various ways of interpreting Holy Scripture, which were also the causes of various sects and disturbances among the **Jews**, and which stirred up not only wordy arguments and insults, but even slaughter, fires, and other most cruel persecutions. For it would be a monstrous thing to tell of that persistent and stubborn hatred of the **Pharisees** <note>The author uses "Pharisees" here to refer to the Rabbinic Jewish establishment of his time.</note> toward the **Samaritans**, or those known by the common name **Textuaries** <note>original Hebrew: קראים (*Karaites*); a Jewish sect that recognizes the Tanakh/Hebrew Bible alone as supreme authority, rejecting the Oral Law or Talmud.</note>, conceived solely for this reason: that the **Samaritans** or **Textuaries**, rejecting all human traditions, rest only upon the text of Scripture. That hatred has been so increased over a long time in their minds that it is not even extinguished by death, but passes to their descendants like a fire; as long as it finds fuel, it does not stop devouring. So too did that hatred rage as long as these two contrary sects flourished. I would even dare to say that although the "accursed hunger for gold" <note>A classical reference to Virgil's *Aeneid*.</note> greatly twists the minds of these men, far more numerous and more horrible crimes have been committed by them for the sake of religion than for the greed of profit or personal advantage. For **Christians** or **Turks** <note>A common early modern term for Muslims.</note> are not so abominable to the **Pharisees** as they loathe and curse the **Samaritans** or **Textuaries** themselves. 

Of this matter, out of many, we shall place before your eyes a single extraordinary example. Among the **Pharisees**, it is cautioned under penalty of anathema <note>A formal curse or excommunication.</note> that no one from the **Textuaries** may be admitted into their assembly. If it should happen, therefore, that a **Textuary**, perhaps convicted in his own conscience, wishes to cross over to the **Pharisees**, they still do not deign to record him among their own—lest they seem to have departed from the law of anathema—unless he first defects from the religion of the **Textuaries** to the faith of the **Turks**, or is first made a **Christian** through Baptism. Furthermore, although they are punished by the same penalty and placed under an equal yoke, they nevertheless do not cease to rage against one another to this very day. Whatever is achieved or prepared by the **Samaritans**, even if for the glory of God, they detest as profane; they even judge their hides and parchments, upon which the Law is written, to be unworthy (though they are less religious regarding the artifacts made by **Christians** and **Turks**). O detestable, O ruinous, O cursed hatred!

<meta>This page continues the author's polemic against Rabbinic Jewish methods of interpreting Scripture. Having previously discussed the specific "insane opinions" regarding the figure of Esau, the author now transitions into a broader critique of Jewish legal codes and the mystical-linguistic interpretive systems (such as Gematria) used by the Rabbis, arguing they lead away from the true meaning of the Bible.</meta>

*What nation was ever so barbaric that it would not shudder at such an insane, brute, and cursed opinion? And what nation would not detest such a raging, detestable, and ruinous hatred? We could still cite many things from their various codices <note>A term for early bound books or manuscript volumes</note>, but the brevity of time and this hasty undertaking of ours did not permit it. For such great contradiction and diversity appear from their fragments that the space of a single year would scarcely suffice for reviewing them. Let anyone who pleases look into the **Talmudic** books. Let him look into the book **Shulchan Aruch** <note>original: Schülchan Aruch; "The Set Table," a definitive 16th-century code of Jewish law</note>, **Maharil** <note>original: Maheril; referring to the customs collected by Jacob Moelin</note>, **Levush** <note>original: Lebhusch; "The Attire," a code of law by Mordecai Jaffe</note>, **Arba’ah Turim** <note>original: Arba Thurim; "The Four Rows," a foundational legal code by Jacob ben Asher</note>, that great **Alfus** <note>original: Alphusum; referring to the legal rulings of Isaac Alfasi, an 11th-century North African scholar</note>, and finally the book **On Co-Stepchildren** <note>original: de Comprivignis</note> written by me, and others, where so many thousands upon thousands of the **Rabbis’** <note>original: Rabinorum</note> dogmas are found—contrary and repugnant to the divine law—which are accepted by the Jews inhabiting our regions, but rejected by those of **Castile**, **Jerusalem**, **Babylon**, and **Italy**. And what wonder is it if, among so many nations distinct from one another in locations, languages, heart, opinion, and customs—living without a king and without a flock—with hearts obstinate in hardness and the malice of sins (on account of which all these things have happened to them), and becoming more and more hardened day by day, they have fostered so many insane opinions and arrived at the highest kind of madness and ignorance? What shall I say of the disturbances of the **Masoretes** <note>The scribes and scholars who standardized the text and pronunciation of the Hebrew Bible</note>? For it has come to this, that the whole **Masoretic** reading is subject to errors and—except for a few of the more excellent **Rabbis**—is foreign and hidden from the eyes of almost all Jews because it deals entirely with abbreviations; it is like a dream for which there is no interpreter, and it does nothing other than inquire how many times each word occurs in the Law, in the Prophets, and in the **Hagiographa** <note>original: hagiographis; "Holy Writings," the third section of the Hebrew Bible (Ketuvim), which includes books like Psalms and Proverbs</note>, and by forging those passages into one, presents some convenient sense and context. Sometimes it advises omitting certain things, sometimes transposing them to another place, and sometimes passing over them entirely: now it uses types of permutations or combinations of categories, now the **Gematric** method <note>original: Gematrico; Gematria is a system where letters of the alphabet are assigned numerical values, allowing words to be interpreted through their sums</note>; or by the mutual exchange of letters, now by the **Notarikon** <note>original: Notarico; an interpretive method using words as acronyms or breaking them into parts</note> artifice, it seeks the context of matters. O fragile defense! O ruinous bulwark! O unstable foundation of faith! Not the strongest and impregnable arguments! Who will provide a fence for this truncated and mutilated enclosure? Who will provide a foundation for this foundation? Who will provide a bulwark for this bulwark? From this it has resulted that, departing from the sound interpretation of Holy Scripture and from the most wholesome mind of the Holy Spirit, they have drunk in vain opinions, and have finally fallen into manifold **idolatries** <note>original: Idololatrias</note>. O fate! O death! to be deplored even by their very enemies! For these things I condemn along with the Rabbis themselves and the theologians of the earliest Hebrews, who were imbued with true knowledge, as is apparent from this and others of their books, and I say that Holy Scripture is to be understood perfectly according to the letter, grammatically and regularly, not entangled in a variety of mysteries by way of **Gematria**, **Notarikon**, or **Permutation**. For even if such methods can sometimes be employed to show the manifold riches of Divine Wisdom, nevertheless they cannot by themselves establish faith in unknown matters concerning the foundations of religion.*

<meta>This page transitions from the previous polemic against Rabbinic legalism into a mystical exposition of Kabbalistic philosophy. While the previous page criticized the "insane opinions" of the Rabbis regarding scripture and law, this page presents a more technical, mystical analysis of the "Twelfth Path" of wisdom, using the commentary of Rabbi Abraham ben David (the Ravad) and the editor Rittangelius’s own extensive notes on the nature of the Divine Chariot.</meta>

### THE TWELFTH PATH.
It is called the Intelligence of Clarity: and it is called so because it is the very form of **MAGNIFICENCE**, which is called *Chachazit* <note>original: חוחזית; a mystical term derived from the Hebrew root for "vision" or "sight"</note>, which is said to be the place from which the vision of seers arises in a manifestation. (*This refers to the prophecy given to the prophets within a vision.*)

#### Rabbi Abraham ben David says:
The twelfth path is called the Intelligence of Clarity: And it is called so because it is the very manifestation through which all seers—that is, those reaching the depth (a) of the **CHARIOT** <note>original: Quadriga; in Hebrew, the *Merkabah*, the central focus of early Jewish mysticism involving the vision of God’s throne</note>—and all the Prophets behold the vision. And it is called the mode of **MAGNIFICENCE**, because within the vision are encompassed the lower things, the higher things, and all existing things. And this is the mystery of the clarity which is in the heavens and is called *Chachazit*, according to the verse in Numbers chapter 24, verse 16: *And he shall see the vision of the Almighty.*

<column-break/>

### The 12th Path:
It is called the Lucent Intelligence; it is so named because it is the essence of the Great Wheel <note>meaning the Sephirah or sphere</note> called *Chachazit*, which means the source of the vision of the seers in a manifestation.

#### The Ravad <note>Rabbi Abraham ben David</note> says:
The 12th path is called the Lucent Intelligence, and is so called because it is the vision in which all the seers—meaning those who descend to the **Chariot** <note>original: yordei hamerkabah; a term for mystics who "descend" into the divine realms</note>—and the prophets gaze. It is called the Mode of Magnificence because within the vision, the higher and lower worlds and all that exists are included. This is the secret of "brightness in the skies," and it is called *Chachazit* after the phrase "and he shall behold the vision of the Almighty."

THE TRINITY, this most simple and highly perfect UNITY of their ESSENCE—from which all true and good beings arise—they called the first of all things. ...the weighing within Himself and the dimension of created bodies, because it is appropriate that this dimension exists until the body is ordered, arranged, and suitably disposed for that purpose for which it was created. He means to say the **NUMBERER** <term>Numerans; referring to the divine consciousness as the author of the 'Book' of reality</term>: if you were to observe a certain architect, a house does not leave his hand until he has first outlined its form in his mind. > Let there be light, and there was light: let there be an expanse, etc.

The Word does not go forth without the thing itself existing at the same time. By **THE NUMBERED** <term>Numeratum; the result of the divine calculation</term>, he says, is understood **WRITING**: And the **WRITING OF GOD** is its outline or form, and the **WORD OF GOD** is its **WRITING**, and the **WEIGHTING OF GOD** is **HIS WORD**. Behold, you have the mystery of the **NUMBERER**, the **NUMBER**, and the **NUMBERED**, which are **ONE** in the heart of the abyss of the **DIVINE ESSENCE**, but in the human heart they are **THREE**: because man weighs with his intellect, speaks with his mouth, and writes with his hand.

And **Number** <term>Sefar; the mathematical or written recording</term>, that is to say, the writing: and the writing of God is His imagery, and the word of God is His writing, and the measure of God is His word. And behold, the secret of the **Book**, the **Numberer**, and the **Story** <note>These three terms—Sefer, Sefar, and Sippur—are the famous "Three Sefarim" from the opening of the Sefer Yetzirah</note> are one thing in the law of God, but in the law of man they are three, because man measures in his mind, speaks with his mouth, and writes with his hand.

In the book *Tikkunei Zohar* <note>A classic text of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah) focused on the book of Genesis.</note> entry *Tikkun* 42, folio 84, columns 1 and 2, *Rabbi Simeon son of Yochai*, the author of the book of *Tikkunim*, says: **There were three ARTIFICES** <note>Or "Craftsmen."</note> up to this point: the First day, the second day, and the third day; and each one produced its own work. Here, the text explores the relationship between "Wisdom" and "Non-being," using the book of Job to explain how divine emanations emerge from a hidden source.</meta>

# Chapter 1, Verse 9
### And God said, let the waters beneath the heavens be gathered into one place so that the dry land may appear.

Rabbi Abraham ben David <note>often referred to by the acronym Ravad, a 12th-century French scholar and kabbalist.</note>, on folios 25 and 26, columns 2 and 3, and folio 27, column 2, in chapter 1, section 1 of the *Book of Formation* <note>original Latin: *libri Iezirah*; also known as the Sefer Yetzirah.</note>, explains the passage from the book of Job, chapter 28, verse 12 through to the end of the chapter, which reads as follows:

(*And **Wisdom** shall be found from **Non-being** <note>original Latin: *de Non-ente*; Hebrew: *Ayin* (Nothingness).</note>, and אי׳ <note>original Hebrew: *Ay* or *Eih*, meaning "Where". In kabbalistic wordplay, this word is treated as a name for a specific divine level.</note>—this is the place of **UNDERSTANDING** <note>original Latin: *Intelligentiae*; Hebrew: *Binah*.</note>. Man does not know its **ORDER**, nor shall it be found in the **LAND OF THE LIVING**. The Abyss said, "It is not in me," and the Sea said, "It is not with me." Pure **GOLD** shall not be given for it, nor shall its price be weighed in **SILVER**. It shall not be valued with the **GOLD OF OPHIR**, with the precious **ONYX** and the **SAPPHIRE**. **GOLD** and **CRYSTAL** shall not equal it, nor shall its exchange be a vessel of **REFINED GOLD**. **CORALS** and **PEARLS** shall not be mentioned, and the drawing forth of **WISDOM** is above **GEMS**. The **EMERALD OF ETHIOPIA** shall not equal it; it shall not be valued with pure gold. And **Wisdom** shall come from **NON-

The Ravad, on folio 25, side 2 and 3, and folio 26, side 2 and 3, and folio 27, side 2: "And wisdom," he says, "shall be found from **Nothingness** <note>Hebrew: *Ayin*.</note>," meaning from the power whose essence is not grasped—from there she is found. And it is "Where?" <note>Hebrew: *Eih*.</note>, the existence of **Being** <note>Hebrew: *Yesh*.</note> from **Nothingness**. He said: this is not a complete absence, for no thing is brought into being from any [random] thing, much less is Being brought into existence from Nothingness. Rather, it is called "Nothing" because it is not grasped, neither by its cause nor by itself, for its cause is the **Cause of Causes**. And it is called the "**Ancient Nothingness**" because it preceded the world, and it is not a physical thing. "And where <note>Hebrew: *Eih*.</note> is the place of Understanding?"—meaning "Where" and "Wisdom" are the causes...

BEING**; and אי׳ <note>original Hebrew: *Ay* or *Eih*.</note>—this is the place of **UNDERSTANDING**, and it is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the heavens. Destruction and death said, "With our ears we have heard the report of it." God understood its way, and He Himself knew its place. For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees under all the heavens. To make a weight for the wind, and He prepared the waters in measure. In making a decree for the rain, and a path for the lightning of the thunder. Then He saw it and declared it; He prepared it and also searched it out. And He said to man: "Behold, the **FEAR OF THE LORD** is **WISDOM** itself, and to depart from evil is **UNDERSTANDING**.")

**WISDOM**, he says, exists out of **NON-BEING**, that is, from the **SUPREME CROWN** <note>original Latin: *Corona Summa*; Hebrew: *Keter*, the highest of the ten Sefirot.</note>, whose essence is not comprehended; from that, I say, exists (**WISDOM**). And that is the existence of **BEING** <note>original Latin: *Entis*; Hebrew: *Yesh*.</note> out of **NON-BEING**. But in truth, this is not a true or perfect privation <note>term: <term>Privation</term> refers to the total absence of a quality.</note>, since that thing which occurs is not made from the thing to which it occurs <note>The author is arguing that creation "out of nothing" doesn't mean "from a void," but from a source so high it is incomprehensible.</note>. How much more so is **BEING** not made from...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of Job 28:13-15. It discusses the "Abyss" (Tehom) and the "Supreme Crown" (Keter Elyon), arguing that the internal logic or "order" of Wisdom (Chokhmah) is hidden even within the highest emanations of the divine.</meta>

...the abyss of the **SUPREME CROWN** <term>Keter Elyon: the highest of the ten Sefirot, representing the Divine Will</term>; we will not be able to grasp it, because the Abyss testifies of itself that within it there is no boundary for its being grasped. This is intended to point out that within the **SUPREME CROWN** there is no grasping of the order of **WISDOM**. If this is the case, how then can one who desires to grasp **WISDOM** grasp it through the abyss? And the abyss is like the three heads of the Bull in the **Work of Creation** <term>Maaseh Bereshit: the esoteric study of the origins of the universe</term>, that is, the face of a man, the face of a lion, and the face of an eagle <note>The author is referencing the four living creatures of the Divine Chariot in Ezekiel; here, the "Abyss" seems to represent the hidden dimension alongside these visible manifestations</note>. Behold, in the *Paths* <note>Referring to the "Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom" from the Sefer Yetzirah</note> I have explained the mystery of the abyss and its essence. If, however, we proceed to examine what is drawn out, what is brought down, what emanates, or what proceeds from the **SUPREME CROWN**—in order to know how the order of **WISDOM** exists within the **SUPREME CROWN**—we will still not be able to grasp its existence. For **WISDOM** is a sea, and a sea of such a kind that it has no limit. Therefore, it also testifies of itself that its order is not within it. If this is how things stand, how then shall we be able to reach the goal of investigating it? *Pure gold shall not be given for it* <note>Quoting Job 28:15</note>. This refers to the purest and cleanest gold. That is to say: If we proceed to take its order in the **SUPREME CROWN** from the side of **STRENGTH** <term>Gevurah: the Sefirah of judgment and power</term> which is in the **SUPREME CROWN**, insofar as it proceeds from the **SUPREME CROWN**, it is called *Sgôr* <note>original Hebrew: סגור, "closely shut gold"</note>, which means *Ne'elam* <note>original Hebrew: נעלם</note>, or "hidden." *Neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof*, which refers to the **MERCY** <term>Chesed: the Sefirah of loving-kindness</term> that proceeds from the **SUPREME CROWN**; that is, even from the side of that **MERCY**, it cannot be reached. *It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir*. And if we attempt to examine the order of **WISDOM** through **BEAUTY** <term>Tiferet: the Sefirah of harmony and balance</term> which is assimi—

...is likened to the most precious gold of **Ophir** <note>original: "auro Ophir"; a legendary region famous for its high-quality gold</note>: for it is similar on the part of the origin of **Judgment** <term>Din: the divine attribute of justice or restraint</term> which will one day be drawn into it from the **SUPREME CROWN** <term>Keter: the highest Sefirah, representing the primordial Divine Will</term> regarding the precious Onyx and Sapphire. And since in the enumeration of **BEAUTY** <term>Tiferet: the central Sefirah that balances Mercy and Judgment</term> there are two causes for itself and for the inferior **DIADEM** <term>Malchut: the final Sefirah, through which the divine light enters the physical world</term>, which is closest to the first creation, for that reason he also multiplied the comparisons in this place: Gold (of **GLORY**) <term>Hod: the eighth Sefirah</term> which comes from the **SUPREME CROWN** shall not equal it. Nor shall Crystal (of **ETERNITY** or **TRIUMPH**) <term>Netzach: the seventh Sefirah</term>, which comes from the **SUPREME CROWN**. Nor shall its exchange be a vessel of **Pure Gold** <note>original: "Obryzo"; highly refined gold</note>, on the part of the **FOUNDATION** <term>Yesod: the ninth Sefirah, which gathers and funnels the higher energies</term>, which comes from the **SUPREME CROWN**. Through all these properties and attributes, the **CAUSE of WISDOM** <term>Chokhmah: the second Sefirah, representing pure intuitive thought</term> shall not be known, nor its order—namely, how it exists within the **SUPREME CROWN**. Regarding the Sublimity and Highness of **WISDOM**, others have rendered these as Coral and Pearl <note>original: "Coralle & Vnio"; referring to the Hebrew words 'Ramoth' and 'Gabish' in Job 28:18</note>; whether they have an order in the **SUPREME CROWN** shall not be mentioned, because we consider it unlawful for us to wish to scrutinize this most profound level of mysteries, as we shall teach in its proper place, namely: *IF THY HEART RUNS, RETURN TO THE PLACE* <note>original: "SI CVRRET COR TVVM REVERTERE AD LOCVM"; a famous instruction from the Sefer Yetzirah (1:8) regarding the limits of mystical contemplation</note>. But the drawing out of **WISDOM** from the **CAUSE OF CAUSES**, which is perceived in the **SUPREME CROWN**, is valued above pearls. Because just as He is not perceived except by Himself, so also **WISDOM** is not perceived except by itself. And **Sublimity** (Highness) <note>original: "ראמות" (Ramoth)</note> is derived from the word *Rum* <note>meaning 'to be high' or 'exalted'</note> according to this: *The height lifted up its hands* (Habakkuk 3:10) <note>original: "רום ידיהו נשא" (Rum yadehu nasa)</note>. This is as if he were saying of the sublimity of the **SUPREME CROWN** that neither the investigator nor the seeker...

It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir—if we investigate the value of **Wisdom** from within the [lower] things that are compared to the gold of Ophir, it is likened to the side of the source of **Judgment** <term>Din</term> that is destined to be drawn to it from the **Supreme Crown** <term>Keter</term>, like the precious Onyx and Sapphire. Because there are in **Beauty** <term>Tiferet</term> two causes for its own essence and for the **Crown** <term>Atarah/Malchut</term> that is attached to the first creation. Therefore, he increased the comparisons in this place: Gold shall not equal it—referring to **Glory** <term>Hod</term> which comes from the **Supreme Crown**; and glass—referring to **Victory/Eternity** <term>Netzach</term> which comes from the **Supreme Crown**; and the exchange of vessels of fine gold—on the side of **Foundation** <term>Yesod</term> which comes from the **Supreme Crown**. In all these attributes, the cause of **Wisdom** and its value in the **Supreme Crown** is not known, [namely] what it is. As for "Highness" and "Crystal" <note>referring to Job 28:18</note> of **Wisdom**, do they have a value in the **Supreme Crown**? No, it shall not be mentioned. For at this level it is forbidden to investigate, as we have learned in its place: *If your heart runs, return to the place.* However, the drawing of **Wisdom** is [valued] more than pearls, coming from the **Cause of Causes** which is intellectually grasped in the **Supreme Crown**. And just as He is not grasped by another, so **Wisdom** is not grasped by another. And the word *Ramoth* (Highness) comes from the expression *Rum* (height), as it is written: *The height lifted up its hands*, which means the exaltedness of the **Supreme Crown**; no seeker or requester is permitted to contemplate there. However, "Crystal" (*Gabish*) means "High-Is" <note>original: "גב-יש" (Gav-Yesh); a wordplay breaking the word into 'Back/Height' and 'There is' or 'Substance'</note>...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Job 28, specifically focusing on the metaphysical interpretation of verse 18 ("No mention shall be made of coral [gabish] or crystal") and verse 19 ("The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it"). It explores the etymology of the Hebrew word 'Gabish' and links it to the emanations of the Sefirot, particularly how the divine light transitions from 'Non-Being' to 'Being'.</meta>

...is one who is allowed to search there: Truly **Gabish** <note>original: "גביש"; often translated as 'coral' or 'crystal'</note> (*eminence, highness*) is a word composed of the word **Gav**, which signifies *back* or *ridge*, and the word **Yesh**, which signifies **Being** <term>Ens: the fundamental state of existence or reality</term>, as if it said **Gav-Yesh**, that is, the **Back of Being** <note>original: "גב-יש" / "Dorsum Entis"</note>. I mean the highest summit of **Being**, and how that **Being** proceeds from **Non-Being** <term>Non-Ente: 'Ayin' or 'Nothingness', representing the infinite source before manifestation</term>, that is, from infinity. *The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it* <note>Job 28:19</note>. Because the stone of paleness, which is also called the line of paleness, says: *If you presume to search the order* of **Wisdom** <term>Sapientia: the Sefirah Chokhmah</term> in the **Supreme Crown** <term>Corona Summa: the Sefirah Keter</term> through the line of paleness (he wishes to point to **Intelligence** <term>Intelligentia: the Sefirah Binah</term>) which proceeds from **Wisdom**, *you will not be able to*. Indeed, they called it the **Stone of Ethiopia**, because this most precious stone of paleness is brought from there. And in this way, this above-named stone of **Ethiopia** represents that mystery to us: *He made darkness his hiding place* <note>Psalm 18:11</note>. And darkness is rightly compared to the word **Kush** (*Ethiopia*) because darkness is black. Therefore he says, out of that darkness—which is most pure, most clean, most clear, and most splendid—how that **Topaz** emanates and proceeds from them; yet we still cannot grasp the order of **Wisdom** from this side, namely how it exists in the **Supreme Crown**. Therefore he goes no further and says, *And it shall not be valued with pure gold*, that is, it shall not be equaled: therefore he says: *Pure gold shall not be given for it, and silver shall not be weighed for its price.* The **Translator Onkelos** <note>Onkelos: author of the famous Aramaic translation (Targum) of the Torah</note> rendered this in clearly the same words, namely, *Pure gold shall not be given for it,*

The celestial **Gabish** <note>original: "גביש"</note> of **Being** <term>Yesh</term>: how **Being** is renewed from **Non-Being** <term>Ayin: the void or nothingness from which creation emerges</term>. *The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it.* For the green stone which is called the **Green Line** <note>original: "Kav Yarok"; a Kabbalistic concept representing the light that encircles the world and distinguishes the physical from the spiritual</note> says: if you come to investigate the value of **Wisdom** <term>Chokhmah</term> in the **Crown** <term>Keter</term> from within the **Green Line**—which refers to **Understanding** <term>Binah</term> spreading out from **Wisdom**—you will not be able to. And they said **Ethiopia** <note>original: "Kush"</note> because that green stone has its origin there. And he said that from that pure, refined, and clean darkness, when the **Topaz** is emanated from it, one still cannot take the measure of **Wisdom** from the side of how it exists in the **Crown**. And regarding this, the translation says: *pure gold shall not be given in its place, and silver shall not be weighed as its price; refined gold shall not be given in exchange for it, nor shall weighed silver be its price; it shall not be exchanged for the pure gold of Ophir, nor for the precious onyx and sapphire.* <note>The Hebrew text ends with an Aramaic paraphrase of Job 28:15-16</note>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Job 28, transitioning from the symbolic meaning of "Ethiopia" (darkness/blackness) to the metaphysical value of Wisdom. It contrasts the physical wealth of gold and gems with the spiritual emanation of Wisdom from the "Supreme Crown."</meta>

*And its exchange shall not be weighed with silver.* It shall not be exchanged for the most precious gold of Ophir, nor with precious Onyx and Sapphire. Another Paraphrast <note>original: "Paraphraftes"; referring to the Targum, the Aramaic translation of the Bible</note> says: a rich man shall not equal it with gold and crystal, nor shall he give vessels of the purest gold for it. And another Paraphrast says: It is impossible for it to be found in "cheapness," that is, at a low price. But it is found in "preciousness," just as gold is; and whoever does not guard it perishes and is shattered like crystal. And the exchange of its reward in the future world <term>futuro feculo: the World to Come or Olam Ha-Ba</term> is vessels of the purest gold. *Coral and crystal shall not be mentioned, and the draw of* **Wisdom** *is beyond pearls.* Coral and crystal shall not be commemorated, and the draw of **Wisdom** is beyond pearls. *The Emerald of Ethiopia shall not equal it, nor shall it be valued with pure gold.* The Paraphrast says: The Emerald that comes from Ethiopia shall not equal it, nor shall it be exchanged for pure gold. After, therefore, he has explained to you that the investigation of **Wisdom** <term>Sapientia: the Sefirah Chokhmah</term> and the apprehension of it is forbidden—that is to say, its arrangement in the **Supreme Crown** <term>Corona Svmma: the Sefirah Keter</term>—he returns and explains to you that if anyone even wished to scrutinize its entity in itself, and how it receives emanation and influence from the **Supreme Crown**, he says that even this is forbidden to human apprehension. And this is exactly what the Scripture says in Job chapter 28, verse 20: *And Wisdom proceeds from* **Nothingness** <note>original: "מאין" (m'Ayin); usually translated as "from where," but interpreted here as "from the state of Non-Being"</note>, that is, from the **Supreme Crown**. And the letters **Aleph** and **Yod** <note>original: "א'י"; the first two letters of the word "Ayin" (Nothingness)</note> are the lo— <note>The Latin text cuts off; the catchword "cus" implies the word "locus" (place).</note>

<column-break/>

Another translation: A rich man cannot set it in order with gold and crystal, nor can he give in its exchange vessels of refined gold. The translation says: it is not possible that it be found in cheapness, but rather in preciousness like gold. And for one who does not guard it, it goes away and is broken like glass; and the reward's fruit for the world to come is vessels of fine gold. Coral and crystal shall not be mentioned, and the draw of **Wisdom** is beyond pearls; and precious stones and gems shall not be remembered, and in the drawing of **Wisdom** from pearls, it shall not be compared. The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it; with pure gold it shall not be weighed. A variant says: the green pearl that comes from Ethiopia shall not be raised up [in value] with pure gold, nor shall it be exchanged. After he explained to you the prevention of **Wisdom** and its attainment—that is, its value in the **Crown**—he returned and explained to you that even after one who wishes to investigate its essence in itself, how it receives emanation and abundance from the **Supreme Crown**, he said that even this is prevented from being attained. ## RITTANGELIUS.

*It should be noted here in passing that the Hebrews, through these three terms* **WAS, IS, and WILL BE** <note>original: "Heiyah, Hoveh, ve-Yihyeh"</note> *express three modes of existing in the divinity, because each one of them is capable of signifying the entire divine essence. Specifically, by this reasoning, if you join the first letter 'vav' from the second word "and he is" <note>original: "ve-hoveh"</note> with the word "he was" <note>original: "heiyah"</note>, you have all the letters of the **Tetragrammaton** <term>The Tetragrammaton: The sacred four-letter Name of God (YHWH)</term>; again, if you join one redundant 'yod' from the third word "and he will be" <note>original: "ve-yihyeh"</note> with the second word "he is" <note>original: "hoveh"</note>, you have the **Tetragrammaton** again, just as in the third word itself, nothing remains except the **Tetragrammaton**.*

<summary>This page discusses the mystical relationship between existence (Being) and the divine source (Non-Being), while explaining how the Hebrew words for "past, present, and future" encode the secret four-letter Name of God.</summary>

In the *Tikkunei Zohar* <note>original: "Tykun." — a classic 14th-century Kabbalistic text composed of seventy commentaries on the first word of Genesis</note>, chapter 28, page 73, column 2; and chapter 55, page 122, column 1, Rabbi Simeon son of Yochai <note>the traditional 2nd-century sage to whom the Zohar is attributed</note> says that the **Head** is the **Crown** <term>Corona: the Sephirah Keter, representing the divine will</term>, the **Highest Point**. The **Brain** is **Wisdom** <term>Sapientia: the Sephirah Chokhmah</term>; in **Understanding** <term>Intelligentia: the Sephirah Binah</term> is the **Heart of the Understanding**. The two arms are **Mercy** <term>Misericordia: the Sephirah Chesed</term> and **Strength** <term>Fortitudo: the Sephirah Gevurah</term>.
The **Body** is the **Middle Column** <note>representing Tiferet, which balances mercy and judgment</note>.
The two legs are **Victory** <note>original: "Triumphus seu Æternitas" referring to the Sephirah Netzach</note> and **Glory** <note>original: "Gloria" referring to the Sephirah Hod</note>. The **Foundation** <term>Fundamentum: the Sephirah Yesod</term> is the **Mother**. **Divinity** <note>original: "Divinitas," likely referring to the Shekhinah, the indwelling presence of God</note> is its sign.
The **Crown** is called the "Highest God" who possesses **Wisdom and Understanding**. The phrase "Our God" signifies **Understanding**, while "the God of our fathers" signifies **Wisdom**. And this is the same as: "The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob." "The Great God" is from the aspect of **Magnificence** <term>Magnificentia: another name for the Sephirah Chesed</term>; "the Strong" is from the aspect of **Strength**; and "the Formidable" is from the aspect of the **Middle Column**.

Moses Botril <note>original: "Moſeh Botril" — a 14th-century Spanish scholar and commentator on mystical texts</note>, page 39, column 4, chapter 1, section 4 of the **Book of Formation** <note>original: "libri Iezirah" — the Sefer Yetzirah</note>: **WISDOM** <term>Sapientia: the Sephirah Chochmah</term> is the second **Enumeration** <term>Numeratio: a Sephirah or divine emanation</term>; because above it is the **HIGHEST CROWN** <term>Corona Summa: the Sephirah Keter</term> which is **MIND** <note>original: "Mens," translating the Hebrew "Machshavah" or Thought</note>, and that is called the first **Enumeration**, and even unbidden by us, **WISDOM** proceeds from the **MIND**.

Rabbi Abraham ben David <note>original: "R. Abraham F. D." — the Raavad</note>, page 29, column 3, chapter 1, section 2 of the **Book of Formation**: The upper **Yod** <note>The Hebrew letter Yod (י), which represents a single point and is associated with the beginning of creation</note>, he says, which encompasses all essences that were created as **BEING** out of **NON-BEING** <note>original: "ENS de NON-ENTE," referring to the concept of *Yesh mi-Ayin* (Creation ex nihilo)</note>, indicates that immediately the ten expansions of the firmament were divided from one another in the midst of the **Yod**, which emanated from that **Ineffable One** <note>The Ein Sof, or the Infinite Godhead</note>; he means to say, from the **HIGHEST CROWN**, which has no "quiddity" <term>Quidditas: the "whatness" or defining essence of a thing</term>. However, to the **Yod** itself, there is a Quiddity, and for that reason it is called **WISDOM** <note>Hebrew: חכמה — Chochmah</note>, which is to say: (a) the **palate** <note>Hebrew: חך — Chekh</note> says **something** <note>Hebrew: מה — Mah; a mystical etymology where Chochmah is broken into "the palate speaks of what/something," signifying the first point of definable existence</note>. And all things mentioned in the Law, the Prophets, and the Hagiographis <note>The Ketuvim or "Writings," the third section of the Hebrew Bible</note> allude to **WISDOM**, just as it is said in Psalm 104, verse 24: *How magnified are your works, O Lord! You have made them all in* **WISDOM**; *the earth is full of your possessions*: alluding to all the essences which are outlined and shaped in **WISDOM**, as we have indicated above. But the **HIGHEST CROWN**, which is called **NON-BEING** <note>Hebrew: אין — Ayin</note>, is also called and denotes that **Ineffable One**.

Moses Botril, page 39, column 4, chapter 1, teaching 4 of the **Book of Formation**: Wisdom is the second Sephirah, for above it is the Crown, which is Thought, and it is called the first Sephirah; and of necessity, Wisdom emerges from Thought.

The Raavad, page 29, column 3, chapter 1, teaching 2 of the **Book of Formation**: The upper **Yod**, which encompasses all existences that were created as "something from nothing," hints that the ten heavens were immediately separated from one another through the **Yod**, which is emanated from the "Without-Whatness" <note>original: "מבלי מ"ה" — a reference to the Infinite</note>, meaning from the Crown which has no essence. However, the **Yod** does have an essence, and therefore it is called **Wisdom** <note>Chochmah</note>, as if to say "the palate [Chekh] said what [Mah]." And everything mentioned in the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings hints at Wisdom, as it is said: *How manifold are Your works, O Lord, in Wisdom You have made them all, the earth is full of Your acquisitions,* to hint at all the existences that are formed in Wisdom, as we hinted above. But the Crown, which is called "Nothing" <note>Ayin</note>, is called "Without-Ending" <note>Belimah</note>.

And further, regarding **Let us make man**, to whom did He say this? And a little later: He who said: **Let us make man** is <note>original Hebrew: יוד הי ואו הי — the letters Yod, He, Vav, He</note>.

# RITTANGEL

<column-break/>

[WISDOM], *he says*, is called the beginning, just as Scripture testifies: *The beginning of WISDOM is the fear of the Lord* <note>original Latin: "Principium, SAPIENTIA, timor Domini"; referencing Psalm 111:10</note>, because it is the beginning of all existing things. It relates to them just as matter relates to form, and as the point—which is the letter Yod <note>The Hebrew letter י, the smallest character, symbolizing the infinitesimal point from which all creation starts</note>—is the beginning of all letters. And this is the mystery of which Scripture says: *I am the first and I am the last* (Isaiah 44:6). It is justly and deservedly called the beginning, because it is BEING from NON-BEING <term>Ens de Non-Ente: the mystical transition from the absolute "Nothing" (Ayin) to the first "Something" (Yesh)</term>. 

But truly, as far as entity is concerned, the beginning is the origin of number. Furthermore, in the mystery of NON-BEING, number is not included. (*This is because that which lacks beginning and end does not fall under the category of dimensional quantity.*) Therefore, since beginning and end fall under the definition of dimensional quantity, it was necessary to indicate to you that you should not say in this place, or in any way call it dimensional quantity properly and absolutely, but rather "depth"; and for that reason he called it depth. 

As if he were saying: regarding the depth of the beginning—that is, of WISDOM—there is no dimension. And thus it is for each of the ten depths, which are the THREE INTELLECTUAL ENUMERATIONS <term>Numerationes Intellectuales: the first three Sefirot (Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah) representing the "brain" or intellect of the divine structure</term> and the seven ENUMERATIONS which are called "changes" *or attributes*. Nor does one of these depend on that—*namely*, on dimensional quantity—because all these DEPTHS are drawn from the SUPREME MIND, of which Scripture says in Psalm 92: *Your thoughts are very deep...*

<column-break/>

Beginning, he said, is Wisdom, as it is said: *The beginning of Wisdom is the fear of the Lord.* For it is the beginning of all existing things, and it is—as it were—like matter to form, and like the point which is the letter Yod, which is the beginning of all letters. And this is the secret of *I am first and I am last*. 

And it is worthy to be called "first" because it is Being from Nothing. And within Being there is a beginning of number, for number cannot be grasped in the secret of Nothingness. And because "beginning" and "end" fall within the definition of measurement, he needed to tell you that you should not attribute actual measurement to it; therefore he used the term "depth." 

The explanation: the depth of the beginning has no measurement. And so it is for each and every one of these ten depths. The explanation: there are three intellectual Sefirot <term>Sefirot: the ten divine attributes or channels through which God interacts with the universe</term> and seven Sefirot which are called "transformations." None of them have measurement attached to them, for all the depths are drawn from the Supreme Thought <note>Hebrew: Machshavah</note>, as it is said: *Your thoughts are very deep.* And Thought has no end; therefore all the depths have no end. 

And after this he said: it is known that the circle has no beginning or end from the side of... <note>This Hebrew text breaks off mid-sentence at the bottom of the page</note>

(*This is because that which lacks a beginning and end does not fall under the category of dimensional quantity.*) Therefore, since beginning and end fall under the definition of dimensional quantity, it was necessary to point out to you that you should not say or in any way call it "dimensional quantity" in a proper or absolute sense in this place, but rather "depth," and for that reason he called it "depth." It is as if he were saying that for the depth of the beginning—that is, WISDOM—there is no dimension. And so it is for each of the ten depths, which are THREE INTELLECTUAL ENUMERATIONS <term>Numerationes: the three highest Sefirot—Keter, Chokhmah, and Binah—associated with divine intellect</term> and seven ENUMERATIONS, which are called *changes or attributes* <note>The lower seven Sefirot related to emotions and action</note>. Nor does one of these depend on that—namely, dimensional quantity. Because all these DEPTHS are drawn from the SUPREME MIND, of which Scripture says in *Psalm 92: Your thoughts are very deep*—

<column-break/>

He said the "beginning" is Wisdom, as it is said: *The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord,* for it is the beginning of all existing things. It is like the matter to the form, and like the point which is the letter *Yod* (י), which is the beginning of all the letters. And this is the secret of *I am the first and I am the last*. It is fitting that it be called "first" because it is Being from Nothing. In the state of "being," it is the beginning of number, for number cannot be grasped in the secret of "Nothing" <note>Hebrew: *Ayin*, referring to the infinite void or the most hidden aspect of God</note>. And because beginning and end fall within the definition of "measure," it was necessary to tell you that you should not attribute literal measure to it; therefore he said "depth." The explanation is that the depth of the beginning has no measure. And so it is for each and every one of these ten depths: meaning, three intellectual Sefirot and seven Sefirot which are called "Changes" <note>Hebrew: *Temurot*</note>. None of them have [measure] attached to them, because all the depths are drawn from the Supreme Thought, as it is said: *Your thoughts are very deep.* And thought has no end; therefore all the depths have no end. And after this he said: "And it is known that the circle has no beginning or end from the side of—"

<meta>This page continues the commentary by Rabbi Abraham ben David (the Ra'avad) on the *Sefer Yetzirah* (Book of Formation). It explores the metaphysical relationship between the first three Sefirot: the Supreme Crown (Keter), Wisdom (Chokhmah), and Understanding (Binah), focusing on the concept of divine unity and the philosophical problem of assigning numbers or qualities to the Infinite.</meta>

We are accustomed to speak of it as duality, as if **Duality** were the foundation of the universe. Others, however, have interpreted these words—*The Lord is supremely one and there is no other or second to Him*—in this manner: that the *Lord*, who is **WISDOM** <note>original Latin: *Sapientia*; Hebrew: *Chokhmah*</note>, is supremely one; **UNDERSTANDING** <note>original: *Intelligentia*; Hebrew: *Binah*</note> "is not to Him" (as if **NON-BEING** <note>original: *Non-Ens*; Hebrew: *Ayin*</note>) to the **SUPREME CROWN**; "another or second" is the **CAUSE OF CAUSES**.

Because **UNDERSTANDING** receives the thread of its emanation or its process from **WISDOM**, because **WISDOM** is supremely one within **UNDERSTANDING**, or is supremely united to **UNDERSTANDING**. The **SUPREME CROWN** <note>original: *Corona Summa*; Hebrew: *Keter*</note>, however, is called **Non-Being**; that is, for that **NON-BEING**—which I call the **CAUSE OF CAUSES**—there is no other second cause for its existence; because it itself is the cause of its own existence in a cause that is most absolute and simple. *But before the number of unity, what can you count?* <note>A famous quote from Sefer Yetzirah 1:4</note> It is as if he were saying: The boundary of number does not apply except to a thing which has entity <gloss>being</gloss>, but not to a thing which is **Non-Being**. But insofar as it equals all things, it is for that reason called "one." *Wherefore also before the number of unity, what can you count?* Since even the number of unity is not correctly attributed to the **SUPREME CROWN** either, except insofar as it is the most perfect equation <note>original: *aequatio*; Hebrew: *hashva'ah*, referring to a state of absolute balance or indistinguishability where all things are "equalized"</note>: and not from the perspective of dimension or number, which is placed within the category of quantity.

If this is how things stand, what word or what term could be attributed to the **CAUSE OF CAUSES**, so that it might be truly and worthily predicated of it? In truth, the term "equation," which in this place...

<column-break/>

...in it there is no duality at all. And some say that the Lord (**Wisdom**) is unique (**Understanding**) and has no (**Understanding**) second (**the Cause of Causes**). Because Understanding receives the thread of Wisdom from [it], for Wisdom in Understanding is unique. And the **Supreme Crown** is called "has no," meaning for the **Cause of Causes** there is no second for its existence, because He is the cause of His existence in a simple cause. 

*And before one, what can you count?* The explanation is: for the name of number does not fall <gloss>apply</gloss> except upon a thing that has being <note>Hebrew: *yeshut*</note>, and not upon a thing of **Nothingness** <note>Hebrew: *Ayin*</note>, except that it is the equalization <note>Hebrew: *hashva'ah*</note> of all; and therefore it is called "one" from this perspective. *And before one, what can you count?*—after [considering] that even the number "one" is not appropriate to say even regarding the **Supreme Crown**, except from the perspective that it is complete equality, and not from the perspective of measure and number, which is within the category of Wisdom. 

If so, what thing or word would be worthy to be believed <gloss>predicated</gloss> concerning the **Cause of Causes**? However, my saying "equality" regarding the **Supreme Crown**—the meaning of equality mentioned is not one of the matters of quality, for quality only falls upon a body, and it is also an accident <note>In medieval philosophy, an "accident" (accidens) is a property that can change or be absent without the substance losing its identity; the author argues God has no such properties.</note>.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the three highest emanations of the Divine, known as the Sefirot. We are accustomed to say of it that duality exists, as if **Duality** were the foundation of the universe. But others have interpreted these words—*The Lord is supremely one, and there is no other or second to Him*—in this manner: that the **LORD** is <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Sapientia" / Hebrew: "Chokhmah"</note>, **supremely one** is <term>Intelligence</term> <note>original: "Intelligentia" / Hebrew: "Binah"</note>, and **There is none to Him** (as if he were **NON-BEING**) refers to the <term>Supreme Crown</term> <note>original: "Corona Summa" / Hebrew: "Keter Elyon". This is because **Intelligence** receives the thread of its emanation or process from **Wisdom**, for the reason that **Wisdom** is supremely one within **Intelligence**, or is supremely united to **Intelligence**. The **Supreme Crown**, however, is called **NON-BEING**; that is to say, there is no other second cause for the existence of this **NON-BEING**, I say, for this **CAUSE OF CAUSES**. This is because it is the cause of its own existence within the most absolute and simple cause.

*Before the number of unity, what can you count?* It is as if one were saying: The limit of number does not apply except to a thing which has "entity" (being), but not to a thing which is **NON-BEING**. However, insofar as it levels and equates all things, it is therefore called "one." *Therefore, even before the number of unity, what could you count?* After all, the number of unity is not rightly attributed to the **SUPREME CROWN** either, except insofar as it is the most perfect "equation" <note>The author uses "equatio" or "aequatio" to describe a state of perfect balance or equilibrium where all possibilities exist in potentiality before they are differentiated.</note>; it is not from the perspective of dimension or number, which is placed in the category of quantity.

<column-break/>

In it, duality is the entire root. And it is said that the **Lord** (**Wisdom**) is **unique** (**Intelligence**) and **there is none to Him** (**Supreme Crown**) **second** (**Cause of Causes**). For **Intelligence** receives the thread of **Wisdom**, because **Wisdom** is unique within **Intelligence**.

The **Supreme Crown** is called **Nothingness** <note>original: "Ayin"</note>; it is explained that there is no **second** for the existence of the **Cause of Causes**, because it is the cause of its own existence in the Simple Cause.

*Before one, what do you count?* The explanation is that the name of "number" will not fall except upon a thing that has "being" <note>original: "yeshut"</note>, and not upon a thing that is **Nothingness**. It is only because it is the **Equating** <note>original: "hashva'ah"</note> of all things that it is called "One" from this perspective.

*Before one, what do you count?* Since even the number "one" is not appropriate to say even of the **Supreme Crown**, except from the perspective that it is **Total Equality**, and not from the perspective of measure and number, which are included within **Wisdom**. If so, what thing or word would be worthy to be believed concerning the **Cause of Causes**? Truly, when I say "**Equality**" regarding the **Supreme Crown**, the meaning of this "Equality" is not one of the categories of **Quality**; for Quality only applies to a physical body, and it is also an accident <note>In medieval philosophy, a "quality" or "accident" is a characteristic that describes a physical thing (like being red or heavy), which the author argues cannot apply to the purely spiritual Divine.</note>.

It interprets the oneness of God as a philosophical unity where Wisdom and Intelligence are perfectly joined.</summary>

# R I T T A N G E L <note>Johannes Stephanus Rittangel (1606–1652) was a professor of Oriental languages who sought to demonstrate that the roots of Christian doctrine, like the Trinity, could be found in ancient Jewish mystical texts.</note>

The author reports that the royal prophet David raised his mind in the Holy Spirit to the most holy **Trinity**. He suggests that the mystery of the most holy **Trinity** can be drawn from the initial letters of these three words—**Because he has set his love upon me** <note>Hebrew: "Ki Bi Chashaq"</note>—in such a way that these three words of the verse enjoy the same initial letters as the three attributed names of the most holy **Trinity**: **Crown** <note>Hebrew: "Keter"</note> (the highest), **Wisdom** <note>Hebrew: "Chokhmah"</note>, and **Intelligence** <note>Hebrew: "Binah"</note>. For example, in the phrase **Because he has set his love upon me**: the first word, **Because** <note>Hebrew: "Ki"</note>, begins with the letter **K** <note>The Hebrew letter Kaf (כ)</note>, just as **Crown** <note>Keter</note> does. The second word, **in me** <note>Hebrew: "Bi"</note>, begins with the letter **B** <note>The Hebrew letter Bet (ב)</note>, just like **Intelligence** <note>Binah</note>. The third word, **he has set his love** <note>Hebrew: "Chashaq"</note>, begins with the letter **Ch** <note>The Hebrew letter Chet (ח)</note>, which is the same letter that begins **Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah</note>. See how all the initial letters of these three words from this verse of Psalm 91 are the same as those with which the three attributed names of the most holy **Trinity** begin.

# RITTANGELIUS
<note>Johann Stephan Rittangel (1606–1652) was a professor of Oriental languages and a convert from Judaism to Christianity who sought to prove Christian doctrines from Jewish texts like the Sefer Yetzirah.</note>

The same Mystery of the **Work of the Chariot** <term>Work of the Chariot: *Ma'aseh Merkabah* in Hebrew. This refers to the mystical study of the vision of Ezekiel and the celestial hierarchy. In order to express the Three modes of subsistence in one and the same divine essence, he does not use a single term as the Hebrew text does, but rather describes their distinct acts and properties through three distinct names: the first under **יהוה** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter sacred name of God.</note> (the Name of the Tetragrammaton); the second under **Memra** <note>original Aramaic: מימרא</note>, which signifies the "Word of God"; and the Third mode of subsistence under the term **Shekhinah** <note>original Aramaic: שכינתא</note> (the Divine Presence). Regarding the first mode of subsistence, the Chaldean <note>Commonly used in this period to refer to Aramaic, the language of the Targums.</note> rendered the Hebrew **יהוה** (Tetragrammaton) through the abbreviation **יי** <note>The double-yod abbreviation for the divine name.</note>, which carries the same sound as the Tetragrammaton, as is clear from the following two-column series; for I have decided that it would be wise to bring forward some testimonies of Holy Scripture out of many.

### Targum
<note>The *Targum* is the Aramaic translation and paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible. Christian Hebraists like Rittangel studied it closely, believing its use of the "Word" (Memra) pointed toward the Christian Logos.</note>

### Mikra
<note>*Mikra* refers to the original Hebrew text of the Bible as it is read and chanted.</note>

1 And the LORD **appeared** to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat at the door of the tent etc.

### *The Chaldaic Paraphrase.*
<note>This refers to the *Targum*, the Aramaic translation. The "Paraphrast" mentioned is usually Onkelos, whose version was highly authoritative in Jewish and Christian scholarship.</note>

1 And the **LORD was revealed** to him in the plains of Mamre, and he was sitting at the door of the tent. <note>original Latin: *Revelatus est*. Notice how the Aramaic changes "appeared" to "was revealed" to emphasize God's spiritual nature over physical sight.</note>

2 And let them be ready for the third day; because on the third day the **LORD will be revealed** in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai.

3 And the **LORD was revealed** upon Mount Sinai, upon the top of the mountain: and the **LORD called** to Moses at the top of the mountain: and Moses went up.

4 And the **LORD was revealed** in a cloud and spoke with him.

5 I am the **LORD your God**, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.

---

Finally, having dispatched these matters, we hasten to the second mode of existence, which the Paraphrast Onkelos, as well as others, described through the **Memra of the Lord** <note>original: *מימרא יהוה*. This is a central concept for Rittangel; he identifies this "Word" (Memra) with the Christian Logos or the second person of the Trinity.</note> (the Word of the Tetragrammaton).

<summary>This page presents a side-by-side comparison of the Hebrew Bible and the Aramaic Targum, demonstrating how the Aramaic translation replaces physical actions of God (like "descending") with the term "revealed." Rittangel uses this to introduce the concept of the "Memra" or "Word of the Lord" as a distinct divine manifestation.</summary>

-># Bible Translation<-

### *The Aramaic Paraphrase*
<note>This column contains the Targum, an Aramaic translation used in synagogues to explain the Hebrew text. It often adds the word "Memra" (the Word) when God interacts with the physical world.</note>

1 And Jacob vowed a vow, saying: "If the **Word** <note>Aramaic: *Memra*. A technical term used to represent God’s manifestation or agency in the world without implying a physical form.</note> of the LORD will be my support, and will guard me on this way that I am going, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear, and I return in peace to my father's house, then the **Word** of the LORD shall be my God."

2 And Laban said: "This heap is a witness between me and you this day." Therefore he called its name Galeed, and the *watchtower* <note>Aramaic: *sokhuta*, translating the Hebrew "Mizpah."</note>; for he said: "May the **Word** of the LORD watch between me and you when a man is hidden from his companion."

3 And the bondage of the children of Israel was revealed before the LORD; and the LORD said in His **Word** to redeem them. <note>The Aramaic adds "in His Word" and "to redeem them" to clarify God's intentional action.</note>

4 And as for us, what are we? Your grumblings are not against us, but against the **Word** of the LORD.

5 And Moses brought the people out to meet the **Word** of the LORD from the camp, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.

<column-break/>

### *The Hebrew Text*
<note>This column contains the original Hebrew verses from the Torah. These serves as the baseline for the comparison.</note>

1 And Jacob vowed a vow, saying: "If **God** will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat and a garment to put on, so that I come again to my father's house in peace, then the **LORD** shall be my God." <note>Genesis 28:20-21.</note>

2 And Laban said: "This heap is a witness between me and you today." Therefore was its name called Galeed; and Mizpah, for he said: "The **LORD** watch between me and you when we are absent from one another." <note>Genesis 31:48-49.</note>

3 And **God looked** upon the children of Israel, and **God knew**. <note>Exodus 2:25. The Aramaic version replaces "God looked/knew" with "it was revealed before the Lord."</note>

4 And what are we? Your grumblings are not against us, but against the **LORD**. <note>Exodus 16:8.</note>

5 And Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet **God**, and they stood at the foot of the mountain. <note>Exodus 19:17.</note>

<summary>This page presents side-by-side scriptural passages from Genesis and Exodus to demonstrate how the Aramaic Targums consistently substitute "the Word of the LORD" (Memra) for "God" or "the LORD" when describing divine interaction with humanity. This serves the author's argument regarding the Jewish theological effort to emphasize God's transcendence and avoid physical descriptions.</summary>

-># Biblical Comparisons<-

->### Hebrew Text. <column-break/> Aramaic Paraphrase.<-

1 **Genesis 28:20–21.** And Jacob vowed a vow, saying: "If **GOD** <note>original: "DEVS"</note> will be with me, and will guard me on this way that I am walking, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear, and I return in peace to my father's house, then the **LORD** <note>The Hebrew text uses the Tetragrammaton יהוה, the sacred four-letter name of God.</note> shall be my **GOD**."

2 **Genesis 31:48–49.** And Laban said: "This heap is a witness between me and you today," therefore he called its name Galeed and Mizpah <note>The Hebrew *Mizpah* means "watchtower."</note>; for he said, "May the **LORD** watch between me and you when we are hidden from one another."

3 **Exodus 2:25.** And God saw the children of Israel, and **GOD** took knowledge of them.

4 **Exodus 16:8.** And what are we? Your grumblings are not against us, but against the **LORD**.

5 **Exodus 19:17.** And Moses brought the people out **TO MEET GOD** from the camp, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.

<column-break/>

1 And Jacob vowed a vow, saying: "If the **WORD of the LORD** <note>original: "VERBVM יהוה". In Aramaic, this is the *Memra*, a term used to represent God’s active presence without implying a physical form.</note> will be with me, and will guard me on this way that I am walking, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear, and I return in peace to my father's house, then the **WORD of the LORD** shall be my God."

2 And Laban said: "This heap is a witness between me and you today," therefore he called its name Galeed and *Sakhutha* <note>The Aramaic term for "watchtower," corresponding to the Hebrew "Mizpah."</note>; for he said, "May the **WORD of the LORD** watch between me and you when we are hidden from one another."

3 And the subjection of the children of Israel was known before the **LORD**, and He said in **HIS WORD** to redeem them. <note>The Paraphrase adds "to redeem them" to explain that God's "knowing" implies an active intent to save.</note>

4 And what are we? Your grumblings are not against us, but against the **WORD of the LORD**.

5 And Moses brought the people out **TO MEET THE WORD OF THE LORD** from the camp, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.

->### Aramaic Paraphrase <column-break/> Hebrew Text<-

**6** Behold, I send an angel to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared. Be on guard before him and receive **his Word** <note>original Aramaic: *Memreiah*. The Aramaic shifts from "listening to his voice" to "receiving his Word."</note>; do not rebel against him, for he will not forgive your sins, for my name is in **his Word**. <column-break/> **6** Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place which I have prepared. Be on guard before him and listen to his voice; do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your transgressions, for my name is in **him**. <note>Exodus 23:20-21. Note how the Aramaic places God's name in the "Word" rather than in the angel itself.</note>

**7** And you shall not walk in the laws of the nations which I am exiling from before you; for they did all these things, and **my Word** distanced them. <column-break/> **7** And you shall not walk in the statutes of the nation which I am casting out before you; for they did all these things, and **I abhorred** them. <note>Leviticus 20:23. The Hebrew "abhorred" (*akuts*) is a strong emotional verb; the Aramaic replaces this with the "Word" distancing or rejecting them to avoid suggesting God feels human-like disgust.</note>

**8** These are the covenants, the ordinances, and the Law which the LORD gave between **his Word** and the children of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses. <column-break/> **8** These are the statutes and the ordinances and the laws which the LORD gave between **himself** and the children of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses. <note>Leviticus 26:46. The Aramaic inserts "His Word" as the intermediary for the covenant.</note>

**9** Because you have rejected **the Word of the LORD** whose **Presence** <note>original: *Shekhinteh*. This refers to the Divine Presence dwelling among the people.</note> dwells among you, and you wept before him, saying: "Why did we come out of Egypt?" <column-break/> **9** Because you have rejected **the LORD** who is **among you**, and you wept before him, saying: "Why did we come out of Egypt?" <note>Numbers 11:20.</note>

**10** I have looked and there are no worshipers of idols in the house of Jacob, and neither are there any who perform wearying falsehood in Israel; **the Word of the LORD** their God is their help, and the **Presence** <note>original: *Shekhinat*. This identifies the "shout" or "acclamation" of the King as the manifest Presence of God.</note> of their King is among them. <column-break/> **10** He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob, nor has he seen trouble in Israel; **the LORD** his God is with him, and the **shout** of a king is in him. <note>Numbers 23:21. The Aramaic "Word" and "Presence" replace the direct "God is with him."</note>

These substitutions serve to distance the Divine from human-like emotions and physical descriptions.</summary>

**6** Behold, I am sending an Angel before you to guard you on the way and to lead you to the place which I have prepared: Be on your guard against him, and listen to **his WORD** <note>original Latin: *verbum*; Aramaic: *Memra*. Here, the Aramaic identifies the authority as the "Word" of the angel/God rather than a physical voice.</note>; do not be rebellious toward him, because he will not dismiss your sins, because **IN MY NAME IS HIS WORD.**

**7** And you shall not walk in the statutes of the nation which I am sending out from before your faces. **9** Because you have rejected the **WORD** of the LORD <note>original: "יהוה"</note>, whose **DIVINITY** <note>original Latin: *Divinitas*; Aramaic: *Shekhinah*. ### Jerusalem Targum
<note>original: "תרגום ירושלמי" (Targum Yerushalmi). An ancient Aramaic translation and expansion of the Hebrew Bible that often adds interpretive details.</note>

2 And the Word of <term>the LORD</term> God called to Adam and said to him: "Behold, the world that I created is revealed before Me; darkness and light are revealed before Me, and how do you think that the place where you are hiding is not revealed before Me?" <note>The Targum expands the simple "Where are you?" into a theological statement about God's omniscience.</note>

3 And the Word of <term>the LORD</term> God said: "Behold, Adam, whom I created, is unique in the world, just as I am unique in the high heavens."

4 And the Word of <term>the LORD</term> remembered Rachel with His good mercies, and the Word of <term>the LORD</term> heard the sound of her prayer, and He said by His Word to give her children.

5 For this reason, the word of prophecy from before <term>the LORD</term> came to Abraham the righteous, and the Word of <term>the LORD</term> was revealed to him in the plains <note>of Mamre</note>, etc.

6 And the Word of <term>the LORD</term> caused to descend upon the people of Sodom and Gomorrah rains <note>of sulfur and fire</note>, etc.

### RITTANGEL.

And let these most powerful examples brought from Moses alone suffice: *as for the remaining Biblical passages, which this book could not contain, I omit their citation for the sake of brevity, and I refer the* Kind Reader *to their own investigation. However, so that the Kind Reader may be more certain that the passages cited above from the Chaldean paraphrase <note>Aramaic was often called "Chaldean" in the 17th century.</note> are the firmest bulwarks of our faith against the Jews, the Anti-Trinitarians <note>Groups who rejected the doctrine of the Trinity, such as the Socinians.</note>, and other attackers, I wanted to add, as a conclusion, a discourse which I recall having with a certain Anti-Trinitarian man, most skilled in Oriental languages, concerning this argument. And when he urged that not only where the Hebrew Text has* <term>the LORD</term> <note>original: יהוה</note> *the Chaldean has translated it* <term>the Word of the Lord</term> <note>Aramaic: מימרא דיי' - Memra d'Yeya</note> (*which sounds like the name* <term>the LORD</term>*): But also that the Hebrew word* <term>speech</term> <note>original: דבר - davar</note> *which signifies "discourse," was rendered as* <term>the Word of the Lord</term>, *that is, the "Word of the LORD"; and consequently, it would be clear that the term* <term>the Word</term> <note>Greek: τὸ מימרא</note> *does not speak of a certain way of existing within God <note>i.e., a person of the Trinity</note>, but is of the same meaning as* <term>speech</term> <note>original: davar</note> (*which denotes a spoken word*), *and signifies nothing else than absolutely the speech or talk of God or of any man; and he boasted that no matter how much effort, industry, or indeed my whole mind I applied for the sake of eliciting another meaning, I would labor in vain, and would be hunting no differently than "angry Delia" with "unwilling dogs." <note>A Latin idiom meaning to engage in a futile, frustrated effort.</note>* I answered and I answer: *First, it is false that where the Hebrew text has* <term>speech</term> <note>original: davar</note> (*that is, speech or speaking*), *the Chaldean has rendered it as* <term>the Word</term> <note>original: מימרא - Memra</note> (*which properly sounds like* THE WORD): *for that can never be proven from Holy Scripture. Second: he is completely mistaken <note>literal: "wanders by the whole sky"</note> who thinks that* <term>speech</term> <note>original: davar</note> (*which signifies speech or speaking in the Hebrew language) is of the same meaning as* <term>the Word</term> <note>original: Memra</note> *in the Chaldean language. For wherever the Chaldean Par-*

<meta>The catchword "daica" at the bottom indicates the next page begins with the completion of the word "Paraphrasis" (Paraphrase).</meta>

## Jerusalem Paraphrase

12. You have made <term>the Word of the LORD</term> <note>original: VERBVM יהוה (Memra)</note> reign over you this day, so that He might be a God to you; and <term>the Word of the LORD</term> has made Himself king over you, to appoint that people as His beloved, as a special treasure, just as He spoke to you, and to keep all His commandments.

---

*It is quite evident that the Aramaic text uses* <term>Memra</term> <note>original: ממרא (Word)</note> *not in an absolute sense regarding the speech or talk of God or any man, but to speak of a second mode of subsisting in the Deity; this is highly probable from the passages of Holy Scripture cited above, especially indeed:*

*Genesis 28:21: AND I SHALL RETURN IN PEACE TO THE HOUSE OF MY FATHER, AND <term>THE WORD OF THE LORD</term> SHALL BE MY GOD.*

*Deuteronomy 4:24: HIS WORD IS A CONSUMING FIRE; HE IS A JEALOUS GOD.*

*Deuteronomy 1:30: THAT SAME WORD OF HIS SHALL FIGHT FOR YOU.*

*Numbers 14:31: AND MY WORD SHALL LOATHE YOU.*

*Deuteronomy 31:6: HIS WORD WALKS BEFORE YOU, AND HE WILL NOT FORSAKE YOU, ETC.*

For it is manifest that all theologians, both the Hebrews and those of our own nation, have taken the liberty to designate things that are distinct in the sacred writings with distinct names. I believe it is undoubtedly clear to each and every person devoted to the sacred page that the most ancient and learned Hebrew theologians from the time of Abraham—as the books of the later Hebrews testify—used this term <term>Memra</term> <note>which we translate into Latin as "Verbum" and English as "Word"</note> for several thousand years in the synagogues as a common term. This is manifest both from the Aramaic paraphrases of <term>Onkelos</term> <note>The authorized Aramaic translation of the Torah</note>, <term>Jonathan son of Uzziel</term> <note>The author of the Aramaic paraphrase of the Prophets</note>, and the <term>Jerusalem Paraphrase</term> of the Old Testament, as well as from the writings and fragments of other ancient Rabbis. Let no one think, however, that the Church wished to establish other articles of faith; rather, I have no doubt that she was always uniquely bound to the Law and the Gospel. But as for the claim that the Aramaic translator turned <term>Davar</term> <note>original: דבר (speech/word)</note> into <term>Memra</term> <note>original: ממרא (Word)</note> wherever the Hebrew has it, that is utterly false; nor can it be proven by a single passage of Holy Scripture.
