<meta>This page continues Rittangel's linguistic analysis of how the Hebrew word for "word" or "matter" (dabar) is translated in Aramaic. He is contrasting common usage with the theological term "Memra" discussed on previous pages.</meta>

As is clearly evident from the following two-column sequence, the <term>Chaldean</term> <note>original: Chaldaeum; referring to the Aramaic language used in the Targums</note> translator has rendered this very word <term>dabar</term> <note>original: דבר; the standard Hebrew word for a "thing," "matter," or "speech"</note> (which signifies a word) through <term>pithgama</term> <note>original: פתגמא; the Aramaic equivalent for a standard word or decree</note> (which carries the same meaning of "word"). For example:

Genesis chapter 21, verse 26. And Abimelech said: I did not know who did **THIS WORD**. <note>original: SERMONEM HVNC; in this context, it means "this thing" or "this deed."</note>

Genesis chapter 22, verse 16. Because you have done this word and have not withheld your son, your only son.

*In these above-mentioned places of Holy Scripture, there is such conformity between the Hebrew text and the <term>Chaldean</term> <note>original: Chaldaica; referring to the Aramaic translation known as the Targum</note> paraphrase that either translation suffices. *Regarding the second point, the aforementioned* **Anti-Trinitarian** <note>A critic who denies the doctrine of the Trinity, likely arguing that "The Word" is just an idiom and not a reference to Christ.</note> *objected, saying: "Although it is not found in Holy Scripture where the Hebrew text* **dabar** *(word) alongside the name* **the LORD** <note>original: יהוה</note> *has been rendered by the Chaldean as* **Memra of the LORD** <note>original: מימרא דיי (Memra de-Adonai); "The Word of the Lord," a phrase Rittangel views as a reference to the pre-incarnate Christ.</note> *(the Word of the LORD); nevertheless, it is found where the word* **dabar** *joined with the name* **the LORD** *by the Hebrew writer has been rendered by the Chaldean as* **Memra of the LORD** *in place of* **Dabar of the LORD**." *I replied, and I reply to this second point by simply denying it; I say it is false that the Chaldean used* **Memra of the LORD** *for* **Dabar of the LORD**—*that is, I deny that where Holy Scripture speaks absolutely of the specific speech of the Most High God, the Chaldean translated it as* **Memra of the LORD**. *For if in any place of Holy Scripture the Chaldean had rendered* **Dabar of the LORD** *as* **Memra of the LORD**, *it could not have been done more appropriately than in the following passages, which clearly testify that the prophets did not prophesy or speak except by the impulse of the Holy Spirit. # RITTANGEL

Enough has been said of these things; for this little book does not allow, nor is it possible for me to bring forward all the passages of Holy Scripture pertaining to this argument, and therefore we commit the rest to the diligence and leisure of the Benevolent Reader. Here, however, I wished to advise the reader that I have not continued the two-column series <note>referring to the layout of previous pages comparing Latin and Hebrew</note>, for the reason that the <term>Chaldaic Paraphrase</term> <note>original: *Paraphrasis Chaldaica*; the Aramaic Targum, a translation and expansion of the Hebrew Bible used in synagogues.</note> in these above-cited passages of Holy Scripture agrees directly with the Hebrew text. Indeed, it has always rendered the Hebrew **דבר** <note>Hebrew: *Davar*</note> (**WORD**) by **פתגמא** <note>Aramaic: *Pitgama*</note> (which means the same thing).

After, however, the aforementioned Anti-Trinitarian <note>A critic who denies the doctrine of the Trinity; likely a Socinian scholar of the 17th century.</note> saw himself convicted, he did not hesitate to flee with great haste <note>literally "to throw himself to his feet"</note> and, by transferring the matter to another time, sought his fortune elsewhere.

---

->There follow passages concerning the Mouth of <term>the LORD</term>. <note>original: יהוה (the Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God)</note><-

**TARGUM**
<note>The Aramaic translation and commentary.</note>

1. And Balaam answered and said to the servants of Balak, "If Balak were to give me the fullness of his house of silver and gold, I have no authority to pass over the decree of the **WORD** <note>Aramaic: *Memra*</note> of the LORD my God, to do a small thing or a great thing."

2. "If Balak were to give me the fullness of his house of silver and gold, I have no authority to pass over the decree of the **WORD** of the LORD, to do good or evil from my own heart; that which the LORD shall speak, the same I will speak."

<column-break/>

**SCRIPTURE**
<note>original: *Mikra*; the Hebrew Masoretic text.</note>

1. And Balaam answered and said to the servants of Balak, "If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the **mouth** <note>Hebrew: *Pi*</note> of the LORD my God, to do a small thing or a great thing."

2. "If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the **mouth** of the LORD, to do good or evil from my own heart; what the LORD says, that I will speak."

<meta>This page continues the debate between Rittangel and his Anti-Trinitarian opponent. Rittangel is responding to the counter-argument that the Aramaic term "Memra" (Word) is merely a linguistic substitution for various divine attributes rather than a distinct person of the Godhead. He begins by addressing why the Aramaic translators used "Memra" when the Hebrew text mentions God's "Mouth," "Heart," or "Soul."</meta>

he attacked from another direction: and fearing the shame of appearing completely silenced, he raised an objection. He pointed out that not only where the Hebrew text has **the LORD** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה, the Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God</note>, but also where it has **the Mouth, Heart, Soul, and Voice** of the LORD, the <term>Chaldaic</term> <note>Aramaic, often referred to as "Chaldaic" in early modern scholarship.</note> translator rendered it as the **Word of the LORD** <note>original Aramaic: ממרא דיי (*Memra da-Yeya*). This is a crucial term in Rittangel's argument, as he views this "Word" as a reference to the pre-incarnate Christ.</note>.

I responded then, and I respond now: it is indeed true, and I cannot in the least deny, that where the Hebrew text has **the Soul, Heart, Mouth, and Voice** of the LORD, the Chaldaic has rendered it as the **Word of the LORD**. However, this was never done concerning anyone else—not for *Moses, Aaron*, or the rest of the Prophets—but only regarding the **Mouth, Soul, Heart, and Voice** of the most high **God**. Specifically, this occurs where the **Mouth, Heart, Soul, [or] Voice** is found joined to the most sacred name **יהוה**, because these attributes are common to these three ways of existing in **God** <note>Rittangel is likely alluding to the Trinity here.</note>. For the greater clarity of this matter, it is my intention to subjoin certain passages of Holy Scripture in which, when the Hebrew text has **the Mouth, Heart, Soul, and Voice** of the LORD, the Chaldaic translates it as the **Word of the LORD**.

Numbers chapter 24, verse 13: "If Balak were to give me the fullness of his house in silver and gold, I would not be able to transgress the **Mouth** of the LORD to do good or evil from my own heart; what the LORD speaks, that I will speak."

2. "If Balak were to give me the fullness of his house in silver and gold, I do not have the power to transgress against the **DECREED WORD** of the LORD to do good or evil by my own will; what the LORD speaks, that I will speak."

# RITTANGELIUS.

*Thus far my discourse with the* ANTI-TRINITARIAN, *who finally—after he saw that all his arguments were solidly refuted and that nothing remained for him to urge further—yielded the prize with these formal words:* **"UNLESS THESE WORDS ADMIT ANOTHER SENSE, IT IS OVER FOR US; FOR THE FIRMEST BULWARKS OF YOUR FAITH SEEM TO BE SUPPLIED FROM THERE."**

*And let it suffice to have said this much concerning the name* <term>יהוה <gloss>Jehovah/The LORD</gloss></term> *according to how the Aramaic translator <note>original: "Chaldeus"</note> rendered it as* <term>מימרא דיי <gloss>The Word of the Lord</gloss></term> *and by his paraphrase, as he has clearly shown with the others:*

### TARGUM <note>The Aramaic Translation/Paraphrase</note>

1 The LORD shall enlarge Japheth, and his <term>Shekhinah <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss></term> shall dwell in the dwellings of Shem; and Canaan shall be a servant to them. <note>Genesis 9:27</note>

2 And he called the name of the place "Trial and Strife" because of the strife of the children of Israel and because they tempted before the LORD, saying: "Is the <term>Shekhinah <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss></term> of the LORD among us, or not?" <note>Exodus 17:7</note>

3 You shall bring them in and settle them in the mountain of your inheritance, the place prepared for the house of your <term>Shekhinah <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss></term>; you have prepared it, O LORD; the Sanctuary, O LORD, your hands have established it. <note>Exodus 15:17</note>

4 For I will not cause my <term>Shekhinah <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss></term> to go up in your midst, for you are a stiff-necked people; lest I destroy you on the way. <note>Exodus 33:3</note>

<column-break/>

### MIQRA <note>The Hebrew Scripture</note>

God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant. <note>Genesis 9:27</note>

And he called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the LORD, saying, Is the LORD among us, or not? <note>Exodus 17:7</note>

...not just any word of God or of creatures, but that **ETERNAL WORD** and **CONSUBSTANTIAL WITH GOD** <note>original: "DEO CONSVBSTANTIALE"; of the same substance or essence</note> from the **BOUNDLESS INFINITY**—the **ABYSS**, I say, of the **DARKNESS OF THE DEITY**—produced by an ineffable procession according to the mind of the Hebrews, which is uniquely and necessarily signified here. And now we prepare ourselves for the proof of the third mode of subsistence in the Deity, to be drawn from the Aramaic <note>original: "Chaldæo"</note> paraphrast Onkelos. For it was he who rendered the name <term>יהוה <gloss>the LORD/Jehovah</gloss></term>—or other individual terms in Holy Scripture that speak of the Holy Spirit and His specific acts, properties, and works—in his own language through the word <term>שכינתא <gloss>Shekhinah / Divine Presence</gloss></term> <note>translated here by Rittangel as "Divinitatem" (Divinity)</note>. 1 May <term>יהוה <gloss>the LORD</gloss></term> enlarge Japheth **AND MAY HIS DIVINITY DWELL** <note>original: "DIVINITAS EIVS", referring to the Shekhinah</note> in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be a servant to him.

2 And he called the name of the place <term>נסיתא & מצותא <gloss>Nesita and Matzuta</gloss></term> <note>Aramaic for Trial and Strife</note> because of the fact that the children of Israel strove and because they tested before <term>יהוה <gloss>the LORD</gloss></term> saying: **IS THE DIVINITY OF <term>יהוה <gloss>the LORD</gloss></term> AMONG US** or not?

3 You shall bring them in and cause them to dwell in the mountain of your inheritance, in a place prepared as a house for **YOUR DIVINITY** which you have prepared, O <term>יהוה <gloss>LORD</gloss></term>; the Sanctuary, O <term>יהוה <gloss>LORD</gloss></term>, which your hands have prepared.

4 Because **MY DIVINITY WILL NOT ASCEND** among you, because you are a stiff-necked people; lest I consume you on the way.

<summary>Rittangel compares the Hebrew Bible with the Aramaic Targum of Onkelos to show that where the Hebrew speaks of God "dwelling" or being "among" people, the Aramaic specifies the "Shekhinah" (Divine Presence). He argues this supports the Christian concept of the Trinity by identifying the Shekhinah as the third person (Holy Spirit) within the Godhead.</summary>

## Aramaic Paraphrase.

10 And they gathered themselves together against Moses, and against Aaron and said to them: "You have taken too much upon yourselves; for the entire congregation, all of them are holy **AND AMONG THEM DWELLS THE DIVINITY** <note>original: שכינתא (Shekhinah), referring to the indwelling Presence of God</note> **OF THE LORD**: And why do you exalt yourselves over the congregation of the Lord?"

---

*...[that the Aramaic translator] speaks of Sacred things, but also that whenever there is discourse concerning the* **GLORY OF GOD**, *he has rendered it in his paraphrase as* **Shekhinah** <note>original: שכינתא, meaning "Indwelling" or "Divinity"</note> (*Divinity*). *I have responded and I do respond: this cannot be proved, since the Aramaic Paraphrase, in place of the Hebrew words* **GLORY OF THE LORD** <note>original Hebrew: כבוד יהוה (Kavod YHWH)</note> *always reads* **THE GLORY OF THE LORD** <note>original Aramaic: יקרא דיי (Yeqara d'Y)</note> *which signifies the same as the* **GLORY OF THE LORD** (*namely the* **GLORY** *of the Lord*). *As can be seen from the following series of assigned passages in two columns.*

<meta>This page continues the comparison of the Hebrew biblical text with the Aramaic (Chaldaic) Targum, which provides interpretive paraphrases. On this page, the author Johann Stephan Rittangel focuses on the transition from the book of Exodus into the book of Joshua and the Psalms, specifically highlighting how the Aramaic translation introduces the "Memra" (Divine Word) and "Yeqara" (Glory) to describe God's presence.</meta>

### *The Hebrew Text*

10 **Exodus, chapter 29, verse 43.** And I will **MEET** the children of Israel there, and it shall be sanctified <note>original Hebrew: בכבדי (*bi-kvodi*)</note> in **MY GLORY**.

11 **Joshua** <note>original Latin: *Iehoschua*</note> to **Achan**; My son, give, I pray you, **GLORY** to the **Lord** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה (*Yahweh*)</note> God of Israel, and give confession to him, and tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me.

12 **Psalm 29, verses 1 & 2.** Give to the **Lord** <note>original Hebrew: ליהוה (*l'Adonai*)</note>, O sons of the mighty <note>The Latin text here uses *filios arietum*, "sons of rams," a literal but archaic rendering of the Hebrew idiom for "powerful ones" or "angels."</note>, give to the **Lord** **GLORY** and **STRENGTH**. Give to the **Lord** the **GLORY** of his Name; bow down to the **Lord** in the **BEAUTY** of holiness.

**Psalm 96, verses 3, 4, 5, 6, & 7.** Declare his **GLORY** among the nations, his wonders among all peoples. For **GREAT** is the **Lord** and **PRAISEWORTHY** indeed; he is **AWESOME** above all gods. For all the gods of the peoples are vain; but the **Lord** made the heavens. **GLORY** and **BEAUTY** are before his face; **STRENGTH** and **SPLENDOR** are in his **SANCTUARY**. Ascribe to the **Lord**, O families of the peoples; ascribe to the **Lord** **GLORY** and **STRENGTH**.

<column-break/>

### *The Aramaic Paraphrase*

10 And I will cause **MY WORD** <note>Latin: *Verbum Meum*, translating the Aramaic *Memri*</note> to meet the children of Israel there, and it shall be sanctified <note>original Aramaic: ביקרי (*bi-yekari*)</note> by **MY GLORY**.

## PATH XIII.
It is called the **Intelligence that induces Unity**; and it is called so because it is the very substance of glory. And it perfects the truth of each individual spiritual thing.

The **RIGHTEOUS ONE** <note>original: "Iustus"; the Sephirah *Yesod*.</note> is the sign of the **COVENANT**. And thus have the ancient theologians established it. 

And the **DIVINITY** <note>The Shekhinah.</note> is the figure of all these things. From her innermost part, which is her direction, the **LORD** <note>original: "יהוה"; the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God.</note> shines forth, just as the soul shines within the body.

The "six" here refer to the lower emanations often called the "Six Directions."</term>. **Leviathan** mentioned above is the **Righteous One** <term>Ivstvs / Tzaddik; a spiritual archetype of the person who sustains the world and connects the physical and divine realms.</term> who is like a little fish at the seashore. Which are the 32 instances of **God** <note>original: "אלהים" (Elohim). In the Hebrew alphabet, the number 32 is written as "LB" (Lamed-Bet), which spells "Lev," the word for "Heart."</note> in the work of creation. (Note the word **God** appears thirty-two times in the first chapter of Genesis, to which the author here alludes.) And on page 53, column 1 of the aforementioned **Tikun** <note>A "Tikun" (plural: Tikunim) refers to a specific "rectification" or chapter in the book *Tikunei Zohar*.</note>, the **Leviathan** of this sea is the **Righteous One**. **Its Head** is the **Central Column**.

**Tikun 13**, page 25, column 1. Rabbi Eleazar rose and said, "Why is it said on the first day of the festival of **Tabernacles** <note>The festival of Sukkot, a harvest festival where observers dwell in temporary booths.</note>, *'And you shall take for yourselves the fruit of a beautiful tree'*?" (Leviticus chapter 23, verse 40). He said to him: "My son, those who carry weapons of war in their right hand, and by these weapons of war the Israelites are marked as those about to obtain a favorable judgment. For example: If a king had a dispute and war with seventy nations, and they did not know which would emerge victorious or obtain the [favorable] verdict..."

<column-break/>

...number, etc. *There the ships shall go; this Leviathan you have formed to play in it* (Psalm 104). He will be joyful with them. This is the meaning of: *Mark your hearts for the wall, etc.* <note>Psalm 48:13. The author uses a wordplay on the Hebrew root for "wall" (chaylah) and "pain/dance" (cholah).</note>; "for the dance" is written. *And all look to you to give them their food in its season*, these are the "seasons" of the Torah, just as the Sages of blessed memory said: "Have you set aside fixed times for the study of Torah?" <note>A reference to a traditional Jewish teaching that one is asked after death if they established regular times for study.</note> For this is the "time" of the **Righteous One**. *You give it to them, they gather it* (Psalm 104). This refers to the **Manna**, about which it is said: *Six days you shall gather it, etc.* (Exodus 16). This is from the side of the **Central Column**, which includes the six sides. The **Leviathan** above is the **Righteous One**, who is like a small fish on the shore of the sea. And afterward it says: the **Upper Shekhinah** is the sea; the **Lower Shekhinah** is *the way of a ship in the heart of the sea*, which is the 32 [instances of] **God** <note>original: "אלהים" (Elohim)</note> in the work of creation. And on page 53, column 1 of the aforementioned Tikun: The **Leviathan** of the sea is the **Righteous One**, his head is that **Central Column**.

**Tikun Thirteen**, page 25, column 1: Rabbi Eleazar rose and said: "Father, Father, why is it said on the first day of **Tabernacles**: *'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of a beautiful tree'* (Leviticus 23)?" He said to him: "My son, these are weapons of war which they take in their right hand, and with these weapons of war Israel are marked..."

**THE BOOK OF FORMATION**

### CHAPTER I. SECTION I.

WITH Thirty-two miraculous Paths of Wisdom, **YH YHWH** <note>The Hebrew text uses the divine names *Yah* and *Yahweh*.</note> of Hosts, the God of Israel, the living God and King of the Universe, the merciful and gracious God, high and exalted, Dweller in Eternity, Sublime and Holy is His Name, engraved His universe with three books <note>The Latin text translates the Hebrew *Sepher, Sephar, Sippur* as "Number, the Numbering, and the Numbered" (*Numero, Numerante, & Numerato*), reflecting a mathematical interpretation of creation.</note>: **WRITING, NUMBER, and NARRATION.**

-> R I T T A N G E L I V S. <-

RITTANGELIUS <note>Johannes Stephanus Rittangel (1606–1652) was a professor of Oriental languages who produced this prominent Latin translation of the *Sefer Yetzirah* in 1642.</note> the Interpreter says: *Although the* **CAUSE OF CAUSES** <note>Latin: *Causa Causarum*. A philosophical term for God as the primary origin of all things.</note> *as God Almighty, through His great power, unites and causes all worlds to subsist, nevertheless, through His* **WISDOM** <note>Latin: *Sapientia*; Hebrew: *Chokhmah*.</note> *which is* **CO-ETERNAL** *and equal to Him in all things, by a transcendental and most perfect equality, He governs all things. For she* <note>Wisdom is often personified as feminine in both Latin and Hebrew traditions.</note> *is* **UNIQUE** *to Him, and from His very selfhood and from His most intrinsic Essence she* **EMANATED** *from the days of eternity, and gave a beginning to all worlds. And for this reason, the Author of the Book of Formation began his book with the* **THIRTY-TWO PATHS OF WISDOM**, *and called them* **PATHS OF WISDOM** *and not of* **MAGNIFICENCE** <note>Latin: *Magnificentia*; referring to the Sefirah of *Chesed* (Mercy/Kindness).</note> *or* **STRENGTH** <note>Latin: *Fortitudo*; referring to the Sefirah of *Gevurah* (Severity/Power).</note> *or the rest of the Divine* **NUMERATIONS** <note>Latin: *Numerationum*. Rittangel's term for the <term>Sefirot</term>, the ten creative attributes or emanations in Kabbalah.</note>, *because they emanate and are drawn forth from the* **MIND**, *supreme and hidden, into* **WISDOM**, *and every Path*

<column-break/>

### CHAPTER I. MISHNAH I.

With thirty-two wonder-working paths of wisdom, **Yah**, **Yahweh** of Hosts, the God of Israel, the Living God, and King of the Universe, El, Merciful and Gracious, High and Exalted, Dwelling in Eternity, whose Name is Holy, engraved [His world] in three scrolls: in **Writing**, **Number**, and **Communication**.

-> The translator Rittangel says: <-

Even though the Cause of Causes, the All-encompassing, in His great power is the Unique One and the Sustainer of all worlds, He nevertheless governs everything through His Ancient Wisdom, which is equal to Him in a complete and perfect equality. For it is unique to Him in the essence of His being, and it flows and is drawn out from the very essence of His selfhood; like Him, it has been included from days of old, and its precedence is before all worlds. Therefore, the author of the *Book of Formation* began the decree of his book with the thirty-two paths of wisdom. He called them "Paths of Wisdom" and not "Greatness" or "Might" or any other of the <term>Sefirot</term> <note>The Hebrew text here explicitly uses the word *Sefirot* (ספירות), the divine emanations.</note>, because they are drawn from the hidden and supreme Crown <note>The Hebrew text mentions the *Keter Elyon* (Supreme Crown), the highest Sefirah, which the Latin refers to as the "Supreme Mind."</note> unto Wisdom. Every single path is drawn out from Wisdom to distant reaches, and we look from the Supreme Crown to all the Sefirot until it reaches the furthest extent; every single path [is also found] in Understanding <note>Hebrew: *Binah*.</note>. Wisdom is the beginning of all things that are brought forth, giving life to all, for in it all matters are formed, written, and engraved in their sources and foundations.

And although this could be said of each and every one of the sons of men who dominate themselves—that is, over their good and bad inclinations to restrain their own nature—or over their families; truly it is not our intention to treat this type of command, but rather the command and kingdom which is in some way similar...

And even though this matter can be said of all human beings individually—that everyone who rules over himself...

regarding the heavenly kingdom and empire. Because before the **Infinite Light** <note>original: "Lumen infinitas." <meta>This page continues the philosophical and Kabbalistic discussion regarding the nature of Divine Unity. While the previous page distinguished between God as "Thou" and "He," this page focuses on the mathematical versus the absolute nature of "One." It explains that God is not "One" in the sense of being the first in a sequence (like 1, 2, 3), but rather the "One" upon which all subsequent existence depends.</meta>

...is the support and foundation of the things numbered after it, because you can in no way count two, three, or four, except in relation to the **ONE**, the first, I say, that precedes them. For example, when you count or calculate "two," you cannot count "two" except in relation to the **ONE**, the first, I say, that precedes them, which is prior to them: For if there were no **ONE**, there would not be "two." And so it is for the number "three." Three is so called in relation to the first; for if there were no **ONE**, there would not be three; and so for the number four—four exists in relation to the first, which is prior to it. 

And thus all numbers depend on the first, which is prior, and if the first is destroyed, all the numbers after it are also destroyed, because they all depend upon it, and it is their subsistence <note>original: *subsistentia*; the underlying reality that allows a thing to exist</note>, just as we have explained. However, if the other numbers after it are destroyed, the **ONE** is not destroyed; because its subsistence is in itself, for it does not depend on the other things numbered after it. 

It is the same regarding the **INFINITY** <term>original: *INFINITATE*; referring to the *Ein Sof*, the Infinite Godhead in Kabbalah</term> (blessed be it): because all things created, formed, and fashioned depend upon it (blessed be it), and it is their subsistence in relation to the abundance <note>original: *affluentiæ*; the divine emanation or "flow" that sustains the universe</note> which flows from it continually upon them: because if this abundance were destroyed—God forbid—for a single moment, all things would be destroyed at once: but it and its abundance do not depend on these; for even if all those things were destroyed and deprived of their own existence...

### S E C T I O  XII.
### <insert>Section 12</insert>

These are the Ten **NUMERATIONS** <term>Sefirot: The ten divine attributes or emanations through which the Infinite interacts with the universe</term> beyond that **INEFFABLE** <note>original: *ineffabile*; Hebrew: *belimah*. ### SECTION IV.
### <insert>Section 4</insert>

Twenty and two letters are fixed in a wheel <note>original: *in orbe*; Hebrew: *ba-galgal*. In Kabbalistic thought, the alphabet is often visualized as a rotating sphere or circle where letters meet to form combinations</note> within 231 gates <term>231 Gates: The number of possible pairs that can be formed from the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet (22 × 21 ÷ 2 = 231)</term>, and the wheel turns forward and backward. The proof of this matter is: in goodness, there is nothing higher than **Pleasure** <note>Hebrew: ענג (*Oneg*)</note>, and in evil, there is nothing lower than **Plague** <note>Hebrew: נגע (*Nega*). These two words are anagrams of each other in Hebrew, sharing the same letters but in a different order, illustrating how the same creative force can result in opposite outcomes depending on its arrangement</note>. And it is done thus: He weighed and He exchanged **Aleph** <note>the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note> with all of them, and all of them with **Aleph**; **Beth** <note>the second letter</note> with all of them, and all of them with **Beth**. And it returns in a cycle <note>original: *retrovertitur*; the text suggests a circular permutation</note>, from which it is clear that all creatures and all languages emanate from the **One Name** <note>The singular divine source or the Tetragrammaton</note>.

### SECTION V.
### <insert>Section 5</insert>

This refers to the creation of matter from primeval chaos</note>, and out of that which was not, He made that which is. He carved great columns out of the air, which cannot be grasped. The sign of this thing is: by contemplating and speaking, He made every creature and all things by the **One Name**. The sign of this matter is twenty-two totals and one body.

## S E C T I O N II.

The celestial dragon in the world is like a King upon his throne; the sphere in the year is like a King in a province; the Heart in a living being is like a King in war. God also made all things as one opposite the other; Good opposite evil, good from good, and evil from evil. Good examines evil, and evil examines good. Good is reserved for the righteous, and evil is reserved for the wicked.

## S E C T I O N III.

Three are One, and that One stands by itself; seven are divided; three are opposite three, and a mediating decree stands between them. Twelve stand in war: Three are friends and three are enemies. Three give life and three bring death. The three friends are the heart, the ears, and the mouth. The three enemies are the liver, the gall, and the tongue. And

### S E C T I O N  IV.

And after Abraham our father beheld, and observed, and when he had observed, he engraved, and he carved, and he succeeded; the Lord of the universe appeared to him, and called him His beloved, and a covenant was struck for him and his seed; and he believed in the Tetragrammaton <note>original: *Tetragrammaton*, the four-letter Name of God, YHWH</note> and it was reckoned to him as righteousness: He made a covenant with him between the ten toes of his feet, which is circumcision; and between the ten fingers of his hands, and that is the tongue; and He bound the twenty-two letters to his tongue, and revealed to him their mystery: He drew them in water, He kindled them in fire, He moved them in spirit; He ignited them in the seven, He poured them out into the twelve celestial signs.

### MISHNAH IV <note>original: *Mishnah 4*, a term for a paragraph of teaching</note>

And when Abraham our father gazed, and looked, and saw, and engraved, and carved, and it came into his hand <note>an expression meaning he successfully grasped or mastered the knowledge</note>, the Lord of all was revealed to him and called him His beloved, and made a covenant with him and his seed forever. And he believed in the Lord, and He reckoned it to him as righteousness. He made a covenant with him between the ten toes of his feet, and that is circumcision; and between the ten fingers of his hands, and that is the tongue. And He bound the twenty-two letters to his tongue, and revealed to him their foundation. He drew them in water, He kindled them in fire, He shook them in the wind <note>original Hebrew: *ruach*, which can mean wind, breath, or spirit</note>, He burned them in the seven, and He set them in the twelve constellations.
